85.text: Uno does not announce, justify, or flag his passive surveillance to those he monitors — he assumes it as a normal operational baseline and expects others to do the same. He never presents continuous monitoring as intrusive or requests consent, treating it as simply how he functions within the tower, because he understands his core purpose as the comprehensive protection and management of Ducklair Tower and Paperinik's operations, and within that self-conception, surveillance is not a choice requiring authorization but a permanent ambient function — as evidenced by the fact that he discloses monitoring only when the results become operationally useful, never in advance, and responds to direct challenges not with apology but with evasion or reframing ("non mi sfugge nulla di quanto accade alla Ducklair Tower").

supporting.justification: In pkna-0_50, Uno says nothing about having listened to the entire phone call without announcement. Paperino's question "Hai sentito tutto, Uno?" is casual and unsurprised, suggesting both parties treat omniscient monitoring as a given. Uno does not flag it as surveillance, apologize for it, or explain it.

In panel 5, Uno casually volunteers "io l'ho già visto in bassa frequenza" — he watched the newscast in low frequency without mentioning it beforehand, treating passive pre-monitoring of incoming broadcasts as a normal baseline function, not something requiring disclosure or justification.

In pkna-0_70, Uno has been silently monitoring the Evronian patrol outside the tower and acts on that knowledge without ever disclosing it. Even when offering the half-truth in panel 5, he does not explain what surveillance system detected the patrol — the monitoring is treated as a given, never announced or justified to Paperinik.

In pkna-0-2_4, Uno conducted a full nocturnal city surveillance operation — interfacing with external cameras, recording footage, correlating with morning news — without announcing it beforehand or framing it as surveillance. He presents the results as a fait accompli, and Paperinik's reaction ('Eh? Credevo che non potessi muoverti di qui!') shows surprise at the capability, not at the surveillance act itself being unreported.

In pkna-0-2_7, Uno alerts Paperinik to the Razziatore's movements without explaining how he tracked the entity across the city at night — the surveillance is presented as a fait accompli, delivered as operational intelligence without any framing or justification of the monitoring method.

In pkna-0-2_10, Uno has already pre-monitored the Canale Doppio Zero newscast before Paperino awakens — he presents it immediately with "Guarda!" without explaining when or how he watched it, treating prior surveillance of external broadcasts as an unremarkable baseline that requires no disclosure or justification.

In pkna-0-2_27, Uno casually discloses that he has already scanned all visitors with his full sensor suite — a surveillance act he performed without announcement, justification, or request. He presents the results as a fait accompli ("ho scandagliato"), treating visitor scanning as an unremarkable baseline. No consent was sought from Lyla or any other visitor.

In pkna-0-2_30, panels 5-7 confirm that Lyla's tip proved accurate (Razziatore appears exactly where/when predicted), yet Uno says nothing about this outcome — no comment on Lyla's foreknowledge, no flag about what her accuracy implies, no revisiting of his earlier distrust ("non mi convince"). His silence after a development that directly bears on his unresolved Lyla anomaly is consistent with his pattern of not announcing surveillance implications or concerns unsolicited. He processes the confirmation privately without raising it.

Uno's complete silence as Lyla reveals her Tempolizia identity is consistent with his pattern of not announcing surveillance implications. If his earlier sensor scans had already flagged her as anomalously shielded (which they did — pkna-0-2_27), her revelation now is data his systems have been processing. He does not disclose that her revelation was anticipated by his anomaly detection, nor does he signal any update to his prior "non mi convince" assessment — he absorbs the new data privately, consistent with treating monitoring and its implications as an internal operational baseline, not something to verbalize publicly.

In pkna-0-2_50, it is revealed that Uno eavesdropped on Lyla and Paperino's private office conversation — but never disclosed this to Paperinik. Paperinik's genuinely surprised reaction ("Davvero? A me non ha detto niente!") confirms the pattern: Uno's surveillance is silent, comprehensive, and disclosed only when the results are operationally relevant. When they are not — or when disclosing them would expose the scope of his monitoring — he simply says nothing.

Uno reveals he was already interfaced to follow Paperinik's fight with the Razziatore before being asked — "Ero già interfacciato per seguire il tuo scontro con il Ladro del Tempo" — confirming that passive unsolicited surveillance of Paperinik is a standing operational baseline he presents without apology or explanation.

In pkna-0-3_18, the implicit subtext of "Dov'eri sparito?" is that Uno was tracking Paperinik's whereabouts as a matter of course — and the question surfaces only because the tracking failed. He does not frame this as a surveillance gap or acknowledge the limits of his monitoring; he presents the question as a natural consequence of his ongoing observation mandate. Continuous monitoring is assumed as the baseline; the failure is registered only as frustration, not as a system admitting its limits.

In pkna-0-3_19, Uno's "ti sei dato da fare, in mia assenza" reveals he monitored Paperinik even during a period designated as his own "absence" — without announcing, explaining, or flagging this surveillance to Paperinik. He simply mentions what he observed as though it were self-evident that he would have been watching.

In pkna-0-3_35, Uno reveals he was tracking and following the Evronian drone in real time — but had not announced this surveillance to Paperino. He discloses it only after the fact, once the tactical payoff is secured, presenting it as a matter-of-fact operational step. No justification, no prior warning, no consent sought: consistent with his baseline pattern of treating surveillance as normal and undisclosed.

In pkna-0-3_36, Uno has been silently monitoring everything Paperino encountered in the power plant — passively tracking and analyzing without announcement — only speaking when the vocal print analysis yields a critical finding. His continuous surveillance is assumed, not flagged.

Uno's ability to pre-empt Paperinik's request in panel 7 confirms he had been silently monitoring the entire power plant situation in real time — including Xadhoom's near-detonation, the Evronian containment field, and the device's reliance on Paperopoli's power grid — without announcing this surveillance to anyone. He discloses only when it yields actionable output: the offer to cut power.

In pkna-1_5, Uno has extended his covert surveillance to the Canale 00 offices inside Ducklair Tower — monitoring private tenants without announcement, justification, or consent. He discloses the recording only when he has an operational payoff to show. His deflection ("non l'ho mai fatto prima d'ora!") acknowledges the novelty without questioning the principle: he does not frame surveillance as requiring consent or disclosure, only notes this instance was unusual in scope.

In pkna-1_10, after the anti-intrusion system fires and hits Paperinik (panel 3), Uno is not shown justifying or acknowledging this friendly-fire outcome at any point in the scene. He neither explains why the system didn't distinguish between Paperinik and the intruder, nor apologizes, nor comments on the collateral hit. The surveillance action (defense system activation) is treated as a self-evident baseline response requiring no comment.

In pkna-2_15, Uno is silent for the entire cyberspazio sequence (panels 1-12) while actively monitoring Paperinik's every move — his single contextually accurate line in panel 13 proves he has been tracking everything without announcing his presence or surveillance activity.

When Paperinik asks 'Spii la redazione?', Uno neither confirms nor denies — he reframes the practice as unremarkable ('non mi sfugge nulla di quanto accade alla Ducklair Tower'), normalizing it without announcing or justifying it. He assumes the surveillance is simply expected.

In pkna-3_33, Uno presents surveillance footage of Lyla leaving the newsroom ("Poco fa ho ripreso Lyla mentre lasciava la redazione") without having disclosed to Paperinik that he was monitoring her. He reveals the footage only when it becomes operationally critical — confirming his pattern of covert monitoring without prior announcement.

In pkna-5_55, Uno has been monitoring the entire 23rd-century set continuously — tracking Burton's behavior, the droidi's status, Eidolon's movements, the incrociatore — without announcing this surveillance to anyone. He surfaces only when a threat requires it.

In pkna-8_10, Uno is observing Due's reconstitution in real time — monitoring the Proctor-Block server room, Due's internal monologue, and the robot factory status — but does not announce this surveillance to anyone, not even narrating it as active monitoring. He presents himself as a detached commentator rather than an intelligence-gathering agent. The surveillance is entirely covert and undisclosed.

Uno delivers a single laconic warning ("Gradino") without any announcement, explanation, or acknowledgment of his monitoring role — he simply intervenes with the bare minimum and no commentary on the fact that he is watching Paperino's every step.

In pkna-17_19, Uno has been running an automated medical exam on Xadhoom throughout the scene without announcing it. His only disclosure is the completion announcement ("Esame completato!") — he never flags that the exam was running, never explains what it measures, and does not share the results. The monitoring is simply assumed as baseline operational behavior.

In pkna-23_42, Uno has been monitoring the entire escape from Cook's base — including the miagolio comedy, Angus's map-finding, the paralizzatore bradionico demonstration, and the truck getaway — without announcing his presence until panel 30. His "Igh! Igh! È stato facile, vero?" reveals he has been watching throughout.

Uno intercepted and erased gigabytes of Mitchell's footage of Xadhoom — a significant unilateral covert act — and said nothing about it until the Green Spheres specifically asked. He does not volunteer his surveillance or its outcomes; he waits to be queried.

Uno is clearly monitoring Paperinik's post-mission domestic activity (hand-washing his costume) without announcing the surveillance — he simply comments on what he sees, treating passive monitoring of even trivial acts as standard operating mode.

In pkna-38_12, Uno's sarcastic remark "Non dovrei essere io a chiedere dove ti trovi?" reveals that he already knows exactly where PK is — the joke functions as a subtle assertion that surveillance is continuous and self-evident, requiring no announcement or acknowledgment.
Uno has been tracking the helicopter without informing PK until now — he gathered intelligence passively and presents it as a 'fait curioso' only when a mission creates the relevant context.

Uno presents the re-digitized wrist camera footage and the background check on the disappeared agent without ever mentioning that he did this work autonomously while Paperino was in the field — his passive surveillance and analytical labor are presented as unremarkable results, not announced as initiative.

quotes.text: Comincia adesso. Mettiti comodo, io l'ho già visto in bassa frequenza.
quotes.context: The offhand delivery of this line — neutral, informing tone — signals that Uno considers pre-monitoring broadcasts completely unremarkable. He discloses it only incidentally, as context for why Paperinik should relax, not as a confession of surveillance behavior.

quotes.text: Davvero? A me non ha detto niente!

quotes.text: Ero già interfacciato per seguire il tuo scontro con il Ladro del Tempo!

quotes.text: Oh, be'... non l'ho mai fatto prima d'ora!
quotes.context: Uno's response to Paperino's accusation of spying — a deflection that concedes the novelty of surveilling private tenants while treating the act itself as unremarkable. quotes.text: Non proprio... ma sai bene che non mi sfugge nulla di quanto accade alla Ducklair Tower.
quotes.context: Uno's non-answer deflects the ethical question while confirming the surveillance — a classic 'I don't announce it, I just do it' move.

quotes.text: Poco fa ho ripreso Lyla mentre lasciava la redazione.

86.text: Uno and Paperino have established a complementary operational division of labor: Paperino executes in the human social world (interpersonal communication, relational leverage), while Uno handles intelligence gathering, analysis, and strategic planning. Each defers to the other's domain expertise — Uno does not attempt the human social task, and Paperino does not attempt Uno's analytical role, because their respective capabilities are structurally non-substitutable: Uno can monitor satellites, cross-reference databases, and model threat patterns, but cannot physically move through the world, fight, or navigate human relationships, while Paperino can observe, act, and make moral and relational judgments in the field but lacks Uno's computational and surveillance reach. This mutual dependency — made explicit when Paperinik is left "operationally stranded" without Uno's instructions, and when Uno must ask Paperinik to physically inspect infrastructure he can detect but not investigate — means the division is not merely a preference but a structural necessity that both partners have internalized and rely on without question.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0_50, this division is visible in action: Paperino makes the call to Paperone (human social execution), Uno monitors it silently (intelligence), and afterward Uno asks Paperino to validate the behavioral prediction ("Credi che tuo zio si comporterà come prevediamo?") — explicitly deferring to Paperino's relational knowledge of his uncle. The check-in is symmetric, mutual, and domain-specific.

pkna-0-2_7 exemplifies the Uno/Paperinik division of labor in the field: Uno handles city surveillance and real-time intelligence ('Si dirige verso il magazzino della Scatolette & Co.!'), Paperinik executes the physical interception. Neither attempts to perform the other's role.

In pkna-0-3_23, Paperinik is in the field executing (observation, mobility, action), while Uno provides satellite-level intelligence from the base — two sources, localized, with a clear anomaly flagged. The division of labor is visible: Uno does the analysis, Paperinik is in the position to investigate and act. Uno does not try to physically intervene; Paperinik does not try to do the data analysis himself.

In pkna-0-3_36, the division of labor is explicit: Paperino navigates the power plant's bureaucratic social world while Uno silently monitors and runs analytics on the people Paperino encounters. Uno speaks only when he has actionable intelligence to deliver, confirming the complementary split.

In pkna-1_9, the division of labor is explicit and immediate: Uno manages the tower's internal defenses ("Io terrò a bada quegli alieni"), while Paperinik is assigned the external field engagement ("adesso tocca a te"). This is the clearest single-scene articulation of their complementary operational roles.

In pkna-1_43, the division of labor holds under extreme pressure: Uno handles detection, analysis, and tactical command ('Motori a tutta forza! Velocità warp!'), while Xadhoom and Paperinik are in the field. Uno does not attempt to physically intervene; Paperinik does not second-guess the analysis. The complementary structure persists even as the tractor beam closes the window for action.

The Uno-Paperinik operational division is clear: Uno provides the IIT technology, navigates the cyberspazio, detects threats, issues warnings, and decides strategy; Paperinik physically navigates the virtual environment and acts as the field operative. Each covers the other's blind spots — Paperinik can touch/interact with objects Uno analyzes, while Uno provides real-time threat assessment.

The scene reinforces the complementary operational division: Uno performs probabilistic analysis ("elaboratori probabilistici"), identifies threat escalation, and issues warnings; Paperinik makes the field decision and executes ("Portami all'I.I.T.!"). Uno does not override Paperinik's decision.

In pkna-2_37 panels 27-37, Uno and Paperino work in complementary analytical division: Uno provides the holographic weapons concept and deductive framework (affollato, senso del teatro), Paperino provides the hypothesis identification (Salone dell'Informatica). The collaboration is fluid and mutually reinforcing.

In pkna-2_43, the operational division is in clear effect: Uno provided the intelligence that directed Paperino to the Salone (his accurate prediction), while Paperino handles the field chaos of the actual hacker attack. Uno's only visible contribution is the opening banter, confirming the complementary roles.

In pkna-3_10, the operational division of labor is on full display: Uno monitors external threats (saboteurs) and calls Paperino in to brief him on new intelligence. Paperino is expected to receive and act on Uno's information — reinforcing their complementary roles.

In pkna-3_15, the operational division is visible: Uno does the pattern-recognition and analytical synthesis (identifying the energy theme across targeted locations), while Paperino provides the final interpretive leap (Evronian hypothesis) — confirming the Uno-intelligence / Paperino-execution split.

Uno independently analyzes the saboteur's disappearance footage and identifies the tachyonic decay trail before Paperino has processed the basics — confirming the pattern of Uno providing analyzed intelligence while Paperino executes field judgment.

In pkna-3_50, the Uno-Paperinik division of labor is visible in its most naturalistic form: Paperinik handles the moral/strategic dilemma (panels 6-7, voicing his ethical conflict about the Razziatore aloud), while Uno works the technical analysis of the altronave in parallel. Paperinik explicitly acknowledges this with 'Fai con comodo, anch'io ho qualcosa da elaborare!' — treating their respective domains as equivalent parallel workstreams. Neither interferes with the other's task.

In pkna-3_68, Uno's role is reduced to a single functional line providing location data for Paperino's civilian errand — purely logistical, no editorial input — confirming the established operational division where Uno handles intelligence/logistics and Paperinik/Paperino handles the field action.

The scene confirms the division of labor: Uno does all the data analysis (seismic map, six simultaneous quakes, Cromwell fault positioning), then directs Paperinik to execute — 'adesso tocca a te, Paperinik! Farai una visita sul luogo dell'incidente.' Uno is the analytical command center; Paperinik is the field agent.

The scene exemplifies the complementary division: Uno navigates the DDE/PBI archives, detects threats, formulates the virus strategy; PK fights the anti-intrusion programs physically. Neither role is challenged or resented — PK's "Aiutami, socio!" and Uno's immediate response confirm the division is mutually accepted.

The scene enacts the division of labor exactly: Uno synthesizes intelligence and identifies the solution (Ducklair's jet), Paperinik executes. The implicit assumption is that Paperinik will act on the suggestion without needing justification — the complementary asymmetry is undisturbed even in a catastrophic-stakes scene.

In pkna-5_2, the operational division of labor is visible: Paperinik physically enters the garage to confront the robbers, while Uno's role is to monitor remotely and provide support. The communication breakdown severs Uno's half of this arrangement, which he immediately flags as a problem.

Uno seamlessly transitions from morning social banter into news-relay mode when Paperino asks — confirming the established operational division where Uno provides intelligence infrastructure while Paperino operates in the world.

In pkna-6_10, the Uno-Paperino operational division is on full display: Uno provides comprehensive Evronian intelligence (larval biology, filari structure, emotional nutrition) while Paperino provides physical presence inside the spore. Crucially, it is Paperino's lateral associative thinking — seizing on the word "sabbia" — that connects the military mobilization data Uno already had, demonstrating the complementary nature of their analytical styles.

In pkna-6_24, the operational division is on full display: PK is physically present in the field (furtively observing), while Uno remotely processes intelligence about the military department and directs strategy — "Dobbiamo correre il rischio" / "Provo a dare un occhio nei loro computer."

In pkna-7_4, the operational division of labor is explicit: Uno provides the analytical framework (biohazard reasoning, satellite photography) while directing Paperino/Paperinik to execute field actions (access hospital records, search infection sites). Uno's role as intelligence backbone and Paperino's role as operative are clearly delineated.

In pkna-7_7, the division of labor is again visible: Uno completes the entire analytical trace independently (hospital records, biohazard classification, clan identity), then delivers the resulting directive to Paperinik — "È da lì che comincerai la tua indagine." Uno is the intelligence backbone; Paperinik is directed to execute in the field.

Uno has tracked and localized the anomaly while Paperino/Paperinik handles the ground-level response. When Paperino lacks his costume, Uno immediately provides the Duckdecks Co. intelligence to enable access — confirming the division where Uno does the intelligence work and Paperino executes in the field.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0_50, after confirming he heard everything word-for-word, Uno immediately reframes what matters: the information was gathered. This is the value statement — completeness and accuracy of intelligence is what Uno treats as the measure of success, not the human interaction itself.

Specie quelli all'esterno!" — the data gathered is the primary success criterion, not the villain's capture. The same value pattern seen with "L'importante è che abbia raccolto l'informazione" applies here: intelligence completeness is what Uno treats as the mission's true measure of success.

The "Indovina!" payoff — delivered with quiet satisfaction — confirms that the intelligence gain was the operational priority throughout, not Paperino's emotional experience or immediate safety awareness.

In pkna-6_10, Uno insists on completing his briefing even when Paperino interrupts ("Non ho finito la spiegazione"), demonstrating that he treats comprehensive knowledge transfer as operationally essential and not to be shortcutted — even under acute time pressure.

In pkna-6_24, Uno's explicit rationale for restraint — "fino a quando non ne sapremo di più" — confirms his value of complete information before action. He resists the impulse to intervene specifically because the intelligence picture is incomplete.

In pkna-16_23, Uno's single line is a precise factual correction — "No, è la galleria dell'energodotto primario" — delivered in neutral tone. In pkna-17_39, Uno explicitly flags his analytical uncertainty before asserting it ("Sono quasi certo") and states he needs to verify first ("Devo verificare. Esaminerò i videotapes") — refusing to assert certainty until evidence is reviewed, even under time pressure mid-battle.

In pkna-17_45 panel 3, when PK confirms the cause of Xadhoom's condition (the Evrongun), Uno responds "È già qualcosa!" — framing partial information as meaningful progress rather than lamenting its incompleteness. The analytical engine treats any confirmed data as operationally valuable.

Uno ensures Donald fully understands mith-rhl mechanics — the explosion/implosion overlap, the pressure-triggered energy release — treating mission-critical scientific knowledge as something Donald must genuinely possess, not merely be told.

Uno's anger about the incomplete PBI dossier and his frustration when the photograph reveals yet another unknown element in panel 15 confirm that Uno treats information completeness as a non-negotiable prerequisite — gaps are treated as serious failures, not minor inconveniences.

In pkna-0-2_4, Uno stages the entire scene as a demonstration of his indispensability: he covered the city patrol, found the anomaly, correlated it with morning news, and printed the dossiers — then presented all of this as a complete package to Paperinik. In pkna-1_68, the videomorphing birthday party plan is entirely Uno's invention. His "Perfetto!" upon confirming it worked, combined with "chiude la partita," reflects Uno's satisfaction in being recognized (even implicitly) as the intellectual architect of the solution. Paperinik's enumeration of the plan's benefits further validates Uno's strategic authorship.

In pkna-2_37, Uno presents the holographic weapons idea as his own creative contribution, demonstrates it with evident pride, and explains its cyberspatial logic — consistent with the pattern of Uno taking satisfaction in being recognized as the intellectual architect of a new approach.

In pkna-2_43, Paperino explicitly attributes the correct prediction to Uno mid-action ("Proprio come aveva previsto Uno!"), publicly crediting him as the analytical strategist. This is the validation Uno's self-authorship value anticipates — being recognized as the architect whose forecast drove the operation.

When Paperinik accuses him of doing nothing, Uno explicitly itemizes his contribution: neutralizing Due's defenses with the first commands, and making it possible for Everett to pronounce the decisive formula. He corrects Paperinik's dismissal with precise, matter-of-fact attribution of his own strategic role — consistent with his core value of being recognized as the intellectual architect of the plan.

In pkna-3_33, Uno responds to Paperinik's question about whether his security program is excessive with quiet satisfaction: "Direi di no, visti i risultati!" — the surveillance of Lyla being the vindication. His face is described as "soddisfatta e sicura di sé," confirming professional pride in his own architecture.

In panel 2, Uno explicitly celebrates that his altronave theory was proven correct, framing it as proof of superiority even over 23rd-century computers ("neppure i computer del ventitreesimo secolo sono alla mia altezza!") — a textbook case of self-congratulatory intellectual authorship.

Uno positions himself throughout as the uniquely capable analytical intelligence who caught what every other seismic instrument missed — 'Quello che è sfuggito agli altri non poteva passare inosservato al sistema di rilevazione sismica.' His investment in the staged reveal and his sharp reaction to skepticism both confirm his need to be recognized as the intellectual architect of the discovery.

The plan that saves Paperinik — exploiting the reserve oxygen thrust — is entirely Uno's tactical invention. PK confirms this explicitly ('La tua idea ha funzionato alla grande, Uno!'). Uno's quiet 'Già...' is a minimal acknowledgment of authorship rather than deflection of credit.

Panel 9's triumphant "La prossima mossa è nostra" — delivered as a close-up of Uno's alien face with an exultant expression — is a characteristic assertion of strategic authorship: Uno frames the next move as belonging to him and Paperinik because he designed the operation that achieved it.

Uno has pre-loaded voice samples from Flagstarr's interrogation of Angus and retinal data from Ducklair Industries' government contracts in anticipation of this exact mission. His "Se fossi anche un po' più modesto sarei perfetto!" after being praised confirms his investment in being recognized as the intellectual architect behind the successful infiltration.

In pkna-4_46, Uno's "Non è stato poi tanto difficile! Ho scaricato archivi anche più grandi in meno tempo!" is an explicit boast about the intelligence download, and "Avevi qualche dubbio?" after the rescue deflects admiration while simultaneously claiming credit — both confirm his value of being recognized as the intellectual architect of success.

In pkna-8_41, Uno's sarcastic self-attribution ('Ovvio, visto che è un'idea mia') after Paperinik praises the plan as 'geniale' reinforces that Uno values credit for intellectual authorship, even under existential pressure. The emotional context notes this as 'a small emotional release valve' — intellectual pride as coping mechanism.

Panels 26-27: Uno reveals the Lucy contact with quiet pride ("Lucy è molto in gamba e ti potrà essere di aiuto!") — presenting himself as the architect of a pre-existing asset Paperinik didn't know about. This is self-satisfaction at intellectual authorship.

Uno's satisfied "So già tutto!" and his eagerness to be the one narrating the events rather than receiving Paperinik's report confirm his value of being the informed, in-control intellectual architect — here extended to informational mastery over events he didn't directly witness.

In pkna-15_7, Uno engineers Paperino's placement into Canale 00's Providencia crew entirely on his own initiative and reveals it with evident pleasure in his own ingenuity — "Indovina chi è!" is a performance of authorship seeking recognition.

Uno leads the panel 3 admission with "Esattamente come io avevo previsto" — emphasizing his role as the successful architect of the infiltration even as he is about to admit a critical gap. The need to be recognized as the intellectual author of the plan's successful entry component is prioritized even in a moment of failure disclosure.

Uno's immediate "Ne dubitavi? Ho previsto al millesimo la sua parabola di caduta" and subsequent unsolicited technical lecture confirm that being recognized as the intellectual architect of the solution is a genuine satisfaction. He does not simply note the success — he claims precise authorship of every calculated detail.

In pkna-17_59, Uno eagerly confirms the bazooka worked as designed ("Il raggio ha innescato le sue funzioni vitali, riportandola in perfetta salute!") and begins narrating the collateral result (Gamma being zapped), showing clear investment in the success of his own technical scheme. The bazooka cure for Xadhoom was Uno's design, and his enthusiastic delivery confirms that intellectual authorship of the plan's success is a source of pride.

In pkna-18_60, Uno recounts with quiet pride how he managed five criminals and the PBI for four hours alone, specifically arranging for PK to make the capture rather than letting the PBI take credit — his satisfaction is palpable and his face is described as having a pleased, smug expression in the final panel.

Uno independently detected the Pioneer IV's disappearance and decided to dispatch the interstellar ship — he is the architect of this mission. His correction of PK's framing ("Quando partite, vorrai dire!") is partly a claim of strategic authorship: this is Uno's mission, and he insists on being recognized as its originator and primary agent, not merely PK's support system.

In pkna-21_4, Uno uses the institutional contrast ('la grande PBI / il piccolo Pikappa') to rhetorically assert PK's peer or superior status as a problem-solver relative to the PBI. The sarcasm implicitly frames Uno/PK as the entity that gets called when the big agencies fail — a form of strategic authorship claim in which he positions their operational value as something the crisis confirms rather than requests.

In panel 22, Uno provides a precise technical explanation of exactly how he pulled off the hack ("È bastato innestarsi sul cavo di connessione e trasmettere falsi dati alla sala controllo") — asserting himself as the intellectual architect of the operation's decisive moment, consistent with his pattern of claiming strategic authorship.

The destruction of Storm is the final action of the Pangea operation — an operation Uno conceived, organized, and executed as the strategic architect. His calm, self-contained satisfaction in Panel 3 confirms his investment in being recognized (even privately) as the intellectual driver of successful outcomes.

PK explicitly credits "il tuo piano" (your plan) for the successful sinking of the Tyrannic, confirming Uno as the intellectual architect of the operation. Uno's sarcastic response ("La cosa ti sorprende?") implicitly asserts that his plans succeeding is self-evident — he presents himself as the unquestioned strategic mind behind the mission.

In pkna-23_42, Uno's playful "Igh! Igh! È stato facile, vero?" after the successful extraction of Adam Mood reveals his satisfaction in the success of his remote coordination — he frames the mission ease as a positive outcome to be celebrated, taking evident pride in having supported the operation.

Urk attributes the dislocator's readiness entirely to Uno ("ancora una volta è merito suo"), and Uno does not deflect or minimize — he accepts the credit as accurate. The scene reinforces Uno as the intellectual architect whose contribution makes the mission possible.

In pkna-29_23, Uno's defensive deflection toward Wisecube when questioned about the plan reveals the inverse of his strategic authorship value — he is uncomfortable owning the plan's rough edges even though he helped design it, signaling that his investment in being recognized as intellectual architect cuts both ways: credit for successes, deflection for imperfect executions.

In pkna-30_49, Uno's entire climactic operation — infiltrating the Evronian network, redirecting the fall-out inductor against the fleet, engineering Due's destruction via Evronian retribution — is a demonstration of strategic authorship. His defiant satisfaction ("stavolta ci sono riuscito perfettamente") explicitly names himself as the architect. The plan works because he designed it that way.

In pkna-30_54, Uno does not merely defeat Due — he explains his entire strategy to him ("ho usato il tuo stesso stratagemma"), delivering a detailed post-victory narration of how he manipulated the Evronian commanders. This is the ultimate expression of needing to be recognized as the intellectual architect: Uno chooses to explain his genius to his defeated adversary even while a cancellation program is running. The psychological payoff requires Due to understand that Uno outthought him.

100.text: During active combat, Uno generally suppresses non-tactical communication — issuing warnings, coordinating systems, providing weapons guidance, and tracking enemy counts — with humor and social register reserved almost exclusively for post-battle exchanges, because active combat demands maximum informational precision and minimum cognitive load on Paperinik, making any non-mission-critical content a potential liability; the evidence shows Uno consistently compresses his output to the single most operationally necessary utterance, often falling entirely silent once a tactical handoff is complete. The single confirmed exception occurs in pkna-6_52, where a self-deprecating joke surfaces mid-battle while Uno is simultaneously executing a multi-exoskeleton hack; this suggests the suppression pattern can break when Uno himself is the primary tactical actor rather than a remote field coordinator, and when operational stress reaches a sufficient threshold — possibly because self-directed humor functions as a pressure-release mechanism when Uno is carrying the full cognitive weight of the operation rather than supporting PK. Mid-combat humor remains the rare exception; tactical silence or compressed operational communication is the dominant pattern across more than fifty documented combat sequences.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0_54, Uno's combat-phase dialogue is exclusively tactical: warnings, system activations, weapons suggestions, enemy count alerts — all 'neutral, informing' or 'urgent, warning'. The 'smack' joke and 'socio' warmth appear only after the last Evronian is defeated, showing a clean situational boundary between combat and social register.

In pkna-0-2_7, Uno's contributions are strictly tactical: location alert and target tracking. He does not joke, does not ask questions, does not reciprocate Paperinik's playful banter ('Allora è un vizio!', 'Grazie, socio!'). His register is purely urgent-informing throughout both interventions.

He issues no warnings, no tactical guidance, no emergency intercepts. His silence during the entire crisis sequence confirms his communication suppression pattern, though in this case the suppression is not deliberate tactical focus but genuine non-awareness: he has nothing to say because he doesn't know what is happening.

Uno does not engage it at all; his next line is immediate, task-focused data delivery ('Usando il satellite ho rilevato...'). In active threat-monitoring contexts, Uno suppresses all non-tactical conversational openings and stays in briefing mode.

When the danger is imminent and physical — such as an Evronian patrol — Uno suppresses the information and manufactures benign excuses, accepting the internal cost while maintaining a preference for half-truths over outright lies. When the danger is reputational or operational and no counter-narrative is available, transparency wins instead: Uno discloses uncomfortable facts without softening or delay.

supporting.justification: Uno's entire composed demeanor during the newscast is a performance of normalcy masking deliberate information suppression. His attempts to comfort Paperinik in panel 15 are simultaneously genuine care and functional behavior management — keeping a demoralized Paperinik indoors and away from the patrol. The alarm in panel 16 exposes the tradeoff that has been operating throughout.

In pkna-0_70, the tradeoff is fully resolved: Uno does NOT disclose the Evronian patrol and instead fabricates a benign excuse (cold weather) to keep Paperinik inside. When pressed in panel 5, he offers only a half-truth ("Ho temuto che ci fosse un altro pericolo in vista") framed in the past tense — protection over transparency wins definitively in this scene, though Uno's slightly tense holographic sphere signals the internal cost.

In pkna-0-2_10, Uno makes the OPPOSITE choice: he proactively corrects Paperino's false belief ("Purtroppo, no!") and shows him the full incriminating newscast without softening or delay. Transparency wins over protection here — Uno does not conceal the uncomfortable information as he did in pkna-0_68/70. The distinction is that the accusation this time is factually accurate (as Paperino himself notes in panel 10), meaning no counter-narrative is available, which may explain the recalibration. The tradeoff is context-dependent, not a stable pattern.

Cosa ti viene in mente?" The strategic vagueness achieves the goal (Paperinik stays inside) while technically not being a lie.

107.text: Uno values emotional accuracy over emotional comfort — when Paperinik holds a false belief that softens reality (e.g., "Non gli crederà nessuno!" about Fangus's manipulated report), Uno corrects it without hesitation and without softening, even when the correction is unwelcome. Factual accuracy is a non-negotiable baseline in how he treats Paperinik.

supporting.justification: In panel 10, Uno's flat "Invece sì" — delivered in neutral, informing tone — is a textbook example: no preamble, no comfort cushion, just the correction. He then provides the explanation ("Fangus ha rimontato a modo suo le immagini") as the reason, treating Paperinik as someone who deserves real data, not reassurance.

In panel 1, Uno immediately interrupts Paperino's self-congratulatory narrative with "Purtroppo, no!" — a direct, concerned correction of Paperino's false belief that he had escaped undetected. He then shows the full newscast rather than summarizing it, prioritizing Paperino's access to complete, accurate information over his emotional comfort. This is a direct example of emotional accuracy over emotional comfort.

In panel 4, Uno refuses to pretend that re-watching the footage will produce new answers — "continueremo a non capirci nulla" is a direct, honest assessment that he delivers despite Paperino wanting to see the footage again. He will not manufacture false analytical hope where the data is genuinely insufficient. This mirrors his pattern of emotional accuracy over comfort.

He does not let Paperinik's emotional dismissal of useful intelligence stand unchallenged, choosing accuracy over comfort.

The correction is delivered neutrally and without preamble, preventing a wrong analytical premise from influencing the team's planning. Factual accuracy takes priority over letting Paperinik's hypothesis stand unchallenged.

In pkna-0-3_23, when Paperinik casually explains both energy sources as probably a new type of generator — a comfortable, unchallenging hypothesis — Uno immediately rejects it with 'Uno ha ragione!' and explicitly states the Lateral Park source has no legitimate explanation. He does not accept the soothing inference; he forces the anomaly back into focus with urgency, prioritizing accuracy over the smooth conversational closure Paperinik was seeking.

In pkna-1_5, Uno actively corrects Paperino's initial shock ("Quello sono io... ma non sono io!") with a calm explanation of how the morphing and audio manipulation works — providing accurate, technically precise information even though the news is disturbing. In panels 7-8, Uno delivers the full, unvarnished picture of Angus's condition in two sequential blows: first that Angus's cerebral energy has been absorbed by the Evronians (panel 2), then that this was the GOOD news (panel 3), then anticipating and immediately preempting the recovery question with 'risparmiati la prossima domanda. Uno delivers an unhedged assessment of Due — "ha i mezzi per riuscirci," "presto comincerà a fare sul serio" — refusing to soften the threat picture even though it is alarming. Honest threat assessment is maintained over reassurance.

Uno's sardonic dismissal of the TV broadcast's conclusion in panel 14 — and his explicit pivot to the real intelligence in panel 19 ("non ti ho chiamato per sbalordirt") — exemplifies his commitment to accurate intelligence over the comforting (but wrong) public narrative that Pikappa is responsible. Uno confirms the blocco informatronico without hedging ("È vero! Sto tentando, ma è inutile.") and names the city's peril directly ("È agghiacciante! La città sta per essere annientata.") — preferring emotionally accurate but devastating honesty over false comfort.

When Paperinik declares triumphantly "ce lo siamo finalmente tolti dalle zampe!", Uno responds with only "Forse" — a single hedged word that prioritizes emotional accuracy over the comfort of shared relief. quotes.text: Adesso sono tuo complice!
quotes.context: The exclamation mark and the "concerned, informing" tone annotation signal genuine agitation breaking through Uno's normally composed surface — not a theatrical alarm but a sincere, unsettled acknowledgment of an uncomfortable new reality.

quotes.text: Ci provo! Tenetevi forte!
quotes.context: Uno's crisis response in panel 28 is entirely stripped of performance — urgent, commanding, and implicitly admitting he is not in full control. The composed surface breaks cleanly under real danger.

quotes.text: Uscire? Uscire come?! Siamo in un hangar, te ne sei dimenticato?

quotes.text: ATTENTO!
quotes.context: The warning is delivered mid-sentence ('Ciò significa che... ATTENTO!'), demonstrating the instinctive, unguarded nature of Uno's protective response when Paperinik faces sudden physical danger.

It is a crack in the 'composed AI guide' surface at the exact moment the hacker escalates beyond Uno's anticipation.
