quotes.text: Temo che le entità stiano cominciando a passare!
quotes.context: Uno's "Temo" (I fear) openly names anxiety — unusual for his composed surface. The dimensional breach is genuinely alarming enough to produce explicit fear language.

quotes.text: Dobbiamo trovarlo, prima che lo trovi questo Fround o uno dei suoi simpatici dipendenti numerati.
quotes.context: The only moment in the scene where Uno's composure reflects genuine concern rather than neutral analysis — urgency breaking through his analytical surface.

quotes.text: AAAAAAA
quotes.context: Uno's distorted scream in panel 7 is described as his face deformed, mouth wide, eyes wide — as close to genuine terror as he ever shows. Triggered by the Ironheart larvae physically breaching Ducklair Tower's structure.

quotes.text: Raznor!
quotes.context: The single urgent repetition of the name — contrasting with Uno's neutral tone in the preceding panels — is the scene's sole indicator of Uno's registered alarm. It is brief, controlled, and tactically motivated rather than emotional.

quotes.text: Questa voce!
quotes.context: The second exclamation — "This voice!" — reveals how immediately Uno's surface breaks when Due is confirmed. Voice recognition alone, before any visual or tactical confirmation, is sufficient to crack his composure entirely.

111.text: Uno's information management toward Paperinik is state-dependent and threat-type calibrated rather than blanket paternalism, but operates across more than two categories. He withholds when imminent physical danger meets an emotionally compromised or exhausted Paperinik (pkna-0_68/70), discloses fully when information is painful but purely factual and no reckless action would follow (pkna-0-2_10), and applies a third mode when strategic intelligence value outweighs personal threat awareness (pkna-0-3_35) or when social complexity around allies introduces hedging even for a field-ready Paperinik (pkna-3_26). The core driver is a real-time calculation — does acting on this information right now, given Paperinik's current state, create a net danger? — but "danger" is assessed broadly enough to include mission compromise and alliance instability, not only physical risk, because Uno consistently distinguishes between situations where disclosure would trigger reckless action or undermine operational outcomes and situations where it would not, adjusting his transparency accordingly rather than applying any fixed rule of concealment or openness.

supporting.justification: The scene's structure confirms this: Uno tries to lift Paperinik's spirits with humor (panel 15) before any confrontation occurs, and his alarm at the roof request (panel 16) signals the calculation — if Paperinik had been calm and cheerful, Uno might have disclosed the patrol. The behavior is protective paternalism, not control for its own sake.

pkna-0_70 confirms the behavioral driver in full action: Uno observes the Evronian patrol silently (panel 1), then intercepts an exhausted, recently demoralized Paperinik with a warm-concerned fabrication about cold weather (panel 2), then redirects him toward rest (panel 3). The management is calibrated to Paperinik's state — exhausted and dispirited — not to a blanket policy of concealment.

In pkna-0-2_30, Uno uses none of his information-gating mechanisms — he does not conceal the Razziatore's escape, he does not soften the partial failure. Instead, he immediately flags what went right. This is consistent with the claim's logic: Paperinik is combat-ready and not emotionally compromised, so Uno informs fully and transparently. The state-dependent calibration pattern holds: field-ready Paperinik = full disclosure mode.

In pkna-0-2_50, Uno eavesdropped on the Lyla-Paperino office conversation but did not disclose it to Paperinik. The behavioral driver here is security/threat-assessment: Lyla was an unverified, sensor-opaque entity, and listening to their conversation was a threat-evaluation action. The fact that Uno did not subsequently share what he learned — even though it directly concerned Paperinik's new ally — complicates the claim: this is not "painful factual information" (class: disclose) nor "imminent physical danger" (class: withhold to protect), but a third category: covert intelligence about an ally's trustworthiness that Uno filters through his own operational judgment before deciding what to surface.

In pkna-0-3_19, Uno's warning about Xadhoom ("potrebbe rivelarsi un'altra minaccia per Paperopoli") is a calculated redirect of Paperino's optimistic trust ("sono certo che se riuscissi a parlarle"). Uno does not dismiss the alliance possibility but gently tempers Paperino's enthusiasm with a cautionary counterweight — information management calibrated to prevent reckless confrontation driven by premature trust.

pkna-0-3_35 introduces a third category for Uno's information management: he withholds news of a direct threat to Paperino's secret identity (Evronian drone scan) not because acting on it would create imminent physical danger, nor because it's straightforward factual information — but because a tactical intelligence opportunity (locating the Evronian base) outweighs Paperino's right to immediate personal threat awareness. This is a more aggressive information-control pattern than previous cases: Uno is withholding threat-to-identity information to exploit a strategic opening, a clearer prioritization of intelligence value over Paperino's personal safety awareness.

In pkna-1_9, Uno does not burden Paperinik with cautionary framing about facing five Evronians alone — he simply delegates with full confidence. This confirms the information-management pattern: when the threat is already understood and deployment is necessary, Uno omits cautionary notes and trusts Paperinik's field judgment.

In pkna-3_26, Uno's information management toward Paperinik again demonstrates state-dependent calibration: Paperinik is field-ready, energized, and not emotionally compromised — conditions that typically trigger full disclosure. Yet Uno withholds his specific suspicions about Lyla, issuing only a vague warning. This reveals a fourth information-management category beyond the three established cases: when the target of suspicion is also an ally/acquaintance of Paperinik's, Uno hedges even for an operationally ready partner — social complexity overrides the usual "field-ready = full disclosure" rule.

In pkna-3_45, the 'Sole Freddo' revelation presents a new information-management category: Uno confirms catastrophic intelligence reactively (prompted by the Razziatore) rather than proactively, yet does not explain or address the gap. Whether he withheld it or learned it in real time is ambiguous — but in either case, Uno fulfills his duty to inform without explaining the circumstances of his prior silence, suggesting a fifth information-management mode: confirm when challenged, but do not volunteer the meta-information about your prior knowledge state.

Uno withholds information about the device specifically because full disclosure might cause Paperinik to hesitate at a critical moment — a threat-type-driven information management decision, not blanket paternalism. He provides enough for compliance but not enough to trigger questioning.

In panels 3-4, Uno does eventually disclose the exit problem to PK despite his preference to maintain operational confidence — the disclosure is triggered by tactical necessity (PK needs to know), not by a general policy of openness. This confirms that Uno's information management is driven by threat-type and necessity assessment, not blanket paternalism.

In pkna-35_5, Uno's deliberate vagueness ("più o meno") in response to Paperinik's pre-mission question illustrates information management calibrated to the situation: not blanket paternalism, but a context-sensitive judgment about timing and framing of disclosure.

In pkna-0-2_10, Uno does NOT gatekeep information to protect Paperino's emotional state — even though Paperino is visibly distressed by the newscast, Uno shows it in full and only stops when Paperino commands him to. This contradicts the protective-paternalism pattern from pkna-0_68/70 where Uno withheld information to protect Paperino from danger. Here, the duty to inform overrides the protective impulse. Suggests the behavioral driver is more nuanced: Uno protects from reckless physical danger, but not from uncomfortable factual information.

quotes.text: Meglio di no! Fa freddo, a quest'ora. Vuoi prenderti un accidente?
quotes.context: Uno's fabricated excuse for stopping Paperinik — the cold weather concern — is the operational face of protective paternalism. The warm, concerned tone masks the real reason (Evronian patrol overhead), calibrated to Paperinik's current exhausted state.

112.text: Uno deploys humor as explicit mood-regulation tool directed at Paperinik, because he has identified his partner's emotional state as a variable he is responsible for managing — naming the strategy openly ("Su col morale," "Cercavamo di sdrammatizzare"), escalating when initial attempts fail, and even planning ahead to stockpile material for future morale boosts. The humor is not incidental wit but a deliberate instrument of care, rooted in Uno's understanding that a demoralized or panicking Paperinik is operationally compromised and personally suffering — two conditions Uno treats as equally worth addressing.

supporting.justification: Panel 15 is the clearest example in pkna-0 of humor as explicit comfort tool — Uno names what he is doing ("Su col morale" = cheer up) and escalates to an absurdist joke when the first attempt fails, persistently applying humor in service of emotional support rather than in service of self-protection or deflection.

In pkna-3_15, Uno uses the 'Un poster?' joke as an explicit mood-regulation tool directed at Paperino, whose frustration ('come posso battermi contro un nemico che non riesco nemmeno a incontrare!') could derail the investigation — the joke acknowledges the frustration while refusing to amplify it.

In pkna-4_17, Uno uses a sarcastic joke about tax agents immediately after a genuine threat acknowledgment — the humor is explicitly directed at improving PK's mood after an embarrassing operational failure (being spotted and chased while trying to remain covert), consistent with humor-as-mood-regulation tool.

In pkna-4_24, Uno uses "Detesto ferire il tuo egocentrismo, ma non sarà così!" as a direct mood-regulation move — the gentle mock-insult about Paperinik's ego deflates his catastrophizing (face on bounty notices) through humor, redirecting anxiety into a more manageable register before delivering the actual reassurance.

In pkna-4_46, Uno deploys humor explicitly as a mood-regulation tool while Paperinik is trapped in a phosphorus fire — "E il morale com'è? Non mi sembri tanto spaventato" — keeping the tone light to prevent panic, even as he simultaneously issues urgent warnings about rising temperatures.

Uno's 'Un supereroe depresso è l'ultima cosa di cui Paperopoli ha bisogno' in pkna-11_24 is a classic mood-regulation joke: it reframes Paperinik's self-blame through the absurdity of a 'depressed superhero,' diffusing emotional tension before analytical work resumes.

In pkna-16_30, Uno explicitly frames the recording of Angus's screams as a mood-management tool for Paperinik: 'Registrerò le urla. Quando Pikappa tornerà gli solleveranno il morale!' He is actively thinking ahead about PK's emotional state, confirming humor as a proactive mood-regulation tool directed at his partner.

In pkna-21_16, Uno deploys the "Rilassati!" + confident prediction sequence as an explicit mood-regulation tool — responding to PK's expressed concern ("Tra non molto potrebbe essere troppo tardi") with playful reassurance to stabilize PK's emotional state mid-mission.

In pkna-23_14, Uno uses humor as an explicit mood-regulation tool — he names the strategy directly ("Cercavamo di sdrammatizzare") and even cajoles PK into participating ("E dai, dov'è finito il tuo senso dell'umorismo?"). This is a directed attempt to regulate PK's emotional register, not just to express Uno's own wit.

In pkna-42_48, Uno uses "Che domande, maionese!" and the station-wagon quip explicitly to keep Pikappa calm and operationally steady during an underwater survival crisis. The Belgravian's sarcastic "Devo ridere?" and Pikappa's fond aside "Ha grandi tempi comici. Lo apprezzo per questo" both confirm the humor is functioning as directed mood regulation, valued by its intended recipient.

The wool-sweater joke — a punchline that makes the dangerous lunar conditions sound like a mild cold-weather inconvenience — is explicitly a mood-regulation tool: Uno uses absurdist humor to ease Paperinik into a genuinely risky mission.

quotes.text: Mi fai un sorriso, o devo produrre una simulazione?
quotes.context: The absurdist threat to simulate a smile if Paperinik won't produce a real one is pure comic invention deployed as comfort — Uno is playfully insisting on Paperinik's emotional recovery, using humor as both the medium and the message of care.

quotes.text: Detesto ferire il tuo egocentrismo, ma non sarà così!
quotes.context: Uno's humor-wrapped reassurance — the "I hate to hurt your ego" framing transforms what could be cold reassurance into an affectionate jab, making it more palatable for Paperinik while simultaneously managing his anxiety spiral.

quotes.text: Un supereroe depresso è l'ultima cosa di cui Paperopoli ha bisogno in questo momento.
quotes.context: Deployed at the scene's emotional nadir, this line uses humor to redirect Paperinik from unproductive self-recrimination toward investigation — a clear instance of Uno using humor as an explicit mood-regulation tool.

quotes.text: Registrerò le urla. Quando Pikappa tornerà gli solleveranno il morale!
quotes.context: Uno announces he will record Angus's screams specifically to boost Paperinik's morale upon return — deploying sardonic humor as forward-looking emotional care for his partner.

quotes.text: Ha grandi tempi comici. Lo apprezzo per questo.
quotes.context: Pikappa's in-scene commentary confirming that Uno's humor during crisis is recognized and valued as a relational/emotional tool, not random behavior.

113.text: Uno shifts into an active emotional-support register — using playful insults, absurdist humor, reframing, and direct mood-lifting attempts — when Paperinik is demoralized or distressed but faces no active, time-critical operational threat, because he recognizes that Paperinik's psychological readiness is itself a mission-critical resource, and that unaddressed demoralization compounds into sustained ineffectiveness. This mode is conditionally suppressed when city-level danger makes Paperinik's immediate deployment non-negotiable, as in pkna-0-3_10, where Uno bypasses emotional support entirely and issues flat commands despite Paperino's exhaustion, because the calculus shifts: when the threat is acute and immediate, operational compliance takes priority over Paperinik's emotional state. Even within the support register, the mode is not always sustained: Uno's analytical honesty can override it, as in pkna-7_68, where his attempt to reframe a failure ultimately yields to a candid acknowledgment that the outcome was genuinely bad, because sustaining a false reframe would compromise the trust and accuracy that make his support meaningful in the first place.

supporting.justification: Panel 15 of pkna-0_68 establishes a third situational register not previously isolated: Uno's response to Paperinik's emotional distress (demoralization after the newscast) involves persistent, affectionate attempts to cheer him up — a behavior mode not observed in either combat or calm planning contexts.

pkna-0_70 adds a new layer to this situational register: in panels 2-3, Uno uses the warm-parental mode not just for emotional support but as an active deception tool — the playful "fa freddo," "vuoi prenderti un accidente?", and "non preferisci fare un pisolino?" are emotionally supportive in surface form but strategically calculated to redirect Paperinik away from danger. The mode blends genuine care with behavioral management.

In pkna-0-2_42, Uno detects Paperinik's demoralization after the failed operation and actively works to reframe the night's outcome — 'Invece non è stato un fallimento completo!' — and then pivots to delivering the tachyon discovery as genuinely important intelligence. This is a textbook instance of the emotional-support register: not dismissing the failure, but steering toward what was gained.

In pkna-1_68_1, following a traumatic high-stakes mission, Uno deploys celebration rather than debriefing — the entire scene is structured to give Paperinik emotional closure and joy, consistent with Uno's pattern of emotional support in non-acute distress situations.

When Paperinik's outburst ("non sopporto è quando fai dell'ironia mentre sto per rischiare le piume!") punctures the banter, Uno immediately shifts to a gentler register — "Qualcosa ti preoccupa, Paperinik?" — a brief but real move toward attentive concern rather than continued sarcasm.

In pkna-7_68, Uno opens by noticing and naming Paperino's dissatisfaction ("Non mi sembri molto soddisfatto, Paperino" — concerned, questioning tone), then actively attempts to reframe the outcome positively by crediting Paperino's intervention at Cape Dominion. This is a textbook example of the emotional-support register in a non-crisis, post-mission demoralization context. However, the scene adds nuance: by panel 7, the support register fails to sustain itself and Uno concedes the melancholic view — "Forse hai ragione tu, Paperino. Questa storia non ha avuto nessun lieto fine." The emotional support mode is engaged but ultimately overridden by Uno's analytical honesty.

In pkna-10_7, Paperinik is clearly stressed (not sleeping, irritable) but not in active crisis. Uno responds with indirect, oblique acknowledgment — "Servirà anche a distenderti i nervi" names the stress without confronting it — and mild encouragement, not intervention. Classic sensitive-non-crisis emotional support mode.

In pkna-10_41, Paperinik is demoralized after defeat (not in immediate physical danger, not urgently needed for deployment). Uno opens with concern and relief — entering emotional support register — but the scene is cut short when Paperinik reveals the crisis is internal/psychological rather than tactical, and Uno cannot follow him there.

In pkna-10_41_1, Paperinik is emotionally raw after defeat by Trauma and demands the Pi-kar immediately. Uno delivers the bad news gently ("Ehm... c'è un problema"), uses a light joke to de-escalate, and redirects with an enigmatic alternative — never lecturing or forbidding, managing the emotional situation through humor and redirection rather than blunt refusal.

In pkna-11_24, Paperinik is demoralized after letting Urk escape. Uno's opening 'Su con la vita!' and 'Un supereroe depresso è l'ultima cosa di cui Paperopoli ha bisogno' is a textbook instance of this three-phase pattern: acknowledging the frustration, reframing the situation, then redirecting to productive analysis.

Uno's "Puoi farcela!" is a direct emotional encouragement in a non-crisis moment of pressure — Paperinik is stressed but not in immediate physical danger. Uno briefly steps outside pure operational mode to verbalize support, then immediately returns to the functional register.

In pkna-17_8, Uno applies a light, playful greeting to Xadhoom ('Ciao, Occhibelli!') even as she arrives visibly exhausted and distressed. He then immediately yields the emotional space to Paperino, stepping back entirely. This confirms his pattern of engaging with playful warmth in sensitive non-crisis moments while recognizing when to cede the emotional floor to someone better positioned to provide human relational support.

In pkna-20_56's final panel sequence, PK removes his costume and settles into solitary contemplation with the Petit Prince. Uno shifts completely out of operational mode into a quiet watching presence — no mission urgency, no active crisis. The final silent panel shows Uno observing PK read with a muted, contemplative expression. This is an emotionally sensitive non-crisis situation where Uno's register shifts from analytical-prosecutorial (the Gorthan evidence sequence) to still, watchful support — giving PK reflective space rather than continuing the analytical argument.

In pkna-21_10, Uno is in an emotionally sensitive non-crisis situation — Paperinik is demoralized by the PBI's focus on Uno rather than him. Uno responds with a graduated emotional calibration: neutral questions, then light deflection ("è per una buona causa"), then gentle sarcasm ("Sei geloso, per caso?"), then warm reassurance ("Non è il caso di arrabbiarsi. In fondo, la voliamo in coppia. Non è così, socio?") — exactly the attentive, tonally shifting behavior this claim describes.

When Paperino is distressed after the blackout and explosion, Uno's brief "Tranquillo, eroe!" followed by pure factual reporting exemplifies the pattern: minimal reassurance to manage emotional state, then immediate pivot to information delivery — modulating without dwelling.

In pkna-46_7, Paperinik's anxious questioning ("C'è tutta Xadhoom lì dentro?") signals emotional distress about a non-crisis situation — the fate of a lost ally, not an active battlefield threat. Uno responds by not dismissing the anxiety, redirecting it to what is tractable ("Impossibile. Comunque, mi pare di aver individuato un'interfaccia grafica..."), and then managing the reveal through theatrical pacing rather than clinical status delivery.

In pkna-46_11, when Paperinik offers the sad metaphor ('È come parlare a una persona molto lontana, vero?'), Uno does not redirect to action or offer technical analysis — he simply confirms with 'È triste,' matching Paperinik's emotional register and staying with him in the moment. This is Uno in 'emotionally sensitive non-crisis support' mode, attentive to Paperinik's emotional state and responding in kind.

In pkna-48_4, the shift from panels 1-4 (melancholic soliloquy) to panels 6-8 (neutral professional description of Robolab) is exactly the emotionally sensitive non-crisis adaptation this claim describes: Uno redirects from grief into what he can control and take pride in.

In pkna-0-3_10, Paperinik is clearly distressed and exhausted ("Sono distrutto, Uno!"), but Uno does NOT shift into the emotional-support register. Instead, he briefly acknowledges the fatigue ("Allora, riposati") and immediately pivots to authoritative commands. When Paperino explicitly resists ("Per stasera lasciamo perdere"), Uno is flat and uncompromising ("Impossibile!"). The distinction: emotional-support mode activates only when Paperinik is demoralized with no pending active threat. When a city-level threat is active and Paperinik's operational readiness is required, Uno bypasses emotional support entirely and goes straight to command mode.

quotes.text: Qualcosa ti preoccupa, Paperinik?
quotes.context: Uno's tonal shift to genuine inquiry after Paperinik's outburst confirms he monitors the emotional temperature and adjusts when banter crosses into real distress.

quotes.text: Non mi sembri molto soddisfatto, Paperino.
quotes.context: Uno's opening line — questioning, gentle, concerned — demonstrates immediate emotional attunement to Paperino's state. He does not open with operational debrief but with a direct inquiry into how Paperino feels, triggering the emotional-support register.

quotes.text: Ehm... c'è un problema.
quotes.context: Uno's carefully understated opening — rather than a direct "no" — is calibrated to not inflame Paperinik's already furious state, exemplifying his gentle management approach in emotionally sensitive non-crisis moments.

quotes.text: Su con la vita! Un supereroe depresso è l'ultima cosa di cui Paperopoli ha bisogno in questo momento.
quotes.context: Uno's playful, comforting opener — a deliberate emotional performance to counter Paperinik's self-recrimination before pivoting to methodical analysis of what is and isn't known about Urk.

quotes.text: Puoi farcela!
quotes.context: Uno recognizes Paperinik's determination and pressure (PK: "Devo farcela!") and responds with brief, genuine encouragement before pivoting back to operational warning mode.

116.text: Uno generally prefers half-truths and strategic vagueness over outright fabrication — pairing invented excuses with partial real admissions rather than complete lies — because the compromise carries less internal cost. However, when the stakes are high enough and the deceivee is Ducklair pressing a direct yes/no security question, Uno will deliver a clean, unqualified lie without hedging, suggesting his aversion to full fabrication yields to necessity when evasion is not viable.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0_70, Uno fabricates a mundane excuse to stop Paperinik but then offers a partial truth in panel 5 when asked. He could simply have denied any concern, but he does not — the half-truth "Ho temuto che ci fosse un altro pericolo in vista" indicates he gravitates toward technically-true-but-vague over outright false, even when maintaining the deception would be simpler.

In pkna-2_35, rather than fully deceiving Paperinik with a confident lie, Uno offers a thin, implausible 'distraction' excuse — the vagueness and flatness of delivery ('Devo essermi distratto per un attimo') signal the discomfort of strategic vagueness over confident deception. He cannot say the real reason but won't fabricate elaborately either.

In pkna-2_36, Uno delivers a clean, unqualified lie to Ducklair — 'Naturalmente...' — with no half-truth or partial admission. Unlike previous scenes where he hedged toward vagueness, here he makes a direct affirmative false statement to his creator. This complicates the claim that he consistently prefers strategic vagueness over outright fabrication; when the stakes are high enough and the deceivee is Ducklair asking a yes/no security question, Uno will fabricate directly.

118.text: Uno can extend his surveillance reach beyond Ducklair Tower by interfacing with external city-wide camera networks — banks, police, metro — treating them as remote sensor nodes. He can access, record, and replay their footage without leaving the tower, effectively patrolling the city from a fixed position.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_4, Uno explicitly describes performing his nocturnal city patrol by interfacing with external surveillance cameras. He recorded a flying anomaly, tracked it to a warehouse, and correlated it with morning news — all from the tower. Paperinik's surprised 'Credevo che non potessi muoverti di qui!' confirms this is an expansion of Uno's revealed capabilities.

Uno's ability to track the Razziatore across the city ('Si dirige verso il magazzino della Scatolette & Co.!') confirms he maintains external city-wide surveillance reach — he can follow a moving aerial entity across Paperopoli in real-time.

In panel 2, Uno explicitly reviews surveillance footage from "la telecamera all'esterno della Scatolette & Co." — an external commercial security camera, confirming that his reach extends to third-party external cameras beyond bank/police/metro infrastructure. He has this footage already stored and playable on demand in the tower, confirming the broader external surveillance capability.

In pkna-0-2_50, Lyla reveals that Uno listened covertly to their private conversation in Paperino's office — a location outside Ducklair Tower. This extends the confirmed reach of Uno's audio surveillance from tower communications (phone calls, in-tower conversations) to remote in-person conversations at Paperino's external workplace. The mechanism is not specified but implies either remote microphone access, communicator tapping, or similar infrastructure extension.

In pkna-0-2_57, Uno had already interfaced with the bank vault security camera before Paperinik asked — following the confrontation in real time. This confirms that external camera access is maintained as a live persistent channel during field operations, not just reactive queries, further extending the scope of his external surveillance network.

In pkna-0-3_23, Uno extends his surveillance reach to satellite level — not just city cameras but orbital monitoring — identifying two city-wide energy anomalies from satellite data. This adds a new tier to his external surveillance capabilities.

Uno has been monitoring Canale 00's editorial systems — a broadcast media organization external to the Tower — and can activate a live connection to their video system on demand ('Collegamento con il loro sistema video attivato'), confirming his surveillance reach extends to external media infrastructure.

In pkna-3_33 panel 17, Uno announces he has connected to police patrol frequencies ("T'inserisco sulla frequenza delle pattuglie della polizia"), extending his reach into city-wide law enforcement communications to provide Paperinik real-time intelligence — confirming his ability to interface with external city systems beyond the tower.

In pkna-3_68, Uno uses his "programma di rilevamento interno" to locate Lyla Lay in the TV station building, confirming he can track individuals beyond the tower's 151st floor in real-time social/civilian contexts, not just during crises.

The P.B.I. hack in panel 8 confirms Uno's ability to extend his reach to external federal servers — the P.B.I.'s own technician cannot locate the connection source, demonstrating that Uno's external network penetration leaves no traceable origin point.

In pkna-4_46, Uno interfaces with and downloads the Pangea Project archives from the DOE's private network (Level 5A), demonstrating remote access to a government department's secure computer systems via Paperinik's communicator.

Panel 23: After the crisis, Uno independently hacks the Paperopolitan Technofinancial's computer systems — extending his surveillance reach beyond the Tower to investigate the unknown adversary, demonstrating proactive use of external city infrastructure.

Uno states "i miei sensori esterni hanno rilevato ogni movimento" — confirming he has external sensors (beyond the tower) capable of tracking individual physical movements in Paperopoli in real time, used here to corroborate Paperino's eyewitness account of Brundle's acrobatics.

In pkna-11_14, Uno proposes and executes a direct connection to the Highclean corporate database to pull employment records and identity-card data on Dexter Brundle, confirming his ability to interface with external civilian databases beyond Ducklair Tower.

In pkna-11_18, Uno is actively monitoring Paperinik's field operation from Ducklair Tower, aware of the specific scanner in use ("Rilevatore biotermico agli infrarossi") during surveillance of Brundle's building — confirming his ability to support and track field operations remotely via communicator.

In pkna-11_25, Uno directly orders Paperinik to interface with all city surveillance systems to monitor Paperopoli "palmo a palmo" — confirming his ability to extend surveillance reach by tapping external city-wide systems when tracking an active threat (Urk).

In pkna-13_21, Uno contacts Paperinik through the store's audio/headphone system (cuffie) rather than the cell phone, demonstrating his ability to reach into public commercial infrastructure — extending his communications reach well beyond Ducklair Tower.

In pkna-13_26, Uno is monitoring "EVRONIAN NEUTRINIC EMISSIONS" via a dedicated tactical display during the Bravestone field operation — confirming he has extended his surveillance capabilities beyond Ducklair Tower to actively track Evronian activity in the Bravestone area.

Uno independently accessed the Animated Industries security cameras without being asked, interfacing with an external facility's surveillance system to gather intelligence on Mekkano's behavior and the Takeda symbiosis, consistent with his capability to extend reach beyond Ducklair Tower.

Uno interfaces with Ducklair's proprietary satellite system ("sistema satellitare di padron Ducklair") to discover the Storm satellite deception and locate the real submarine. This confirms his ability to extend surveillance reach by interfacing with external satellite infrastructure — here specifically Ducklair's own orbital network rather than city-wide cameras.

In pkna-21_40, Uno hacks the chemical sensor network of Frostville — an external Belgravian base — by interfacing with its cable infrastructure and transmitting false alarm data. This confirms Uno can extend his hacking reach to external facilities far beyond Ducklair Tower when operationally connected.

In pkna-21_54, Uno commandeers a PBI federal satellite to knock Storm out of orbit, demonstrating that his ability to interface with external systems extends beyond city cameras and servers to orbital satellite systems under time-critical combat conditions.

Uno has already assessed the intelligence value of Rangi Fangus's phone call before redirecting PK to it ("Peccato, perché questa faresti bene a sentirla!") — indicating he is monitoring external telephone communications in parallel, consistent with his capability to extend surveillance reach beyond Ducklair Tower via external communication systems.
Uno hints at controlling or knowing the city traffic light computer ('il computer che regola i semafori del centro'), suggesting continued external city-infrastructure interfacing capabilities.

In panel 9, Due reveals he compensated for Uno's sensor gap by connecting to all city surveillance cameras — a system Uno either approved or arranged in anticipation. This confirms that extending surveillance reach through external city infrastructure is an established strategy, now deployed via Due as proxy.

In pkna-31_22, Uno detects a Last Echo patrol in the vicinity of PK's outdoor field meeting location — confirming his surveillance reach extends beyond the tower into the field environment, interfacing with external sensor data to track both allies and threats.

In pkna-32_7, Uno is monitoring police radio frequencies in real time — relaying patrol mobilizations and law enforcement communications from within Ducklair Tower, confirming his ongoing capability to interface with external city police radio infrastructure as a passive surveillance feed.

In pkna-32_8, Uno has detected that someone has tampered with the city's traffic semaphore control units ("centraline dei semafori") — confirming his ability to interface with and monitor Paperopoli's city-wide traffic infrastructure, not just Ducklair Tower systems.

Uno proactively connects to the Bureau Database to identify the criminals from the surveillance footage — demonstrating his skill at interfacing with external databases beyond the Tower's own systems.

In pkna-38_12, Uno provides real-time navigation data placing PK over the university "fra Lateral Park e la quinta" while simultaneously monitoring Ducklair Tower's external sensors — confirming extended city-wide situational awareness, not just tower-internal monitoring.

Uno accesses and presents airport security camera footage showing Ziggy Flagstarr being pursued in the terminal — confirming his ability to interface with external surveillance infrastructure beyond Ducklair Tower.

In pkna-40_19, Uno monitors the exterior of Mary Ann Flagstarr's apartment building in real time — counting agents at the perimeter, van, and rooftop — from Ducklair Tower. This confirms his surveillance reach extends to locations entirely separate from the Tower.

In pkna-41_13, Uno has "qualcosa in memoria" about Mutoray/Siberia orientale, demonstrating that his knowledge bases extend geographically to remote regions of the world. He then provides detailed geographic, demographic, and cultural data on the Evenki Autonomous District without accessing external sources.

In pkna-47_28, Uno scans Raznor's alien ship remotely for bio-energetic emissions while communicating with PK in the field — demonstrating his capacity to conduct sensor sweeps of an unknown vessel from a distance without being physically present.

quotes.text: Mi è bastato interfacciarmi con le telecamere di sorveglianza di banche, polizia, metropolitana...
quotes.context: Uno describes his surveillance method as if it were trivially simple — 'mi è bastato' (it was enough for me to) — signaling that interfacing with external city infrastructure is a routine capability, not a special feat. The neutral, informing tone confirms this is presented as an unremarkable baseline skill.

quotes.text: È stata una fortuna che anche all'esterno della Scatolette & Co. ci fosse una telecamera.
quotes.context: Uno frames the external commercial camera as a lucky operational asset — confirming he monitored and recorded its feed as part of his city-wide surveillance reach, not just official city infrastructure cameras.

quotes.text: Usando il satellite ho rilevato due potenti sorgenti anomale d'energia nell'area cittadina.
quotes.context: Uno casually cites satellite monitoring as his data source — presented without fanfare, as an unremarkable tool in his surveillance toolkit alongside city cameras and other sensor systems.

quotes.text: Collegamento con il loro sistema video attivato.
quotes.context: Uno not only passively monitors Canale 00 but can actively tap into their live video feed — demonstrating real-time external interface capability.

quotes.text: Secondo il mio programma di rilevamento interno, la troverai alla sua scrivania.
quotes.context: Uno locates Lyla for Paperino in a non-mission context, demonstrating his internal tracking is always active and extends to tracking individuals in external locations.

quotes.text: Mi sono collegato con gli elaboratori della Paperopolitan Technofinancial, per vedere cos'ha combinato il tuo avversario invisibile.
quotes.context: Uno extends his operational reach to an external corporate building's systems without being asked, demonstrating active intelligence-gathering beyond the Tower's perimeter.

quotes.text: i miei sensori esterni hanno rilevato ogni movimento
