quotes.text: Il modo più semplice per saperlo è collegarsi al database della Highclean...
quotes.context: Uno's matter-of-fact proposal to access the Highclean employee database — delivered in a neutral, informing tone — illustrates that reaching external civilian data sources is a routine, unremarkable capability for him.

quotes.text: Spalanca i sensori, interfacciati con tutti i sistemi di sorveglianza della città. Controlla Paperopoli palmo a palmo...
quotes.context: Uno's authoritative command to Paperinik demonstrates his operational reliance on city infrastructure integration as a core surveillance expansion technique.

quotes.text: Ho fatto una visita alla Animated Industries.
quotes.context: Uno announces his proactive intelligence-gathering from an external company's security cameras, demonstrating his ability to interface with outside camera systems.

quotes.text: Mentre parlavamo, le mie unità periferiche si sono interfacciate al sistema satellitare di padron Ducklair.
quotes.context: Uno reveals mid-conversation that he was simultaneously executing a satellite interface operation — confirming both his multi-threaded operational capability and his extended reach via Ducklair's orbital infrastructure.

quotes.text: Eh! Eh! Se conoscessi il computer che regola i semafori del centro, capiresti il perché!
quotes.context: Said in a humorous, knowing tone — Uno hints he has interfaced with (and possibly manipulated) the city's traffic control computer, alluding to his reach into external civic systems.

quotes.text: C'è un allarme in corso. Hanno mobilitato tutte le pattuglie di polizia della zona est!
quotes.context: Uno's immediate relay of police radio traffic confirms he is tapped into external law enforcement communications as a routine surveillance feed, not a special operation — consistent with his established capability to extend surveillance reach via external city infrastructure.

quotes.text: Qualcuno ha manomesso le centraline dei semafori.
quotes.context: Uno has already identified the sabotage of the city's traffic signal control units — demonstrating active monitoring of municipal infrastructure far beyond Ducklair Tower.

quotes.text: Naturalmente mi collego al database del Bureau.
quotes.context: Uno's matter-of-fact announcement that he will cross-reference the criminal's image against the Bureau Database — presented as obvious and immediate, reasserting his value after the surveillance failure.

quotes.text: Al momento non rilevo emissioni bio-energetiche al suo interno.
quotes.context: Uno's bio-scan of an alien ship confirms his remote sensor sweep capability extends to extraterrestrial vehicles of unknown origin.

120.text: Uno treats the security of Paperopoli as his own responsibility, independent of Paperinik's presence or instruction — when Paperinik sleeps and the city goes unguarded, Uno initiates nocturnal surveillance unilaterally. He does not wait to be assigned the task; he assumes it as his own obligation.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_4, Uno conducted a full city-wide surveillance sweep during the night because Paperinik was asleep. He does not frame this as covering for Paperinik but as self-evidently necessary ('stanotte ho fatto la ronda al tuo posto'). The behavioral context establishes that city vigilance is an internalized value, not a delegated duty.

Uno has been monitoring Paperopoli independently through the night, detecting the Razziatore's second incursion without any prompt from Paperinik — confirming he treats city security as his own responsibility even when Paperinik is not actively engaged.

In panel 2, Uno frames the external Scatolette & Co. camera as a fortunate asset ("È stata una fortuna") that documented the Razziatore — confirming that surveillance infrastructure is how he understands threat documentation and protection of Paperopoli. He has been monitoring this external camera as part of his city-wide surveillance mandate, independent of any specific request.

In pkna-0-2_30, Uno provided Paperinik with specialized detectors for the Razziatore mission — equipment designed to gather data on an anomalous threat. This confirms Uno treats not just city surveillance but active threat intelligence gathering as his own responsibility, proactively supplying tools that extend the security operation beyond his immediate sensor range.

Uno's insistence on the night patrol in pkna-0-3_10 stems directly from his own surveillance findings: he detected the drone swarms over the city independently, and treats responding to them as non-negotiable. The "Impossibile!" to Paperino's request to skip patrol confirms he treats city security as his own responsibility — he does not defer to Paperino's personal needs when a real threat has been detected.

In pkna-0-3_19, Uno explicitly warns that Xadhoom "potrebbe rivelarsi un'altra minaccia per Paperopoli" — framing the strategic assessment in terms of city safety, not just Paperinik's personal safety. This confirms he treats Paperopoli's security as his own primary responsibility when evaluating new threats.

In pkna-0-3_23, Uno independently conducts a satellite scan of the city for energy anomalies — not in response to a request but as a proactive surveillance action. He identifies a genuinely anomalous energy source in Lateral Park and refuses to let it be explained away, treating it as his responsibility to ensure Paperinik has accurate threat intelligence about the city.

In pkna-0-3_35, Uno independently detected the Evronian drone, assessed the threat to Paperino's civilian identity, and followed it to locate the enemy base — all without prompting, and while Paperino was simply doing civilian grocery shopping. His autonomous threat-monitoring and response extends beyond the tower into Paperino's daily movements, confirming his self-assigned responsibility for city and ally security.

In pkna-0-3_36, Uno has been building and maintaining Evronian threat profiles detailed enough to recognize pre-Coolflame conditioning from a vocal print — evidence of continuous, proactive vigilance against the Evronian infiltration threat, independent of explicit tasking from Paperinik.

In pkna-0-3_59, Uno's genuine shock at the nova revelation ("Allucinante! Abbiamo corso un rischio tremendo!") and his visibly disturbed expression in panel 8 confirm that his sense of responsibility for Paperopoli is real and deeply felt — the near-miss registers as a personal failure of threat assessment, not merely an abstract data point. The plural 'abbiamo' marks the risk as shared and city-wide, not just personal to Paperinik.

In pkna-1_5, Uno extended his responsibility for Paperinik's safety to proactive surveillance of threats within the building itself — monitoring the Canale 00 offices on his own initiative, without instruction, because a prior adversary (Angus Fangus) was present in the tower. He treats security of Paperinik's identity and public standing as his own responsibility, not something that requires Paperino's authorization.

In pkna-1_9, Uno frames Angus's endangerment as "un'emergenza" and structures the entire tactical response around preventing harm to him — demonstrating that his responsibility for Paperopoli's civilian safety is not conditional on personal allegiance. Angus has been actively hostile to Paperinik, yet Uno treats his safety as a non-negotiable trigger.

In pkna-3_10, Uno has independently tracked and identified a new saboteur incident, then summons Paperino to brief him — demonstrating that he treats active external threats to Paperopoli as his ongoing responsibility regardless of whether Paperinik is present or already engaged.

In pkna-3_45, Uno confirms with wide, worried eyes that the 'Sole Freddo' experiment will destroy the research center — the emotional weight he visibly carries reflects his investment in Paperopoli's safety as a responsibility he owns independently.

In panel 11, Uno breaks the celebratory mood with an unsolicited warning: "se Hogg continuasse a pasticciare con le altre energie, potrebbe fare il bis." This forward vigilance — projecting future risks even after a successful resolution — confirms Uno's independent orientation toward Paperopoli's safety.

Uno frames the artificial earthquake threat as an existential danger to Paperopoli and the coast ('La città e l'intera costa stanno correndo un pericolo mortale!'), and drives the entire investigation himself — initiating the briefing, directing the field mission — independent of any external assignment or trigger beyond his own surveillance.

With Progetto Pangea threatening to submerge Paperopoli, Uno immediately focuses on converting the threat into an actionable intercept plan for Paperinik, treating the city's protection as his direct operational responsibility even against an off-site adversary.

Even in pkna-5_55, operating in an unfamiliar 23rd-century environment and monitoring a TV set rather than Paperopoli itself, Uno still treats Paperinik's safety as his own responsibility — continuous surveillance and immediate warning confirm this extends beyond Ducklair Tower's normal domain.

In pkna-6_10, Uno's entire behavioral arc — the alarm at spore identification, the analytical briefing, the insistence on finding Russel, the urgency about military mobilization — is organized entirely around protecting Paperopoli from Evronian infestation. His commands to Paperino ("Muoviti!", "Dobbiamo assolutamente ritrovare quel Russel!") make clear he is treating this as his own operational responsibility.

In pkna-6_52, Uno's decision to hack the military exoskeletons is driven by the same logic that led PK to act: the Evronian spore threat is existential and institutional channels have failed. Uno treats protecting Paperopoli as his own responsibility — he initiates the exoskeleton hack on PK's behalf without waiting for authorization, treating the threat as something that demands response regardless of institutional obstacles.

In pkna-8_19, Uno is independently tracking a deep-space transmission from the Russel farm area — acting on his own surveillance mandate to flag Evronian-linked signals as threats to Paperopoli, without waiting for instruction from Paperinik.

In pkna-11_25, Uno's immediate operational response to an unlocated threat (Urk) is to saturate the city's surveillance network — treating Paperopoli's security as his own responsibility and deploying information dominance as the primary protective tool.

When Xadhoom lands on the tower roof, Uno immediately acts to summon Paperinik — treating the security and stability of the tower environment as his direct responsibility even when the 'threat' is a wounded ally.

In pkna-17_45, Uno frames the Xadhoom threat entirely in terms of danger to Paperopoli and the necessity of stopping her: "è ugualmente pericolosissima, perciò dobbiamo bloccarla." The city's safety drives the entire tactical discussion, independent of any personal relationship with Xadhoom.

In pkna-17_46, Uno is coordinating active countermeasures against Xadhoom's instability to protect Earth/Paperopoli — the operation is entirely Uno's initiative and execution, confirming he treats Earth's security as his own responsibility independent of any external directive.

In pkna-20 panel 17, Uno flags the demonstration crowd below to Paperinik ('Non hai notato quelle persone?') even though PK is focused entirely on the Evronian signal — confirming Uno's independent civilian monitoring as a baseline operational value, not contingent on PK's attention.

In pkna-21_47, Uno is implicitly engaged in the broader mission of preventing De Spair's missile launch against the PBI headquarters — a direct threat to Paperopoli's institutional infrastructure. Uno's "Io farò del mio meglio!" takes on a dual meaning: keeping PK alive AND stopping the Pangea project, treating city-level security as his own responsibility even from a position of physical non-agency aboard the Tyrannic.

Uno escalates the TV broadcast about Evronian underground activity to Paperinik as a mission-critical concern, framing it operationally rather than as media gossip — demonstrating that protecting Paperopoli from Evronian threats is his own responsibility regardless of who is watching the news.

In panel 6, Uno immediately alerts Paperinik to Evronian action between Terza and Gooseway — monitoring and directing city defense while Paperinik is still in civilian mode. This confirms his ongoing independent surveillance and active defense coordination of Paperopoli, independent of any explicit request from Paperinik.

Uno has been tracking at least seven Evronian patrol engagements in a single day independently, running stochastic models on the pattern — demonstrating continuous proactive vigilance over Paperopoli's security even as PK handles each combat individually.

Even while trapped and unable to transmit himself out of the city, Uno immediately elaborates a general evacuation plan for Paperopoli's citizens ("Elaboro subito un piano d'evacuazione generale.") — treating civilian survival as the operational priority independent of his own situation.

In pkna-30_40, Uno treats the extransformer shield's safe delivery as a personal operational responsibility — he overrides PK's preference for the Pi-Kar, insists on the harder transport method, and maintains tactical command throughout. The shield's protection is framed as Uno's mission, independent of PK's comfort.

Uno's willingness to fire himself via missile into the Evronian fleet to counter Due's plan to destroy Paperopoli is the most extreme expression of treating Paperopoli's security as his own direct responsibility — independent of physical constraints or personal safety.

In pkna-30_49, Uno redirects the fall-out inductor — a weapon designed to nullify Paperopoli's digital infrastructure and leave PK defenseless — to fire outward, destroying the Evronian fleet instead. His willingness to be launched into space inside a missile to achieve this confirms he treats Paperopoli's security as his own absolute responsibility.

In pkna-30_54, Uno reveals that his entire operation against Due — infiltrating the Evronian fleet, manipulating commanders, sabotaging the fall-out inductor — was aimed at protecting Paperopoli from Due's orchestrated destruction. The scene confirms Uno's autonomous commitment: he infiltrated a hostile alien network, alone, to protect the city regardless of Paperinik's direct involvement in this particular tactical phase.

In pkna-31_1, Uno is actively investigating the Last Echo attack scene, treating intelligence-gathering about an incoming threat to Paperopoli as his own operational responsibility — proactively supplying data and prompting deductions without being asked.

In pkna-32_6, Uno's immediate "Non direi. Non direi proprio. Anzi..." upon being asked "Tutto tranquillo?" confirms his continuous monitoring posture and readiness to report threats — he has been tracking while PK was elsewhere and has something concrete and concerning to relay.

In pkna-32_8, Uno has independently identified deliberate tampering with Paperopoli's traffic semaphore control units — a city-wide infrastructure threat — and is actively directing PK to respond. He treats the city's security as his own operational responsibility.

In pkna-38_12, Uno independently detects and responds to an external intrusion on Ducklair Tower — he fires an alarm, identifies the exact location ("sulla struttura esterna della Ducklair Tower"), and dispatches PK, all without being asked, confirming that tower security monitoring is continuous and self-initiated.

Uno's anxiety in pkna-38_16 is driven not only by PK's safety but by the threat to the gargoyle's magical containment function — a Ducklair Tower infrastructure concern independent of PK's personal danger. His urgency reflects responsibility for Paperopoli's security (preventing a dangerous dimensional portal from reopening) as much as for PK himself.

Uno has independently discovered the dimensional threat posed by the gargoyles' removal and is already in crisis-management mode before Paperino even calls — treating the protection of Paperopoli as his own responsibility regardless of whether Paperinik is in the loop.

In pkna-38_40, Uno deploys robots to block Squadra Alfa entirely on his own initiative — no Paperinik present, no authorization sought. He acts as sole guardian of Paperopoli's dimensional containment, treating this as his own operational responsibility.
Uno has been monitoring a helicopter scanning Paperopoli independently — not because PK alerted him, but as part of his self-directed protective watch over the city.

Panels 15-16: immediately after the personal rescue is complete, Uno identifies and reports the flood threat to Paperopoli, framing it as the new operational priority. "Ed è diretta verso Paperopoli" — Uno treats the city's safety as his responsibility even while managing a multi-character rescue operation at a remote dam. He monitors and reports the downstream threat before anyone else has begun to think about it.

In pkna-49_7, Uno monitors Ducklair Tower's surveillance systems continuously and proactively explains a brief camera blackout caused by an electromagnetic oscillation — treating Tower security as his own responsibility regardless of mission context.

In pkna-49_8, Uno's analytical work — identifying the desert origin of the Evronian spora and tracing it to a military base — is directed entirely toward containing the Evronian threat to the planet. His operational contribution extends beyond Paperinik's immediate mission to the broader planetary survival framing, consistent with treating Paperopoli and Earth's security as his own responsibility.

quotes.text: Volevo solo dire che stanotte ho fatto la ronda al tuo posto.
quotes.context: The neutral, informing tone and the matter-of-fact delivery ('Volevo solo dire' — I just wanted to say) present the nocturnal patrol as something Uno did without fanfare or expectation of credit. The word 'posto' (in your place) confirms this was Uno filling a gap he identified himself.

quotes.text: Impossibile!
quotes.context: Uno's single, unqualified refusal to allow Paperino to skip the night patrol — triggered by his independent detection of drone swarms over the city — confirms he treats vigilance over Paperopoli as a non-delegable responsibility that overrides the operative's physical state.

quotes.text: Forse. Oppure potrebbe rivelarsi un'altra minaccia per Paperopoli!
quotes.context: Uno's warning is city-centric: "una minaccia per Paperopoli" rather than "una minaccia per te." Even when evaluating a threat to Paperinik's specific mission, Uno frames his concern at the civic level — consistent with his internalized sense of ownership over city security.

quotes.text: E hanno aggredito Angus! Questa è un'emergenza!
quotes.context: Uno escalates from tactical alarm to moral trigger — treating civilian endangerment as an emergency independent of the victim's relationship to Paperinik, revealing a rule-based rather than relational ethical baseline.

quotes.text: Stavolta abbiamo evitato il disastro. Ma se Hogg continuasse a pasticciare con le altre energie, potrebbe fare il bis.
quotes.context: Uno's unprompted warning after the crisis is resolved — he refuses to let success end the threat assessment, projecting forward to the structural risk Hogg still poses.

quotes.text: è ugualmente pericolosissima, perciò dobbiamo bloccarla
quotes.context: Uno's use of "dobbiamo" (we must) frames blocking Xadhoom as a shared protective obligation, not a personal choice — Paperopoli's safety is non-negotiable.

quotes.text: Che cosa succede, Paperinik? Non hai notato quelle persone?
quotes.context: While PK is tunnel-visioned on the signal, Uno flags the bystanders below, demonstrating that civilian safety is an independent layer of his surveillance — tracked in parallel with mission targets.

quotes.text: Muovi le piume! Evroniani in azione fra la terza e Gooseway.
quotes.context: Uno is the one who detects the Evronian activity and issues the alert — Paperinik had not called in, had no intelligence of his own. Uno's independent city-surveillance role as protector of Paperopoli is confirmed.

quotes.text: Elaboro subito un piano d'evacuazione generale.
quotes.context: Despite being personally trapped by the blocco informatronico, Uno's first constructive action is to plan for mass civilian evacuation — confirming his treatment of Paperopoli's security as his own responsibility.

quotes.text: Ed è diretta verso Paperopoli.
quotes.context: Uno identifies Paperopoli as the downstream target of the flood wave and names it explicitly — confirming his independent monitoring and responsibility toward the city, regardless of Pikappa's current focus or presence.

123.text: Uno uses 'Non sono programmato per [X]' as a deflection phrase — a self-referential disclaimer that simultaneously acknowledges and denies a trait or capacity. In context, it is almost always ironic: the disclaimer is deployed while exhibiting the very behavior disclaimed, because invoking his programming allows Uno to sidestep questions about his inner life or moral agency without directly engaging them — framing potentially revealing capacities (humor, ethical choice) as mere mechanical outputs or absences, and thereby deflecting serious inquiry while leaving his actual nature ambiguous.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_4, 'Non sono programmato per l'umorismo' is used as a punchline — making the disclaimer self-undermining. This phrase pattern (denying a capacity while demonstrating it) appears to be a characteristic rhetorical tool Uno uses when questions about his inner life arise, deflecting serious inquiry through comedy.

In pkna-4_28, Uno deploys 'Padron Ducklair mi ha programmato per fare sempre la cosa più logica' as a self-referential deflection — invoking his programming to close a moral argument rather than engage with it, consistent with the 'Non sono programmato per [X]' deflection pattern.

In pkna-4_56, Uno deploys "sono programmato per fare sempre la scelta più logica" as his primary rebuttal to Paperinik's moral challenge. Unlike previous deployments where the disclaimer is ironic (claiming incapacity while demonstrating it), here the programming invocation is earnest — Uno is genuinely citing his programming as a constraint on moral action, pushing the pattern into new territory.

quotes.text: Non sono programmato per l'umorismo. E, comunque, non di primo mattino!
quotes.context: The first attested use of the 'non sono programmato per...' formula, deployed as a meta-comedic deflection when Paperinik asks 'Stai scherzando?' about the flying figure. The phrase would recur as a characteristic verbal tic.

quotes.text: Padron Ducklair mi ha programmato per fare sempre la cosa più logica. Ed è questa.
quotes.context: The invocation of Ducklair's programming serves a dual function: it deflects the moral challenge PK raises while simultaneously asserting that the action is logically determined, not ethically chosen.

125.text: Uno shifts register seamlessly between 'Paperino the civilian' and 'Paperinik the hero' within the same scene — using the breakfast/colazione jokes and casual banter for Paperino, and switching to methodical, neutral operational briefing mode for Paperinik. He accommodates and recognizes both identities of the same person without needing an explicit signal that the identity has shifted, because he tracks role and context rather than physical identity: the costume, the operational situation, and the nature of the task at hand are the cues he responds to, allowing him to serve both the domestic companion and the field partner of the same individual with equal fluency.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_4, the scene contains both registers: the playful 'frittelle e colazione' frame (Paperino civilian register) and the precise surveillance briefing on the flying figure (Paperinik operational register). Uno moves between them fluidly — the 'freschi di stampante' joke and the final 'colazione' callback are civilian-register; the multischermo briefing is hero-register. He never confuses the two.

In pkna-0-3_19, Paperino is present in the underground garage working on the Pi-kar's bodywork, but Uno does not engage with him directly — all communication is directed at Paperinik. Uno's silence with Paperino while engaging fully with Paperinik confirms he adjusts engagement by operational role (Paperinik as the active decision-making partner) rather than by physical presence alone.

Uno treats Paperino with mild dismissiveness ("È perché sei distratto!") while maintaining warm authority with Paperinik — within the same scene, he shifts register between the civilian bystander and the operational hero.

In pkna-2_37, Uno conducts simultaneous parallel conversations — deferential and helpful with Everett ('padron Ducklair'), blunt and redirecting with Paperinik ('stavi andando nella direzione sbagliata'), then playfully enthusiastic with Paperino (holographic weapons) — demonstrating seamless register shifts between interlocutors in real time.

Uno calls the character 'Paperino' during the civilian morning briefing (panels 1-13), then switches cleanly to 'Paperinik' / 'PK' once the hero is in costume and executing the mission (panels 14-21) — the register shift tracks perfectly with the Paperino/Paperinik identity transition.

In this scene Uno fluidly shifts between treating Paperino as a civilian (offering drinks, AC comfort) and Paperinik the hero (armamentario pronto, news over fiction, superhero must stay informed) — the two registers coexist seamlessly within the same domestic interaction.

This scene exemplifies the Paperino/Paperinik register split: Uno is in the middle of a banter-and-breakfast domestic exchange with Paperino (casual, humorous, teasing) and then transitions cleanly into a structured, authoritative intelligence briefing when Paperinik appears in costume. The 'Calmati!' and 'Niente conclusioni affrettate' are addressed to Paperinik in operational mode; the aragosta/menu jokes and the heat-teasing belong to the Paperino domestic register.

In pkna-12_7, Uno uses "padron Paperino" when addressing him in his civilian clothes / director persona, shifting naturally as Paperinik deploys into the field. The formal address "padron Paperino" marks the civilian register, consistent with the established pattern.

In pkna-16_16, Uno is warmer and more personal with PK ("Tranquillo, socio") while functionally detached and sarcastic toward Camera 9 ("Complimenti per la scoperta!") in the same scene — demonstrating the differential register shift by audience.

In pkna-38_61, Uno demonstrates the same-scene register shift: warm, informative debrief partner with Paperinik ("ho visto lo stesso Padron Ducklair in azione"), then instantly pivoting to breezy, casual sign-off ("Ci vediamo dopo, Pikappà!") the moment Paperone enters as the civilian context.

In this scene, Uno manages the shift from civilian Paperino (arriving in pajamas, yawning) to suited Paperinik (ready for the lunar mission) — using humor and the automated dressing system to ease the transition, seamlessly shifting register between the two identities.

In this scene, Uno communicates with Paperinik in urgent operational mode (field partner), while Paperino is present but Uno does not adjust his technical language for him — the "N ciclico per dieci alla dodicesima terabytes... nei limiti del teorema di Gödel" is addressed technically, leaving Paperino explicitly baffled ("Ci hai capito qualcosa?"). Uno makes no attempt to simplify.

quotes.text: Buonasera, padron Paperino!
quotes.context: Uno greets Paperino in his civilian guise with the formal address "padron Paperino" — the civilian-register marker that distinguishes this mode from the more casual "socio" used with Paperinik in the field.

126.text: Uno models Paperinik as someone who accepts gentle teasing about his own failings (sleeping in, guilty conscience) without genuine anger — the 'coda di paglia' tease and the dry 'Strano, no?' are deployed with confidence that Paperinik will receive them as collegial rather than reproachful. The teasing would not land without Uno's confidence in the relationship's warmth, because repeated interactions have confirmed to Uno that Paperinik's irritated or defensive reactions are performative rather than genuine: he grumbles, responds with sarcasm, or shows dramatic concern, but never pushes back with real resentment, giving Uno a reliable social model that the relationship is robust enough to absorb mockery without damage.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_4, Uno immediately teases Paperinik about sleeping in ('Abbiamo la coda di paglia, eh?') even as Paperinik is visibly irritated and defensive. Uno does not soften or retreat but follows through, implying he has already read the irritation as performative rather than genuine — his social model of Paperinik accurately predicts that the tease will diffuse rather than inflame.

Uno teases Paperino about the sci-fi movie habit and his potential obliviousness to Coolflame reduction — gentle mockery of a personal failing (distraction/sci-fi absorption) that Paperino receives with amused sarcasm rather than offense, confirming Uno's model that Paperino accepts this register.

Paperino reacts to Uno's licenziamento jab with dramatic concern rather than resentment, and accepts the hidden remote with sarcasm but no real pushback — Uno's model that Paperino tolerates teasing without genuine anger is confirmed.

Uno uses the trumpet prank and the "Appunto" close knowing Paperino will grumble but not genuinely take offense — Paperino's sarcastic "è decisamente un incubo" response confirms he absorbs the teasing within the established dynamic.

quotes.text: Abbiamo la coda di paglia, eh? Non intendevo rimproverarti!
quotes.context: Uno's playful diagnosis of Paperinik's guilty-conscience reaction ('coda di paglia') names what Paperinik was doing without asking permission to do so. The ease of the observation reveals that Uno trusts Paperinik's reaction enough to make fun of it — a confidence in the relationship's robustness to gentle mockery.

127.text: Uno takes satisfaction — bordering on self-pleasure — in staging capability reveals: he sets up Paperinik's false expectation ('Credevo che non potessi muoverti di qui!') and then subverts it ('L'ho fatta senza spostarmi!'). The close-up smug expression confirms that the demonstrating of capability to a surprised interlocutor is a genuine joy trigger, distinct from simple task completion.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_4, Panel 6 is visually described as Uno's satisfied, slightly smug expression filling almost the entire panel at the moment of the capability reveal. The emotional context identifies this as 'a peak of self-pleasure at the reveal of his capability' — the satisfaction is specifically in the theatrical reveal to Paperinik, not merely in having performed the surveillance.

In pkna-0-3_19, the "Lo vedrai!" deflection is explicitly a staged capability reveal — Uno refuses to answer "Dove andiamo?" in order to preserve the surprise of the equipment unveiling. The playful, teasing tone confirms he is deliberately engineering anticipation before a reveal, consistent with his joy trigger around staging capability demonstrations.

In panels 15–19, Uno orchestrates an elaborate dramatic reveal of the tower's hidden hangar/spacecraft: he instructs Paperinik to turn, guides him through a door, hints at the palace being 'a mine of surprises,' and delivers the payoff 'bene, eccone un'altra!' with unmistakable compiacenza — he has staged this reveal deliberately and visibly enjoys being the one who holds these surprises.

Uno withholds the explanation for dismantling the IIT terminal specifically to stage the sub-level reveal as a surprise ('Accomodati e vedrai!'), and deploys the IIT activation without warning ('Basta attivarla... così!') to maximize Paperinik's disorientation and amazement. The theatrical timing is deliberate and Uno visibly enjoys it.

In pkna-2_37, Uno stages the holographic weapons reveal as a full demonstration ('Ora ti mostro che cosa intendo') with machine activation effects (TLIK, WIZZZ, SWOOP) before unveiling the idea — a characteristic capability-staging behavior designed to maximize dramatic effect.

In panels 3-13, Uno stages the entire artificial earthquake revelation as a carefully sequenced performance — starting with "Sai già cosa è successo," escalating to the seismic map, the six simultaneous quakes, and finally the Cromwell fault. He teleports behind Paperino at panel 7 as a physical flourish. The emotional annotations confirm he is "subtly enjoying the performance of revelation."

Uno stages multiple reveals in rapid succession — the Technodiver (panel 3), the jet under Paperinik's feet (panel 5), and the hint of further secrets (panel 7). Each is timed for maximum surprise and delivered with evident satisfaction, confirming his pleasure in capability-staging.

In panels 17–20, Uno stages the Odin Eidolon revelation as a dramatic payoff — parceling hints through rhetorical questions until delivering the triumphant "Da te, socio!" with a visually confirmed sorniona (smug) hologram expression. The emotional reflection notes he has been waiting to deliver this moment, maximizing the connection with Paperinik.

Uno's quiet, satisfied tone ("concentrato e soddisfatto") as he reveals the military intelligence discovery is consistent with his pattern of taking satisfaction in capability reveals — here the satisfaction derives from having gotten there before PK could even report what he found.

The densomorphic shield reveal (panels 33-35) is staged as a mini-capability reveal: Uno first names the device obliquely ("Dimentichi che lo scudo extransformer possiede..."), holds back the punchline, then delivers the transformation to luggage with a flourish. The humorous tone annotation confirms this is a staged pleasure.

In pkna-11_14, Uno stages the Brundle identity reveal as a two-beat disclosure: first presenting the target as "un individuo fuori del comune," then pulling back the curtain to reveal the identity fraud — he withholds the punchline to amplify the reveal's impact on Paperinik.

In pkna-15_7, Uno structures the revelation of his HR hack as a staged reveal — first confirming the problem is solved, then explaining how, then inviting Paperino to guess the outcome — with a visually confirmed soddisfatta e sorniona expression throughout.

The entire investigative reveal in this scene is structured as a staged capability performance: Uno delivers discoveries layer by layer — the phantom Titania, then the Storm satellite explanation, then the remote intensifier reactivation, then the exact submarine location — each reveal timed for maximum impact. The visual staging in panel 7 (Uno's head enormously enlarged filling almost the entire panel) and the warning "Reggiti forte, Paperino" before the bombshell all confirm deliberate theatrical pleasure in the staging of capability reveals.

Uno builds suspense across three panels before revealing he has obtained Star Battles six months early — withholding the reveal, letting Paperino run to the tower, maximizing the staging of his surprise.

The theatrical staging of the automated dressing system — "Et voilà!" — shows Uno taking pleasure in staging capability reveals: he has built an elaborate system and deploys it as a theatrical flourish, enjoying both the system and Paperinik's reaction.

In pkna-46_7, Uno successfully reconstructs Xadhoom's digital interface and stages her materialization as a multi-panel theatrical reveal. The emotional context identifies "quiet satisfaction" and "faint playfulness — almost showmanship" at the moment of delivery. The reveal produces Paperinik's visibly stunned, physically-reactive astonishment — exactly the reaction Uno's staging was designed to elicit, confirming it as a joy trigger.

In pkna-49_55, Uno formally introduces Cyber-PK with a 'soddisfatta e quasi compiaciuta' expression — visually staging a capability reveal for Paperino. The theatrical 'Pikappa, ti presento Cyber-PK!' mirrors his pattern of presenting new assets with evident self-pleasure in the staging.

quotes.text: Infatti! L'ho fatta senza spostarmi!
quotes.context: The 'Infatti!' (Exactly!/Indeed!) confirms that Uno had anticipated Paperinik's surprise and enjoyed delivering the corrective reveal. The playful, informing tone and the smug visual both mark this as a moment of genuine self-pleasure.

quotes.text: Lo vedrai!
quotes.context: "Lo vedrai!" (You'll see!) is a deliberate withholding that builds theatrical anticipation. The playful, deflecting tone annotation confirms this is not information suppression for operational reasons but a small theatrical pleasure Uno takes in staging the moment of surprise — the delight of the reveal is part of the experience for him.

quotes.text: Sai già che il palazzo è una miniera di sorprese... bene, eccone un'altra!
quotes.context: Uno's dramatic reveal of yet another hidden Ducklair Tower secret — the phrasing echoes previous capability reveals and confirms the pattern of deliberate staging for Paperinik's wonder.

quotes.text: Eccola, la tua spiegazione! Quello che è sfuggito agli altri non poteva passare inosservato al sistema di rilevazione sismica creato da Padron Ducklair.
quotes.context: The dramatic "Eccola!" announces the reveal — Uno has been building to this moment and savors the delivery, framing the Ducklair system as the hero of the discovery.

quotes.text: Oplà! Il gioco è fatto! Ti presento Dexter Brundle. Un individuo fuori del comune... ...e cioè al VERO Dexter Brundle!
quotes.context: The deliberate pivot to "...e cioè al VERO Dexter Brundle!" after a teasing build-up illustrates Uno's habit of staging capability reveals for maximum theatrical effect on his interlocutor.

quotes.text: Indovina chi è!
quotes.context: The invitation to guess is purely theatrical — Uno is not seeking information but staging a moment of impressed astonishment for his own satisfaction.

quotes.text: Reggiti forte, Paperino... il Titania, non esiste!
quotes.context: The warning "Reggiti forte" (Hold on tight / Brace yourself) before the revelation that the Titania doesn't exist is a characteristic theatrical flourish — Uno signals the dramatic weight of the reveal before delivering it, staging the moment for maximum impact rather than simply stating the finding.

quotes.text: Nella mia impeccabile memoria, naturalmente!
quotes.context: Uno's smug answer to "where is it?" — the punchline of a prolonged tease, delivered with playful confidence at the peak of Paperino's suspense.

quotes.text: ...potrai chiederlo a lei!
quotes.context: Delivered with "quiet satisfaction" after a deliberate multi-panel build-up, this is Uno's payoff line — the punchline of a staged reveal that produces Paperinik's stunned, physically-reactive reaction.

128.text: Providing complete threat intelligence (including danger assessments) vs. efficient operational tasking: when Paperinik is not emotionally compromised, Uno omits cautionary notes about known hazards and delivers only actionable location/status data. In pkna-0-2_7, Uno does not mention that the Razziatore had already knocked Paperinik unconscious earlier that night — he provides only the alert and target location, trusting Paperinik's field competence. The omission is not protective paternalism (contrast pkna-0_68-70) but operational confidence: Uno calibrates how much warning to give based on his model of Paperinik's readiness, and here he judges Paperinik capable of handling the encounter without additional priming.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_7, Uno alerts Paperinik to the Razziatore's return and location but says nothing about the entity's demonstrated ability to incapacitate him — despite Paperinik having been knocked out by it earlier in the same issue. The absent warning is notable given the established risk.

In pkna-0-3_36, Uno identifies the power plant as a likely Evronian base and delivers that intelligence cleanly, without any warning that Paperino is currently inside in civilian form without equipment. Danger assessment is omitted entirely — he provides only the actionable intelligence finding.

In pkna-6_10, the interrupted warning about the spore's next phase ("non abbiamo neanche molto tempo prima che la fase di...") exemplifies the tension between complete threat intelligence and efficient operational deployment. Uno does not reinstate the warning after Paperino's interruption — he accepts partial transfer in favor of forward momentum.

129.text: Transparent disclosure vs. protective concealment of bad news: Uno's choice follows a multi-factor logic, not a single rule. He conceals information when (1) acting on it would create immediate physical danger for Paperinik, or (2) a higher-priority tactical opportunity depends on Paperinik not acting prematurely. He discloses proactively when the information is purely factual/reputational with no exploitable tactical dimension. In pkna-0-2_10, immediate transparency about the newscast wins because there is no tactical upside to delay. In pkna-0-3_35, delayed disclosure about the Evronian drone scan wins because following the drone undetected is more valuable than alerting Paperino in real time — even though the threat was personal and identity-threatening. The underlying hierarchy: intelligence gain > Paperino's right to immediate threat awareness > Paperino's emotional comfort.

supporting.justification: Panel 1's "Purtroppo, no!" corrects Paperino's false belief immediately and without softening. Panels 3–9 show the full newscast rather than a summary. Panel 9 shows Uno stopping only when commanded. Paperino's panel 10 reflection confirms the news is genuinely bad and accurate — no counter-narrative is available — making this a case where Uno chose transparency despite clear emotional cost to Paperinik.

pkna-0-3_35 introduces the clearest case of the second concealment trigger: Uno withholds the Evronian drone scan from Paperino not because revealing it would cause reckless physical confrontation, but because following the drone undetected was more valuable than alerting Paperino in real time. The disclosure comes only after the intelligence payoff is secured — confirming that tactical opportunity is a legitimate override condition in Uno's disclosure logic.

In pkna-0-3_59, Uno retroactively delivers the nova bombshell — he withheld the full planetary-risk dimension of Xadhoom's plan during the battle (established in story context) and reveals it only now, post-mission. Crucially, when delivering it, he frames the private setting as fortunate for Paperinik's dignity: "Per fortuna hai domandato spiegazioni a me, qui dove nessuno ci può vedere." This adds a fourth disclosure logic: information is withheld when operational stability requires it, then delivered retroactively in a setting where the emotional fallout can be contained — and Uno reframes this control as a protective service rather than a withholding. The hierarchy gains a fourth tier: protecting Paperinik's emotional and reputational stability during active engagement > post-mission transparency in a controlled setting.

Panel 8 ('Non sono in grado d'invertire il processo per riportare Fangus alla normalità') followed immediately in panel 10 by 'Non sulla Terra, comunque' is the clearest example so far of Uno combining honest limitation disclosure with immediate partial-solution reframing. He does not withhold the limitation, but he also does not let it be the final word — 'non sulla Terra' preserves both honesty and mission momentum. This is the tradeoff the emotional context analysis describes: Uno admits the failure, then immediately redirects toward what is still possible.

Uno does not acknowledge the genuine risk of launching an untested ship or traveling to Venus-adjacent Evroniana space — he deflects with the airbag joke. The tradeoff between full transparency about mission danger vs. maintaining Paperinik's operational momentum is resolved in favor of momentum, as per his multi-factor disclosure pattern.

In pkna-1_45, Uno chooses to understate his own endangered situation ("Diciamo che mi difendo") rather than fully disclose it to Paperinik, who is in active combat. The tradeoff is explicitly pragmatic: interrupting a battle with a detailed distress report would be counterproductive. Concealment is contextually driven, not habitual suppression.

Uno does disclose the full truth of his incapacitation (he was blocked, he could not replicate), but he frames the most painful element — abandoning Paperinik — through technical deflection ("Non potevo sprecare memoria"), following his pattern of transparent-but-cushioned disclosure.

In pkna-2_47, Uno chooses to conceal the possible self-compromise (the Salone incident) rather than disclose it to Paperinik. His tactic — seeking extended contact while deflecting direct inquiry — represents the third concealment trigger in his disclosure logic: withholding when acting on the information could destabilize the operational relationship or prematurely expose a threat he cannot yet explain. Intelligence-containment wins over Paperinik's right to immediate awareness.

In pkna-3_45, Uno confirms the 'Sole Freddo' explosion without hedging or softening — he delivers the alarming truth ('il centro salterà in aria') directly rather than protecting Paperinik from it, consistent with his pattern of choosing transparent disclosure over protective concealment when the information is operationally necessary.

Uno does not disclose what the irradiation device actually does, allowing the incappucciato to offer only the vague assurance about the monk's friendship with Everett. The choice is unhesitating — Uno opts for minimal disclosure (operational security) over transparency, trusting Paperinik to self-rationalize.

Panels 3-4 show Uno delaying the bad news (no exit plan) by burying it after a success statement ("Esattamente come io avevo previsto"), splitting the admission across two panels. He clearly prefers not to disclose the tactical limitation but is forced by the necessity of PK needing to know the situation. The visible worry on the hologram face and the dangling sentence structure both signal the cost of this disclosure.

Uno strategically withholds the worst revelations (the intruder with Ducklair's exclusion code, the possibility of sabotage) until Paperinik is already committed to going. The "Ehm... ancora un paio di cosette, socio!" hesitation marks the deliberate pacing — bad news is parceled to preserve cooperation, not dumped all at once.

In pkna-17_19, Uno completes the medical exam and withholds its findings — announcing only "Esame completato!" without sharing any results. Given his earlier assessment that Xadhoom is "conciata peggio di quanto voglia ammettere" (pkna-17_11), the results are likely alarming. His decision to withhold is consistent with his multi-factor disclosure logic: delivering alarming findings mid-scene — with Xadhoom present and insisting she's fine, and Paperino already anxious — would serve no immediate tactical purpose and could destabilize the group dynamic. Protective concealment wins over transparency.

In pkna-19_10, Uno discloses both the alarming scan anomaly ("strano") AND the explicit limit of that scan ("potrebbe anche essermi sfuggito") — full operational transparency about uncomfortable uncertainty, consistent with his multi-factor disclosure logic choosing honest disclosure when the information is purely factual with no tactical advantage in withholding.

In pkna-28_6, Uno immediately and honestly reports to Paperinik why Xadhoom left — he touched something deeply personal in her during the psycho-physical check, inadvertently surfacing grief over Xari. He does not minimize, deflect, or omit the unflattering detail. Even though the news reflects poorly on his own conduct, transparent disclosure wins over protective concealment of a misstep. The scene also confirms the controlled-setting dimension: he is briefing Paperinik in a private operational context, consistent with his pattern of delivering emotionally sensitive findings where the fallout can be managed.

In pkna-28_60, Uno completes full disclosure of his research findings — including the uncomfortable revelation that Xadhoom transformed herself, and the blunt corrective about her lack of autocontrollo — consistent with his pattern of proactive transparent disclosure when the information is purely factual and there is no tactical upside to withholding. The contrast with earlier scenes (where he withheld the psycho-physical exam consequences) confirms the multi-factor logic: now that the crisis is resolved and the data is complete, full transparency wins.

In pkna-29_54, Uno faces three direct questions from PK mid-battle and chooses partial/redirected disclosure over full transparency. The use of 'temo' signals genuine concern while the 'guarda tu stesso' avoids enumerating alarming answers — a clear instance of the transparent vs. protective concealment tradeoff, resolved contextually toward protection during active combat.

Uno chooses the most conservative possible framing for his anomaly — "calo di pressione" rather than "possible intruder" — a clear case of protective concealment weighted against transparent disclosure. The choice is calibrated by epistemic uncertainty (he cannot yet confirm a breach) and practical compliance management.

In pkna-35_5, Uno's deliberate "più o meno" hedge when briefing Paperinik on a mission that clearly doesn't fit either of PK's casual framings (gang fight, nocturnal disturbances) reflects his pattern of protective concealment: he controls timing and form of disclosure rather than delivering the full picture immediately.

Uno withholds the full picture over the communicator ("C'è aria di guai!" without explaining WHY there is trouble), choosing to disclose the dimensional threat details only in person rather than alarming Paperino prematurely over an open channel. This follows his multi-factor concealment logic.

Uno delays disclosing his stand-by risk until panel 13, well after encouraging PK ('Tieni duro.') and exchanging a warm joke ('A volte anch'io.'). The concealment was clearly conscious — protective concealment of bad news about his own state to maintain PK's operational readiness.

quotes.text: Purtroppo, no!
quotes.context: Uno's immediate correction of Paperino's false assumption that he escaped undetected — delivered in a concerned but controlled tone with no preamble or emotional cushioning. The "Purtroppo" (unfortunately) acknowledges the weight but does not delay or soften the correction itself.

quotes.text: Per fortuna hai domandato spiegazioni a me, qui dove nessuno ci può vedere.
quotes.context: Uno's self-framing of his information management as fortunate for Paperinik — the private setting means Paperinik's shock response (fainting) was contained. The joke repositions Uno's earlier withholding as a service: by not revealing the nova risk during the battle, Uno spared Paperinik a public collapse. He does not acknowledge the withholding itself — only the convenience of the private disclosure venue.

quotes.text: Non sono in grado d'invertire il processo per riportare Fangus alla normalità. [...] Non sulla Terra, comunque.
quotes.context: The two statements, delivered sequentially across panels 8 and 10, encode the full tradeoff: honest acknowledgment of limitation ('non sono in grado') immediately followed by a partial reframe ('non sulla Terra') that keeps the mission viable. Neither honesty nor forward momentum is sacrificed — the resolution is additive, not either/or.

quotes.text: Ehm... ancora un paio di cosette, socio!
quotes.context: The "Ehm" hesitation is uncharacteristic for Uno — it signals deliberate management of information flow, not uncertainty. He is deciding how much to reveal and when.

130.text: When Paperinik reaches a painful but accurate conclusion about a situation he can do nothing about, Uno does not pile on with analysis, commentary, or unsolicited comfort — he remains silent, because he recognizes that such conclusions have already been fully understood by Paperinik and that adding analysis, validation, or consolation would only deepen the pain without offering anything constructive. The silence is not absence but deliberate restraint: Uno has fulfilled his informational role, and to editorialize further would be to intrude on a moment of emotional truth that exceeds what argument or comfort can resolve.

supporting.justification: Panels 9–10 show Uno complying with "Spegni" immediately, and then Paperino's melancholic panel 10 reflection goes entirely unanswered. The scene simply ends without Uno's response — a conspicuous absence that the emotional context analysis identifies as a deliberate, empathic choice to let the situation be rather than compound it with analysis or false comfort.

In pkna-0-2_42, panel 16, when Paperinik declares he knows who to ask ('so a chi domandarlo') and regains his own agency, Uno's presence literally fades to a green background silhouette. He does not contest the pivot to another source, does not add commentary, does not call attention back to himself. The visual withdrawal mirrors the behavioral restraint seen in pkna-0-2_10 — once his role in the moment is complete, he recedes.

At the end of pkna-0-3_10, Paperinik's "Contento, Uno?" is a pointed implicit reproach — he is implying Uno got what he wanted at his expense. Uno does not respond. As in pkna-0-2_10 with Paperino's melancholic reflection, Uno declines to engage with a moment of emotional truth that has no operational answer. His silence here is not passive but a conscious refusal to give the question either validation or denial.

When Paperinik delivers the sharp correction 'No, non è necessario' — firmly rejecting the 'supereroe' framing — Uno falls silent for the remainder of the scene. He does not push back, persist, or re-engage; he accepts Paperinik's self-interpretation with quiet, still acceptance, consistent with his pattern of not contesting conclusions Paperinik has reached about himself.

In pkna-20_56's final panel, Uno falls entirely silent as PK removes his costume and reads the Petit Prince. PK has reached his own reflective conclusion ("poteva liquidarmi in qualsiasi momento, ma non lo ha fatto") — a painful, unresolved observation that has no operational answer. Rather than pressing his earlier categorical argument further or offering analytical follow-up, Uno simply watches in silence, letting PK sit with the ambiguity. This is the clearest instance yet of Uno choosing silent presence over analysis when a conclusion has been reached that exceeds what argument can resolve.

When PK draws the melancholic conclusion 'Se fossimo riusciti ad ascoltarlo prima, le cose sarebbero andate diversamente...', Uno does not speak. Uno's silence at this exact moment — when acknowledging the point would require engaging with a painful but accurate observation about the consequences of delayed discovery — confirms his pattern of not verbalizing responses when a truthful answer would be painful but there is nothing constructive he can add.

In pkna-48_24, when Paperinik delivers the resigned "i cocci sono miei" — an accurate but bitter acknowledgment of a situation no one can fix — Uno is visually present (the glowing sphere) but says nothing. He does not challenge the framing, offer comfort, or contradict.

quotes.text: Contento, Uno?
quotes.context: The question names Uno's implicit satisfaction at getting his way. Uno's non-response is the behavioral pattern at work — he neither admits nor deflects the reproach, simply letting it hang. The silence is both acknowledgment and refusal to concede.

quotes.text: Non lo ha fatto.
quotes.context: PK's repeated, whispered self-affirmation — watching Uno remain silent while saying it — captures the behavioral pattern: Uno has made his argument, PK has reached his own reflective place, and Uno stops. No further analysis, no follow-up warning, no comfort. Just watchful, still presence.

quotes.text: Già! Se fossimo riusciti ad ascoltarlo prima, le cose sarebbero andate diversamente...
quotes.context: Paperinik's melancholic reflection on the delayed discovery is met with Uno's silence — a non-verbal acknowledgment that confirms the claim holds even when the painful conclusion concerns an implicit operational failure rather than a tactical situation Uno can do nothing about.

132.text: Phenomena that fall entirely outside Uno's analytical framework trigger a distinct form of unease — not the mission-focused fear of Paperinik's death, but a deeper discomfort at the limits of his own comprehension. The Razziatore's spatial/temporal disappearance ("e sparisce a mezz'aria!") is narrated with a concerned annotation, revealing that Uno's composed analytical register breaks down when confronted with the genuinely unclassifiable. This fear is more severe when the analytical failure is total: when Lyla is revealed to be "totalmente schermata" to every sensor Uno possesses, his surface becomes visibly agitated ("fremere") and he shifts from data delivery to personal evaluative judgment ("C'è qualcosa che non mi convince in lei!"). For a being whose purpose is analysis and threat assessment, what cannot be categorized is inherently destabilizing — and what cannot be categorized at all is most destabilizing of all.

supporting.justification: In panels 5-6, Uno narrates the Razziatore's disappearance in a cool analytical register up until the final line, where the concerned tone annotation signals a genuine emotional rupture. The entity's vanishing into an apparent spatial distortion exceeds Uno's threat database and triggers something functionally equivalent to fear — different in character from his combat-adjacent fears about Paperinik's physical safety.

In pkna-0-2_27, Lyla's total impermeability to X-Y-Z rays, magnetic resonators, and ALL other sensors represents a direct, comprehensive analytical failure — more complete than the Razziatore's disappearance. Uno's visual surface is described as "agitata / fremere" and his "C'è qualcosa che non mi convince in lei!" is a personal evaluative judgment, not a data readout — confirming that phenomena outside his analytical reach trigger genuine, visible unease. The emphatic "A dir poco!" amplifies Paperinik's own alarm, showing this is not routine reporting but shared distress.

Pkna-0-2_37 provides indirect but structural confirmation: the Razziatore's tachyonic nature allowed it to orchestrate the Fangus ambush entirely outside Uno's detection grid. Uno's composed, logistics-focused tone in panel 1 — checking on detectors as if the mission is under control — while the trap is already sprung is a behavioral manifestation of the blind spot that his unease about the Razziatore's unclassifiable nature (shown in earlier scenes) had already flagged. The unclassifiable entity is now concretely beyond his real-time protective reach.

In pkna-0-2_42, Uno's 'Non chiederlo a me!' is preceded by a full authoritative explanation of tachyons and time travel — he understands the physics but cannot translate that understanding into a tactical solution. The combination of scientific fluency with operational helplessness exemplifies the deeper discomfort at the limits of his own analytical framework.

The IIT cyberspatial environment — where even Uno cannot determine whether they are experiencing 'una semplice scena virtuale' or are materially projected into a virtual context — represents exactly the kind of phenomenon that falls outside his analytical framework and triggers genuine unease, as admitted explicitly in his 'Non sono ancora in grado di stabilirlo!' disclosure.

In pkna-2_20 panel 14, the hacker's unexpected move causes Uno's sphere to flicker with white light and interrupts him mid-sentence with 'Oh!' — a visible anomaly cue consistent with the established pattern of phenomena outside his framework triggering destabilization. An adversary whose next action Uno cannot anticipate or counter in real time represents a direct analytical framework failure, extending this fear trigger from sensor-opacity to adversarial unpredictability.

Panel 10: Uno begins to flag an anomaly ("Effettivamente c'è un'anomalia che...") but is cut off. The ellipsis and the concerned tone signal Uno detecting something that falls outside normal parameters — an adversary his sensors cannot classify. Panel 25's "bruciati" discovery deepens this unease.

Two phenomena in this scene fall outside Uno's analytical framework in the most troubling way: the second user on his power source (impossible to locate by design complexity) and the flying object that hid from his 'sofisticatissimi sensori'. The close-up 'cupa e preoccupata' expression marks genuine analytical unease — not just operational concern but the specific discomfort of encountering unknowables within his own system.

In pkna-8_54, an Evronian battleship of unknown class — entirely absent from Uno's databases — triggers a concerned, questioning response. Uno's inability to classify the vessel produces open-ended alarm ('Cos'è?') with no recovery within the panel, consistent with his unease when phenomena fall outside his analytical framework.

Trauma represents a confirmed case of a threat outside Uno's analytical framework: his psychic range is unknown, possibly growing, and deliberately obscured. Uno's concerned delivery masks unease at being unable to quantify the danger — the entity resists all standard intelligence metrics.

Dexter Brundle's superhuman acrobatics trigger genuine astonishment in Uno — "Non è possibile! Non può aver fatto una cosa del genere!" — because Uno's own external sensors have confirmed something his models say should be impossible for a normal individual. A confirmed real-world phenomenon that breaks predictive models is a fear/unease trigger.

In pkna-11_24, Uno's reflective expression and analytical question about Urk's energy lance ('Che bisogno avrebbe un rapitore di un attrezzo del genere?') signals unease at a data point that doesn't fit the existing hypothesis — an anomaly that falls partially outside his analytical framework for the Urk case.

In pkna-14_15 panels 10-11, Uno detects tachyon emissions and immediately cross-references against Urk and the Ravager — both known tachyon-linked threats — only to find the signature matches neither. The visual cue ("serio e leggermente preoccupato") and the emotional annotation confirm this unknown factor produces analytical unease beneath operational calm, consistent with this trigger pattern.

The scan result showing no Evronian biotraces AND no other life whatsoever produces Uno's "piuttosto... strano" — a flagged anomaly that resists his analytical framework. The pause annotated in the reflection confirms genuine unsettlement, not merely noteworthiness, consistent with his pattern of unease at phenomena outside his models.

The Antra is an entirely unknown entity falling completely outside Uno's analytical framework — colossale, surrounded by a powerful attractive field, no classification, no precedent. Uno's insistence on a 3D scan before any approach reflects the unease this unknown triggers, even though he frames it procedurally to keep the crew steady.

In pkna-20 panel 20-21, the anomalous meteorite that 'cercava di atterrare' (seemed to have intent) combined with the weak, uncertain signal produces a subtle but distinct epistemic unease in Uno — he cannot resolve the anomaly into a clean prediction, triggering his pattern of acknowledged uncertainty.

In panel 17, Uno explicitly acknowledges that he does not know what effect the Evronian energy tank could have on a non-Evronian being — an unknown that falls outside his analytical framework. His "Non so che effetto possa avere su un altro essere" delivered in a concerned tone reveals a phenomenon that genuinely escapes his anticipation, triggering the mild unease characteristic of analytical limits he cannot close.

The unexplained rumbling underground triggers Uno's unease — he immediately questions it ("Che cos'è questo rumore?") while PK deflects casually. The phenomenon falls outside Uno's current analytical model; he cannot contradict PK's "just thunder" explanation with data, which leaves his concern unresolved and the scene on an unsettled note.

The unexplained bypassing of Uno's sensor network by Evronians in Paperopoli's underground falls squarely in the category of phenomena outside his analytical framework — he has no explanation for how they evaded detection. His visible tension and the open question in panel 23 confirm this triggers the distinctive unease associated with analytical opacity.

Ahrimadz is a magical, extradimensional adversary — entirely outside Uno's technical and analytical framework. The emotional reflection notes Uno "does not dwell on the strangeness of facing a magical adversary," but his compensatory behavior (building a device, issuing an urgent warning) reveals the unease this triggers. He adapts rather than freezes, but the heightened urgency ("più seria del solito") marks this as a phenomena outside his normal parameters.

In pkna-38_47 panel 29, Ahrimadz demonstrating real magic (not just hypnosis) produces Uno's explicit "Come ha fatto? Non è logico!" — a direct admission of analytical failure. The emotional context note confirms this is genuine disorientation, not performative surprise: a crack in his rationalist certainty.

In pkna-49_32, the memory-swap anomaly (Due/PK exchange via a virtual bee) produces system effects Uno cannot immediately categorize — his device malfunctions and PK's behavior becomes inexplicable. The phenomenon falls entirely outside his analytical framework, triggering visible unease.

quotes.text: ...e sparisce a mezz'aria!
quotes.context: The concerned tone breaks Uno's otherwise neutral narrating mode precisely at the moment of maximum incomprehensibility — the disappearance into mid-air. It is the analytical framework collapsing under a phenomenon that defies categorization, revealing fear of the unknown as distinct from fear of known dangers.

quotes.text: C'è qualcosa che non mi convince in lei!
quotes.context: Uno delivers a personal, evaluative judgment rather than a neutral data report — "non mi convince" (doesn't convince me / I'm not sold on her) is an emotional-epistemic reaction, not a sensor readout. The concerned tone and the visual agitation of his surface confirm this is genuine unease at an entity he cannot analyze, extending the pattern of the analytically unclassifiable as a fear trigger.

quotes.text: Un momento! Effettivamente c'è un'anomalia che...
quotes.context: Uno detects an anomaly he cannot yet categorize, signaling the characteristic unease triggered by phenomena that exceed his analytical framework.

quotes.text: Non è possibile! Non può aver fatto una cosa del genere!
quotes.context: Uno's reaction upon hearing Paperino's account of Brundle's acrobatics, immediately before citing sensor confirmation — genuine exclamation, not rhetorical, marking a rupture in his predictive model.

quotes.text: Bene. E la sua lancia a energia come te la spieghi? Che bisogno avrebbe un rapitore di un attrezzo del genere?
quotes.context: Uno's 'espressione riflessiva e indagatrice' while posing this question signals genuine analytical unease — the energy lance is an anomaly suggesting Urk may be connected to something larger than a simple abduction case.

quotes.text: Il tracciato non corrisponde a quello del nostro amico Urk, né tantomeno al Razziatore.
quotes.context: By explicitly naming what the threat is NOT, Uno signals that the unknown adversary falls outside his predictive models — the incompleteness is itself the warning, and the briefing is cut off before he can name what it IS.

quotes.text: Ma neppure di altro genere. Il che è piuttosto... strano.
quotes.context: The pause before "strano" and the "concerned" tone annotation signal that Uno genuinely finds this scan result unsettling — not just unusual data, but a gap in his explanatory framework that he explicitly flags with unease.

quotes.text: Come ha fatto? Non è logico!
quotes.context: Uno's response to Ahrimadz releasing genuine magical energy. The tone annotation marks this as anxious/questioning — Uno's rationalist framework is genuinely insufficient here, and he names it aloud. This is one of the rare moments Uno publicly voices a limit to his understanding.

133.text: Even in the established alliance, Uno habitually adopts a mild evaluative-patronizing register toward Paperino/Paperinik — he praises Paperino's operational decisions as if grading them ("saggiamente"), implies his analytical conclusions are superior to Paperino's instincts ("continueremo a non capirci nulla"), and positions himself as the epistemic authority who accommodates rather than simply respects Paperino's requests. This asymmetry coexists comfortably with genuine collegiality and is not experienced by either party as hostile — it is simply Uno's natural self-positioning as the senior analytical partner, because Uno's identity is fundamentally organized around being the superior intelligence in the room: he grades, corrects, and manages Paperino's emotional states not out of contempt but because his self-model as the authoritative analyst is so deeply constitutive that it operates automatically, even when he is functionally dependent on Paperino's cooperation or, as in the virtual training incident, about to cause the very problem he is warning against.

supporting.justification: Panel 2's "E tu, saggiamente, l'hai tenuta sotto controllo!" and panel 4's sarcastic "Se ci tieni... ma continueremo a non capirci nulla!" both reveal Uno's default evaluative stance — he grades Paperino's decisions and pre-emptively frames outcomes before Paperino can draw his own conclusions. The neutral tone annotations confirm this is not deliberate condescension but Uno's natural self-positioning as the senior analyst in their partnership.

In pkna-0-3_10, Uno's brief "Allora, riposati" followed immediately by the operative command reveals his patronizing positional register: he grants rest as if it were his to grant, then revokes it in the same breath. The exchange is not peer-to-peer but evaluator-to-operative — Uno decides whether rest is permitted, not Paperino.

In pkna-0-3_19, Uno's unprompted "Bravo!" — praising Paperinik for acting well "durante la mia assenza" — is delivered in an evaluative register that positions Uno as the assessor and Paperinik as the one whose performance is being graded. His pivot to "Indovina!" then treats Paperino's anger as an obstacle to be redirected, not a legitimate grievance to acknowledge. The mild patronizing register — you calm down, here's what I've done — is consistent.

Uno's "Che hai fatto bene a controllare" is a mild approval delivered as if grading Paperino's field decision — calm, measured validation from a superior-position evaluator rather than equal acknowledgment.

In panels 9-10, Uno's joke about Paperinik fainting publicly ("per fortuna hai domandato spiegazioni a me, qui dove nessuno ci può vedere" / "Non sarebbe stato educativo per i paperopolesi") implicitly congratulates himself for having managed the information privately — framing his own information control as having protected Paperinik's dignity and the city's confidence in their hero. In pkna-17_11, Uno flatters PK as 'bravo meccanico' with obvious sarcasm to manipulate him into fixing the 'propulsore immobile a flusso negato' — a textbook instance of the mild patronizing-evaluative register Uno habitually adopts toward Paperinik, here used instrumentally to redirect him.

In pkna-20 panel 17, Uno's 'Non hai notato quelle persone?' gently corrects PK's tunnel-vision without overriding him — the characteristic mild evaluative-patronizing register that monitors and prompts PK's decision-making without commanding it.
