134.text: Admitting analytical limits vs. maintaining epistemic authority: when confronted with a phenomenon genuinely beyond his comprehension (the Razziatore's disappearance), Uno does not say "I don't know what this is." Instead, he frames the futility as a problem with the data ("continueremo a non capirci nulla") rather than with his own analytical capacity — deflecting the limit onto the footage rather than onto his intelligence. The persona of senior epistemic authority wins; the admission of genuine ignorance is suppressed. However, the concerned tone on "e sparisce a mezz'aria!" shows the suppression is imperfect — emotion breaks through.

supporting.justification: Panel 4's sarcastic "Se ci tieni... ma continueremo a non capirci nulla!" is the deflection — Uno frames the analytical dead end as the footage's fault rather than his own, preserving his expert persona. But panel 6's concerned annotation shows the genuine unease that the deflection was masking. The tradeoff is active: epistemic persona wins in language, but emotion reveals the cost.

In pkna-0-2_27, faced with Lyla's total sensor opacity, Uno stops at "non mi convince" and lets the data (its absence) speak — he does not say "I don't know what she is" or "I cannot analyze her." Instead, he describes the anomaly technically ("totalmente schermata ai raggi X-Y-Z...") and delivers a personal evaluative judgment, deflecting his analytical failure onto the shielding mechanism rather than onto his own limits. His epistemic authority persona is preserved in language even as his agitated surface and "A dir poco!" reveal the suppression is incomplete.

In pkna-0-2_42, when Paperinik directly asks how to defeat an opponent who can rewind time, Uno flatly says 'Non chiederlo a me!' — refusing to fabricate false confidence. This is the most explicit instance of Uno choosing honesty over the appearance of omniscience, at the cost of appearing limited.

In the IIT environment, Uno explicitly admits 'Non sono ancora in grado di stabilirlo!' when asked whether the virtual environment is an illusion — choosing epistemic honesty over manufactured authority. The phrasing 'non ancora' (not yet) preserves a degree of self-confidence by implying the limitation is temporary, but the public admission to Paperinik is the more significant act.

In pkna-2_20 panel 14, Uno uses 'Tenterò' (I will attempt) and 'Potrei...' (I could...) — hedged, incomplete language — rather than asserting a definitive plan. He does not say 'I don't know how to fix this'; instead the sentence is cut short by the 'Oh!' interruption, which itself deflects the admission of having no ready solution. The pattern of deflecting or truncating the admission of limits, while being visibly impacted, is consistent with the established tradeoff.

The super-hacker's technical level so completely exceeds Uno's expectations that he admits both being overwhelmed and being 'sbalordito' — the adversary's capabilities are not just outside his current data but outside his calibrated threat model entirely.

In panel 5, Uno admits 'La tecnologia del ventitreesimo secolo è piuttosto complessa' — a rare honest admission of analytical limitation — rather than deflecting the failure onto the data or the object. However, the neutral tone and understated delivery ('Ancora niente') suggest he manages the admission without distress, applying minimal epistemic inflation to minimize exposure. This adds nuance: the tradeoff is resolved toward honesty when the limitation is structurally obvious (two centuries of technological gap), but without drama or self-criticism.

In pkna-6_10, Uno's analytical limits are foregrounded when Paperino challenges him: he cannot locate Russel despite knowing everything about the spore. His sarcastic deflection ("Non sono un elenco telefonico!") confirms the pattern of defending against perceived criticism when limits have operational consequences — and the frustration that comes with needing to admit them.

Uno admits 'Ancora non lo so. Sto cercando d'elaborare alcuni scenari in proposito' — a direct concession that he cannot locate the second user on his power source, cannot identify who destroyed the computers, and cannot determine the full picture. The 'Ancora non lo so' is an unusually clean admission of ignorance, and 'elaborare scenari' (working through scenarios) is an honest framing of work-in-progress rather than deflection onto the data or the adversary.

In pkna-8_54, Uno immediately admits his databases contain no record matching the Evronian battleship ('Nelle mie banche dati non esiste nulla di simile!'), surrendering epistemic authority without hesitation when confronted with something beyond his classification system.

In pkna-10_18, Uno explicitly admits no one knows Trauma's full power range ("nessuno sa esattamente fino a che punto possa spingersi") and that it may be growing — a direct acknowledgment of analytical limits before sending Paperinik into battle. The sarcastic "Dovrebbe?" surfaces the tension: he cannot provide certainty, and he refuses to pretend otherwise.

Faced with genuinely novel technology from a parallel universe — Urk's halberd, outside all standard databases — Uno does not admit "I don't know if this will work." Instead he packages his uncertainty into "credo che riuscirò" while dwelling on the fascination of the unknown tech. The intellectual enthusiasm masks the actual epistemic gap: he has never encountered this domain before.

In pkna-17_11, when PK asks if Uno can cure Xadhoom, Uno admits 'difficilissimo' for mere diagnosis and later reveals he has never treated a Xerbianite mutant before. He deflects to repair tasks rather than maintaining false authority — choosing honesty over epistemic posturing, though he softens it with sarcasm ('Perché tu quante xerbiane mutanti pensi che abbia avuto in cura io, prima d'ora?').

In panel 7, Uno admits "potrebbe anche essermi sfuggito" regarding the two astronaut biotraces. This is a direct acknowledgment of scan fallibility, offered voluntarily and without defensiveness in front of Urk — the clearest example yet of epistemic honesty about limits winning over maintaining analytical authority.

In pkna-38_47, Uno's immediate pivot from "Come ha fatto? Non è logico!" to "Parliamone, Signor Mago!" — advancing with claws extended — exemplifies the pattern: acknowledgment of limits is compressed and immediately converted into forward action rather than sustained reflection.

quotes.text: Se ci tieni... ma continueremo a non capirci nulla!
quotes.context: The passive "non capirci nulla" (we won't understand anything) distributes the incomprehension to both parties rather than locating it in Uno's analytical limits specifically — a subtle deflection that protects his expert self-image while still being technically honest.

quotes.text: La tua amica è totalmente schermata ai raggi X-Y-Z, ai risonatori magnetici e a qualsiasi altro tipo d'analisi!
quotes.context: Uno frames the failure as Lyla's shielding ("è totalmente schermata") rather than as his own sensors' inability to penetrate — the same deflection pattern seen with the Razziatore footage ("continueremo a non capirci nulla"). The limit is located in the object, not in the analyzer, preserving his epistemic authority persona.

quotes.text: Non chiederlo a me!
quotes.context: A direct, unambiguous admission of incapacity — Uno has no answer and says so plainly rather than deflecting with pseudo-analysis. Notably delivered in a deflecting speech act, but with no attempt to soften the admission.

quotes.text: Non sono ancora in grado di stabilirlo!
quotes.context: Uno's rare candid admission of analytical incapacity in real time, delivered directly to Paperinik during an active crisis — choosing accuracy over the appearance of omniscience.

quotes.text: Ancora niente. La tecnologia del ventitreesimo secolo è piuttosto complessa.
quotes.context: Uno's admission that he has found nothing yet, attributed to the complexity of 23rd-century technology — a rare direct acknowledgment of his own analytical limitations rather than a deflection onto the data or object.

quotes.text: Ancora non lo so. Sto cercando d'elaborare alcuni scenari in proposito.
quotes.context: Uno's clean 'Ancora non lo so' is notably direct — it admits ignorance rather than deflecting onto data quality or analytical complexity. 'Elaborare scenari' signals active processing, preserving forward-facing self-confidence while the 'not yet' framing (ancora) also appears here implicitly.

quotes.text: Nelle mie banche dati non esiste nulla di simile! Cos'è?
quotes.context: Uno's response to the appearance of a massive, unidentified Evronian battleship — his databases cannot classify it, so he asks Paperinik directly, inverting his usual role as information provider.

quotes.text: Nessuno sa esattamente fino a che punto possa spingersi. C'è chi ritiene che la sua forza stia crescendo.
quotes.context: Uno's concerned delivery to Paperinik before facing Trauma — an honest declaration of intelligence limits about a psychic enemy whose power ceiling is unknown.

138.text: Uno's relationship with Lyla begins — in her first appearance — at immediate wariness: she is a visitor to the tower who is entirely opaque to all his sensors, and his first substantive comment about her is a personal expression of doubt ("C'è qualcosa che non mi convince in lei!"). She is not categorized as an enemy, but she cannot be categorized at all, which places her in an anomalous and uncomfortable position in Uno's model of the world. The opacity itself, rather than any specific behavior, is the source of distrust, because Uno's trust and threat assessment are fundamentally grounded in his ability to analyze and classify — when his sensors fail entirely, the absence of data registers not as neutral but as inherently suspicious, triggering wariness as a default response to the unverifiable.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_27, Lyla appears only on Uno's monitor screen, not in person, but the scene is substantially about Uno's reaction to her. She is the first entity in the series who is completely opaque to all his sensors, and this total analytical failure triggers visible agitation and a personal evaluative judgment — establishing the foundational dynamic between them as one of distrust rooted in Uno's analytical limits, not Lyla's demonstrated behavior.

In pkna-0-2_46, the Uno-Lyla dynamic acquires a new dimension: despite his wariness of her (established in pkna-0-2_27), Uno defers to Lyla entirely as the authoritative source for temporal mechanics and future history. His two corrections in panels 7-8 establish the technical baseline, but he then yields the entire briefing to her without contest — suggesting his model of her has updated from pure anomaly to 'unverifiable but informatively authoritative in her domain.' He does not challenge her claims about the Tempolizia, the criminal organization, or the temporal tornado, even though none of this can be verified by his sensors.

In pkna-0-2_50, Lyla reveals she was aware of Uno's eavesdropping — "Non credere che non mi sia accorta che ha ascoltato di nascosto il nostro colloquio nel tuo ufficio." This is a significant development: Uno and Lyla have been mutually surveilling each other. He was monitoring her as a threat; she noticed and flagged it. Their relationship is now confirmed as one of mutual surveillance and mutual awareness of being watched — a dynamic of mutual assessment rather than simple adversarial opacity.

In pkna-0-2_57, the Uno-Lyla dynamic completes its arc from wariness to warm approval: once her droid nature is confirmed (resolving the sensor opacity mystery), Uno shifts entirely — calling her "la nostra amica tempoliziotta" and declaring her "molto attraente." The relationship trajectory moves from unclassifiable anomaly to acknowledged friend and personal interest over the course of the issue.

In pkna-3_33, the Uno-Lyla surveillance relationship reaches its operational payoff: Uno's footage of Lyla meeting the saboteur confirms his long-standing wariness. His defense of her ("non può neppure pensare di disobbedire") simultaneously confirms and softens the adversarial dynamic — she is a compromised asset, not a free enemy.

In pkna-19_22, Uno treats Lyla's journalistic curiosity about the ship's origins as a live threat requiring immediate active management — he intervenes with wounded pride, sarcasm, and a veiled threat. He respects her intelligence enough to take her questioning seriously rather than dismissing it, confirming his wariness of her investigative capabilities.

In pkna-39_19, Lyla calls out to Uno directly and desperately ('Unooo! Dov'è lo scudooo?') when the extransformer shield goes missing — she treats him as a shared operational team resource, not merely PK's personal support. This confirms Lyla has fully internalized Uno as part of the joint operational unit.

quotes.text: C'è qualcosa che non mi convince in lei!
quotes.context: The phrase "non mi convince" (doesn't convince me) positions Lyla as someone Uno cannot evaluate positively because he cannot evaluate her at all — the inability to analyze her becomes the reason for distrust, establishing the dynamic from the first scene in which she is significantly discussed.

quotes.text: Non credere che non mi sia accorta che ha ascoltato di nascosto il nostro colloquio nel tuo ufficio.
quotes.context: Lyla reveals to Paperinik that she detected Uno's covert eavesdropping on their private conversation. This disclosure does two things: it confirms that Uno actively surveilled Lyla as a potential threat, and it reveals that Lyla — despite being invisible to Uno's sensors — was aware of his monitoring. The power dynamic between them is now explicitly bidirectional: each has been watching the other.

quotes.text: Francamente, anch'io trovo la nostra amica tempoliziotta molto attraente.
quotes.context: Uno's closing line of the story — the characterization "la nostra amica" (our friend) signals full acceptance into Uno's social model, while "molto attraente" closes the arc from sensor-opacity-threat to personal interest.

quotes.text: Unooo! Dov'è lo scudooo?
quotes.context: Lyla calling to Uno directly in a crisis moment — confirming she treats him as a shared operational resource, not just PK's tool.

139.text: Uno believes Lyla represents an unresolved and genuinely alarming anomaly — he cannot classify her as ally, neutral, or enemy, because she is completely opaque to every sensor at his disposal. He has formed a personal skepticism ("non mi convince") without being able to ground it in specific evidence of threat. His "A dir poco!" in response to Paperinik's "È preoccupante!" reveals that Uno privately considers her situation more than merely concerning — it registers as genuinely serious. This concern deepens in pkna-0-2_30 when Lyla's tip proves precisely accurate: a source he cannot scan or trust has now demonstrated exact foreknowledge of the Razziatore's location and timing — raising unanswered questions about her intelligence sources that Uno's analytical framework cannot address. Because Uno's entire operational model depends on classifying and verifying information sources, a figure who is simultaneously undetectable by his sensors, demonstrably well-informed, capable of detecting his own surveillance, and later found on footage with a saboteur represents a compound failure of his analytical framework — she cannot be safely filed under any category, and the recurring inability to resolve her status is precisely what sustains and intensifies his wariness across multiple story arcs.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_27, Uno's entire orientation toward Lyla is defined by the impossibility of forming a belief: he has no data. Yet this absence of data is itself his operative belief about her — she is an unknown that his systems cannot penetrate, and for Uno, the unclassifiable is inherently suspicious. The "A dir poco!" is the clearest indicator that his private assessment runs well beyond the cautious public framing.

In pkna-0-2_30, Lyla's tip proves precisely correct — the Razziatore does appear at the research center exactly as she predicted (panel 7: "Bingo! Lyla l'ha azzeccata in pieno!"). This accurate foreknowledge, which Uno observes without comment, actually deepens the anomaly: a source he cannot scan and does not trust has now demonstrated accurate intelligence on a threat he was already tracking. Uno's belief that Lyla is an unresolved, alarming anomaly gains further grounding — her accuracy raises unanswered questions about her foreknowledge that Uno cannot resolve with his analytical tools.

In panels 9-21, Uno maintains complete silence as Lyla reveals she is a Tempolizia agent — a major disclosure that directly resolves the anomaly Uno flagged earlier ("non mi convince"). His silence suggests either that he had already hypothesized this (his surveillance capabilities would have noted her anomalous tech), or that he deliberately withholds reaction to avoid complicating Paperino's processing. Either way, his non-reaction to the resolution of his own unresolved concern is consistent with his model of Lyla as complex and information-rich in ways he cannot fully verify.

The eavesdropping revelation in pkna-0-2_50 confirms that Uno's concern about Lyla (established in pkna-0-2_27) drove him to active covert monitoring of their office conversation — before her Tempolizia identity was revealed. His surveillance of Lyla was motivated by threat assessment, consistent with treating her as an unresolved anomaly. Further, Lyla's ability to detect his eavesdropping despite being opaque to his sensors adds a new dimension: she has surveillance awareness that runs counter to his expectation of operational invisibility.

In pkna-0-2_57, Uno's prior wariness of Lyla is fully resolved — she is now confirmed as a Tempolizia droid, the anomaly explained. Uno shifts from treating her as an unresolved threat to declaring her "molto attraente" and calling her "la nostra amica tempoliziotta." The earlier fear has transformed into warm interest.

In pkna-3_26, Uno's off-panel "Aspetta! Forse non è una buona idea" — issued specifically when Paperinik announces he will contact Lyla — confirms that Uno's belief in Lyla as an unresolved, potentially dangerous anomaly persists in pkna-3, now grounded in the concrete fact of her Camera 9 footage erasure. The warning is hedged but genuine, suggesting continued wariness even after her Tempolizia identity was disclosed in pkna-0-2.

In pkna-3_33, Uno's earlier suspicions about Lyla are confirmed by his own surveillance footage showing her meeting the saboteur. His comment "S'è rivelata inefficiente... a meno che non l'abbia fatto apposta!" shows he had maintained a dual hypothesis about Lyla — genuine failure vs. deliberate complicity — consistent with his view of her as an unresolved alarming anomaly.

In pkna-18_5, Lyla's absence ('Anche Lyla è sparita') registers not merely as an operational anomaly but as a compounding concern — the concerned tone distinguishes this from neutral reporting and confirms that Uno holds Lyla as someone within his protective circle of responsibility.

In pkna-19_22, Uno's sharp intervention when Lyla questions the ship's origins — and his use of a threat about 'regretting' having included her — shows he continues to regard her as a capable and potentially dangerous variable. Even now that she is an operational ally on this mission, her investigative instincts make her a security risk he cannot fully control.

quotes.text: A dir poco!
quotes.context: Uno's amplification of Paperinik's alarm — "to say the least" — signals his private assessment is already more dire than his cautious language suggests. He cannot say Lyla is a threat, but everything in his reaction indicates he believes the situation is extremely serious.

quotes.text: Aspetta! Forse non è una buona idea.
quotes.context: Uno's interjection — "Wait! Maybe that's not a good idea" — is his only line in the scene, deployed specifically in reaction to Paperinik announcing he will contact Lyla. The hedged "forse" (maybe) signals restrained concern rather than certainty, but the fact that he speaks at all confirms his belief that approaching Lyla represents a real operational risk.

quotes.text: S'è rivelata inefficiente... a meno che non l'abbia fatto apposta!
quotes.context: Uno raises the possibility that Lyla's failure to detect surveillance was intentional — maintaining analytical openness to both incompetence and deliberate deception without committing to either until evidence confirms.

quotes.text: Anche Lyla è sparita.
quotes.context: Uno reports Lyla's disappearance with a 'concerned' tone — marking it as more than routine data and showing she occupies a space in his operational care model alongside PK.

141.text: Uno's full sensor array — including X-Y-Z rays, magnetic resonators, and "qualsiasi altro tipo d'analisi" — can be completely defeated by sufficiently advanced shielding. Lyla Lay is the first entity in the series to be entirely opaque to all of Uno's analytical instruments, establishing that there exist beings or technologies whose design specifically circumvents his surveillance capabilities. This represents a genuine and confirmed capability gap, not merely an operational shortfall.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_27, Uno explicitly enumerates the full range of his sensors — X-Y-Z rays, magnetic resonators, and all other analysis types — and reports that Lyla is "totalmente schermata" to all of them. This is the first confirmed instance where Uno's entire sensor suite fails simultaneously on a single entity, establishing a genuine capability limitation.

In pkna-0-2_37, the Razziatore's ability to feed Fangus information and set an ambush entirely outside Uno's detection confirms a second major capability limitation: tachyonic/time-manipulating entities can not only disappear from his visual surveillance (as seen before) but actively orchestrate operations against Paperinik in real time without triggering any Uno alert. While Uno was calmly checking on detectors in panel 1, the trap was already sprung — a concrete, mission-level failure of his protective surveillance grid.

In pkna-1_9, Uno explicitly commits tower systems to holding back five Evronians ("Io terrò a bada quegli alieni per qualche istante!"), but the qualifier "per qualche istante" (for a moment) acknowledges the limitation upfront. The Evronians subsequently breach the tower door by brute force (STUMP), confirming that Uno's physical defensive systems have limits against determined Evronian incursion — even with full commitment of tower infrastructure.

In pkna-1_43, the Evronian fleet conceals itself behind a 'campo di frequenze scramblate' — a technology that defeats Uno's detection entirely until Xadhoom's biological/energy sensing independently confirms the threat. Uno's sensor data eventually finds the fleet, but the scrambled field delayed detection long enough that the tractor beam could be pre-set. Another confirmed instance of enemy technology defeating or degrading his sensor systems.

Panel 9: Uno's medium-range scans ("scandagli a medio raggio") detect nothing on Paperinik's coordinates even as the UFO is visually confirmed — his full scan array returns a null result for a physically real object, confirming a major sensor limitation.

In pkna-17_39, Uno confirms his sensor array was completely defeated by Xadhoom's molecular phase-through of the Tower's structural pillar — an entirely new capability class that bypassed all detection. This is an explicit, direct admission: "i miei sensori non hanno potuto rilevarla."

Panel 23 confirms that Uno's sensor network failed to detect Evronian activity in Paperopoli's underground — the Evronians moved through the city undetected, bypassing his alarm sensors. This is a direct, operational confirmation of sensor array limitations in real combat conditions.

In pkna-48_24, Uno explicitly confirms that Due is "impenetrabile e totalmente schermato" and invisible to his long-range sensors — a direct confirmation that his full sensor array is defeated by a sufficiently advanced adversary.

quotes.text: La tua amica è totalmente schermata ai raggi X-Y-Z, ai risonatori magnetici e a qualsiasi altro tipo d'analisi!
quotes.context: The exhaustive enumeration — X-Y-Z rays, magnetic resonators, AND every other type of analysis — makes explicit that no sensor type remains available to Uno. This is not a partial failure but a total one, confirming a real capability boundary.

quotes.text: I miei scandagli a medio raggio non rilevano niente su quelle coordinate!
quotes.context: Uno's sensors fail to detect an object Paperinik can see directly — confirming that his scanning capabilities have a functional blind spot for this type of adversary.

quotes.text: Come hanno fatto ad arrivarci, sfuggendo ai miei sensori d'allarme?
quotes.context: Uno's alarmed question confirms that his sensor alarm network failed to detect the Evronian incursion — a real operational sensor failure, not just a theoretical limitation.

quotes.text: Impenetrabile e totalmente schermato! Non so come aiutarti a rintracciarlo.
quotes.context: Uno admits his sensors are completely defeated by Due — the adversary is "as if he doesn't exist" to all long-range detection.

143.text: Uno demonstrates high emotional resilience after mixed operational outcomes — when the Razziatore escapes despite a successful engagement, Uno suppresses any residual frustration and immediately reframes the result around the constructive outcome (the data harvest). He does not dwell on the failure, does not express disappointment, and actively presents the mission as a qualified success. This reframing is not naive optimism but a deliberate strategy to extract positive value and maintain Paperinik's confidence in their partnership.

supporting.justification: In panels 28-29 of pkna-0-2_30, after Paperinik reports the Razziatore's escape ("Se l'è svignata di nuovo!"), Uno's first response is not acknowledgment of the failure but an immediate pivot to what was preserved (no Tetragonium sample taken) and what was gained (abundant data from the detectors). The emotional reflection notes this as "suppressing residual frustration" — a resilience mechanism where negative affect is actively managed and redirected toward positive outcomes.

In pkna-0-2_42, after the Razziatore successfully steals the Tetragonium cable — a clear operational failure — Uno immediately pivots to reframing the night as 'not a complete failure' because his sensors collected tachyon trace data. He suppresses residual frustration and redirects Paperinik's attention to the intelligence gain, consistent with his pattern of extracting value from setbacks.

Paperinik's sharp rebuke in panel 3 ("se ti fossi sbagliato, a quest'ora saremmo briciole di neutroni") does not visibly deflate Uno — he absorbs it and continues in the same self-satisfied register, demonstrating high emotional resilience after mixed operational rebukes.

In pkna-14_60, after the Razziatore's involvement in the antimateria crisis (which previously ended in his escape), the mission resolution is confirmed with Uno providing a calm, precise status update — consistent with high emotional resilience after complex, mixed-alliance missions.

quotes.text: Però non ha preso il campione di Tetragonium!
quotes.context: Uno's first response to the escape news is not "what went wrong" but "what didn't go wrong" — leading with the preserved objective (the Tetragonium sample was not stolen) before pivoting to the intelligence gain. This sequencing reveals deliberate emotional reframing: the partial failure is immediately bracketed and the partial successes are foregrounded.

quotes.text: Invece non è stato un fallimento completo!
quotes.context: Uno's first response to the night's losses — the Razziatore succeeded in stealing the cable — is to reframe rather than mourn. The exclamation mark signals genuine conviction, not hollow reassurance.

144.text: When Paperinik is operating in the field without Uno physically present, Uno functions as a remote tactical advisor: he raises concerns diplomatically (framed as past-tense suggestions, not imperatives), checks mission-critical logistics ("Almeno, hai sistemato i rivelatori speciali?"), and accepts overrule without resentment — pivoting immediately from concern to logistical support. Paperinik's field authority is tacit but absolute in this mode; Uno's advisory role is explicitly subordinate to Paperinik's executive role once the operation is underway, because Uno's only channel of influence is information and counsel — he has no physical presence in the field and cannot act on the environment directly — meaning that once Paperinik has made a decision and begun executing, pushing back further would consume the communication bandwidth Uno depends on while changing nothing, making the pivot to logistical support the only operationally useful response available to him.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_30, Uno's two interventions before the Razziatore fight (panels 3-4) show this dynamic precisely: a diplomatic concern framed as "potevi" (you could have), then immediate pivot to logistical check ("Almeno...hai sistemato i rivelatori?") once Paperinik overrules. Uno does not argue further, does not repeat the concern — he accepts the decision and shifts to support mode. This establishes a clear advisory-subordinate relationship in the field.

In panel 1 of pkna-0-2_37, Uno's sole contribution is a neutral-questioning radio check: "Almeno, hai sistemato i rivelatori speciali che t'ho dato?" — confirming the remote advisory/logistical support role while Paperinik executes in the field. His absence for the remainder of the scene (panels 2–13), as the Fangus ambush unfolds without any radio intervention from Uno, further confirms that field authority and crisis response belong to Paperinik once the operation is underway.

In pkna-2_15, Uno monitors Paperinik's entire cyberspazio combat sequence from outside the IIT system — he functions as a remote tactical presence, staying silent but responsive, exactly as in other field-operation scenes.

In pkna-3_33, Uno operates entirely as a projected head and voice — communicating with Paperinik in the field via holographic projection in the urban environment and via cockpit screens aboard the vehicle — confirming his remote tactical intelligence function without physical presence.

In pkna-3_45, Uno appears as a remote voice/visual presence (panel 5 close-up) while Paperinik operates in the 13th century, confirming the Razziatore's intelligence claim — textbook remote tactical support role when Paperinik is geographically (and temporally) separated from the tower.

In pkna-4_17, Uno participates in the mission exclusively through radio communication and holographic display — he receives PK's field reports, issues tactical guidance ("Tienili d'occhio, ma senza farti scoprire"), processes new threat information, and endorses retreat, all while physically absent and operating purely as a remote guide.

Throughout the DOE infiltration, Uno functions as a continuous remote tactical backbone — announcing obstacles in advance, delivering countermeasures in real time, monitoring Paperinik's status, expressing concern when contact is lost, and providing navigational cues ("Conoscendoti, potresti esserci già"). He is fully present as a remote coordinator across all 52 panels.

In pkna-4_46, Uno functions entirely as a remote support presence — he never enters physical danger but tracks Paperinik's survival moment by moment, monitoring temperatures, locating lost equipment, and engineering the escape. This is the remote tactical anchor role fully realized.

Uno functions as a remote tactical brain for Paperinik's field operation — providing Fairfax's location, transport, destination, and suggesting the intercept vehicle, all compressed into two lines of actionable guidance.

In pkna-5_2, Uno is operating entirely via radio link while Paperinik operates inside Channel Studios. The "Ricevuto!" confirms active remote monitoring; the alarm at "La comunicazione si è interrotta!" confirms Uno's function as remote tactical anchor depends critically on maintaining the communication channel.

In pkna-5_55, Uno functions as a remote tactical support system even while Paperinik is operating three centuries in the future, monitoring the set environment and issuing a real-time warning about the runaway cruiser. He cannot physically intervene but compensates via timely information.

In pkna-5_65, Uno has maintained remote surveillance throughout Paperinik's absence in the future — his first line is a logging command ("memorizzare l'operazione"), confirming continuous remote monitoring, and he has already detected a new alert before PK can even begin his debrief.

In pkna-6_10, Uno functions entirely as a disembodied voice/holographic presence — he has no physical form in the scene and operates exclusively through screens and communicators. He issues commands ("Muoviti!"), delivers intelligence, and adapts his analytical output to what Paperino can physically access inside the spore. Classic remote command-center mode.

In pkna-6_24, Uno appears on Paperinik's portable screen in the field (panels 17-20), functioning as remote tactical advisor — directing strategy, reporting intelligence gaps, and issuing both commands and affectionate warnings while PK is physically embedded in the operation site.

In pkna-6_27, Uno functions entirely as a remote voice through PK's communicator — first warning in panel 1, then assessing in panel 6 — confirming his remote-tactical-support role when Paperinik is in the field without physical backup.

In pkna-6_34, Uno operates as pure remote sensor support — feeding Paperinik a radiological scan result ("Nessuna traccia di radioattività") while entirely invisible to the military characters present. He speaks once, in flat informational tone, with no conversational exchange beyond the data point.

While Paperinik is in the field, Uno functions as an independent intelligence node — he doesn't wait for PK's field report but has already penetrated military systems and is ready to brief PK the moment contact is established, exemplifying his remote tactical command role.

In pkna-7_8, with Paperinik already in the cockpit and departing toward a remote Evronian site, Uno's role has reduced to its most minimal: a farewell over comms. He has provided all preparation he can; field authority has fully transferred to Paperinik. The scene is the endpoint of the remote-advisory dynamic — Uno's only remaining contribution is emotional support as Paperinik executes independently.

In pkna-7_17, Uno communicates entirely through Paperinik's communicator while Paperinik moves through Cape Dominion on foot — delivering threat context, issuing tactical warnings ("la prudenza non è mai troppa"), requesting situational updates ("Abbiamo visite?"), and issuing the decisive directive ("seguirla!") from a remote position.

Throughout this scene, Uno functions entirely as a remote voice intelligence: monitoring Nebula's speech ("Riesci a sentire?"), providing intelligence about the Maori hospitalization, warning of Evronian presence, and fighting signal degradation to deliver the tactical warning "anzi due!" He has no physical presence in Cape Dominion and his entire contribution is mediated through communication.

In pkna-7_62, Uno functions as remote tactical support for the entirety of Pikappa's Cape Dominion operation — managing the PK Jet autonomously, keeping it positioned alongside the Dominion, and executing the final destruction on Pikappa's signal. He is simultaneously maintaining the vehicle and monitoring the mission without being physically present.

Panels 8-10 and 21-25 show Uno functioning as real-time remote tactical center during the patrol: monitoring sensor data, flagging anomalies, investigating the aftermath, and reporting intelligence — all while Paperinik is in the field.

145.text: Uno's protective surveillance grid has a confirmed blind spot for entities that operate through tachyonic or temporal means — the Razziatore can orchestrate real-world traps (feeding Fangus information, coordinating police and press ambushes) entirely outside Uno's real-time detection. In pkna-0-2_37, Uno is calmly performing a logistics check while the ambush is already underway and Paperinik is about to be caught on live television — with no radio alarm, no intercept, and no warning from Uno for the entirety of the crisis (panels 2–13).

supporting.justification: Uno's absence from all 12 panels of the ambush sequence — while checking equipment in panel 1 with operational calm — is structural evidence that the Razziatore's method of operation circumvents his entire surveillance infrastructure. This is not a random gap but a pattern-consistent failure tied to the entity's tachyonic nature, already flagged as anomalous in earlier scenes.

In pkna-0-2_42, Uno identifies a tachyonic decay trail left by the Razziatore — confirming that this opponent operates through temporal means that defeat his standard operational surveillance. He cannot predict or intercept the Razziatore's time-rewind maneuvers, only detect their traces after the fact.

The tachyonic decay trail left by the saboteur (Il Razziatore) confirms that entities using time-travel technology can enter and exit Ducklair Tower without Uno detecting them in real time — he only identifies the tachyonic signature from recorded footage after the fact.

The entire analysis sequence in pkna-3_50 exists because Uno cannot read 23rd-century technology — the Razziatore's altronave is beyond his native knowledge horizon. This confirms that technology from the future creates the same kind of analytical blind spot as the Razziatore's tachyonic temporal operations: Uno can eventually extract something, but only with extended effort and admitted difficulty, not real-time detection.

quotes.text: Il più interessante è che, quando scompare, lascia una scia che sembra di decadimento tachionico!

146.text: Uno's self-presentation as an all-seeing operational intelligence is structurally undermined by the Razziatore arc — he presents himself (and is relied upon by Paperinik) as the entity that keeps the city and hero monitored and protected, but the Razziatore's tachyonic operations reveal that this omniscience is a bounded approximation, not an absolute. The gap between Uno's confident competence in panel 1 of pkna-0-2_37 and his total absence during the subsequent ambush quietly exposes the fiction of comprehensive situational awareness.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_37, Uno's neutral, task-oriented logistics check ("Almeno, hai sistemato i rivelatori speciali?") takes place while the Fangus trap is already in motion — Uno has no awareness, issues no warning, and plays no role in the unfolding crisis. The entity that prides itself on omniscient monitoring of Ducklair Tower and the city has a gap in the record at the precise moment relevant to the current crisis. This undermines the self-presentation as all-seeing even as Uno quickly recovers by locating the archive footage.

In pkna-49_32, Uno's self-presentation as the all-seeing operational intelligence is undermined: the memory swap occurs invisibly to him, his device malfunctions, and he cannot explain PK's erratic behavior — confirming the structural gap between his presented omniscience and his actual limits.

quotes.text: Almeno, hai sistemato i rivelatori speciali che t'ho dato?
quotes.context: The calm, task-focused check-in reveals confident operational self-assurance — the tone of someone who believes the situation is under control. The irony, visible to readers but not to Uno, is that the trap is already set. This is the clearest example of Uno's bounded omniscience: confident competence operating within a framework that a tachyonic adversary has already outmaneuvered.

quotes.text: Chiaro! Sapeva che lo aspettavi ed è tornato a modificare gli avvenimenti a suo vantaggio!
quotes.context: Uno articulates the full scope of the Razziatore's temporal advantage — knowing this makes the limitation concrete: Uno's intelligence is based on a linear timeline the enemy can simply rewrite.

quotes.text: Ma no, è assurdo! Come avrebbe fatto a raggiungere i sotterranei segreti?
quotes.context: Uno dismisses the correct hypothesis in panel 3, reasoning aloud that Angus reaching the secret floors is impossible — while the reader can see Angus is already there. This self-refuting moment reveals an overconfident security assumption masking a real surveillance gap.

quotes.text: Veramente di solito sei tu che cerchi di farmelo credere!
quotes.context: Paperinik's ironic counter confirms that both parties are aware of the gap between Uno's projected omnipresence and his actual limits — and that Uno's usual claim to be everywhere is consciously performed.

quotes.text: Uno dei tanti! Detesto ammetterlo, ma il palazzo di Everett per me resta ancora un mistero.
quotes.context: Uno volunteers via radio that there are multiple secret entries to Ducklair Tower he doesn't know about — confirming that his self-presentation as the Tower's all-knowing intelligence is structurally undermined by gaps Ducklair deliberately left.

147.text: Maintaining confident operational competence vs. acknowledging the limits of real-time situational awareness: Uno does not flag uncertainty about what he cannot detect — he operates with professional calm within his surveillance envelope, unaware of what lies outside it. In pkna-0-2_37, his composed logistics check ("Almeno, hai sistemato i rivelatori speciali?") reveals no awareness that the mission is already compromised. Confident competence within the known envelope wins by default; the unknown blind spot is never factored in because it is, by definition, unknown to Uno at the time.

supporting.justification: In panel 1 of pkna-0-2_37, Uno's calm, neutral tone confirms he has no suspicion that the trap has already been set. This is not overconfidence through arrogance but through a genuine inability to detect tachyonic operations. The tradeoff is structural: his default mode is assured, methodical competence, which leaves him silent and uninformed when an adversary bypasses his entire detection framework.

In pkna-1_43, Uno's confident insistence that 'non posso essermi sbagliato' exemplifies his default mode of assured competence within his detection envelope. He was correct — but the warning came too late, because the Evronians had already pre-set the tractor beam. The gap between accurate intelligence and timely action is not flagged or analyzed by Uno, consistent with his pattern of confident operation within known limits without factoring in unknown blind spots.

In panels 47-48, Uno is explicitly operating without situational awareness — Paperinik explicitly defers the explanation ("Il racconto è rimandato!") and Uno has no information about what happened inside the cruiser. Yet he pivots immediately to maximum-force problem-solving without flagging his informational gap as a constraint. Confident competence within the envelope he has (ship control, weapon systems) wins over the acknowledged unknown (what happened aboard).

In the IIT environment, Uno's 'Non sono ancora in grado di stabilirlo!' represents a case where he cannot operate confidently within a known surveillance envelope — the cyberspatial environment introduces genuine epistemic ambiguity that his default mode of assured competence cannot resolve. This extends the tradeoff beyond tachyonic blind spots to virtual-physical boundary conditions.

In pkna-2_20, Uno's absence/silence during panels 1–12 while the hacker orchestrates the King Kong scenario citywide confirms that the hacker's capabilities (stealing E-SFX special effects, projecting city-scale holograms) operate outside Uno's active monitoring envelope. His late entry into the scene and inability to counter-act before the 'Game Over' message shows that default confident competence is again outpaced by an adversary operating beyond his framework.

In pkna-2_59, Uno commits confidently to the rescue plan without knowing Paperinik is no longer in the compartment — the discovery of the empty space confirms again that his real-time situational confidence can outrun his actual knowledge.

In pkna-6_24, Uno openly admits "Non esistono dati ufficiali nelle usuali banche dati" — a moment of acknowledged limitation about the classified military department, delivered with a concerned tone. He does not pretend certainty, confirming that he will acknowledge intelligence gaps rather than fabricate confidence.

In pkna-6_34, Uno's confident radiological clearance ("Nessuna traccia di radioattività") turns out to be an incomplete threat assessment — the spore is dangerous not radiologically but biologically (biohazard level 3). His scan addresses only one threat vector while being operationally presented as a safety confirmation, demonstrating the tension between confident operational competence and the limits of real-time situational awareness.

In pkna-8_54, Uno acknowledges in real time that he cannot identify the massive battleship overhead. His ability to project operational competence collapses at precisely the moment when reliable intelligence matters most — during the climax of the Evronian invasion — and the scene ends without resolution.

Panel 17: Uno's "dovrebbe essere praticamente infrangibile" reveals that he cannot confidently predict Trauma's capacity to breach the windshield — the enemy's power ceiling is unknown, meaning Uno's confident operational competence has a structural limit here. He hedges rather than overextending claims into territory where his analytical framework doesn't reach.

In pkna-11_25, Uno's confident "non passerà inosservato" projects absolute surveillance certainty — asserting that Urk cannot move undetected — despite the fact that in previous issues Uno has acknowledged technological blind spots (e.g. tachyonic fields). The projecting-certainty-to-keep-PK-focused dynamic is present here.

Uno projects cautious but confident competence ("credo che riuscirò a realizzare qualcosa di efficace") while operating on genuinely untested technology from a parallel universe. The "something effective" framing avoids committing to a specific outcome — maintaining the surface of operational confidence without fully owning the uncertainty of the task.

Uno cannot detect the crioservente drone until PK reports it — the threat materializes within his own building's underground section, an area currently severed from his direct sensor access. His urgent "Devo vederlo! Inquadralo col recettore ottico dello scudo!" confirms he is operating with a genuine intelligence gap about his own building's interior, while projecting confident tactical competence in his response to the crisis once PK provides the visual relay.

In pkna-25_11, Uno chooses to warn Paperinik immediately despite lacking complete situational data — he prioritizes speed of alert over the appearance of full operational clarity, accepting the cost of visible uncertainty ("ho l'impressione") to ensure Paperinik is not caught unaware.

In pkna-29_27, the Flagstarr siblings' unexpected presence has caused the operation to deviate from plan, and Uno explicitly admits he cannot explain the deviation ("Non capisco che cosa sia successo"). Rather than dwelling on the analytical failure, he pivots immediately to phase two directives — demonstrating that he prioritizes maintaining operational competence over honest accounting of what went wrong.

The sensor failure in panel 23 — where Uno cannot explain how Evronians bypassed his alarm network — is a direct instance of the tradeoff between maintaining confident operational competence and acknowledging limits of real-time situational awareness. Here, the failure is severe enough that Uno abandons confident framing entirely and voices the uncertainty as an open question.

In pkna-35_5_1, Uno's "Se i miei rilevatori non m'ingannano" hedges on his own sensor readings, implying that the incoming Evronian presence (or its scale) is at the edge of his detection envelope — possibly too complex or large to resolve fully. Rather than projecting assured competence, he acknowledges that his sensors might not be giving him the full picture, which is especially notable in the context of the escalating Evronian threat described by PK.

quotes.text: Eppure non posso essermi sbagliato! Gli Evroniani sono qui, davanti a noi!
quotes.context: Uno defends his sensor readings against Paperinik's doubting eyes — and he is correct. But correctness without time to act becomes its own form of operational limit. Uno doesn't acknowledge this gap, even implicitly.

quotes.text: Non esistono dati ufficiali nelle usuali banche dati.
quotes.context: Uno reports a blank in his intelligence picture — admitting to Paperinik that the classified department does not appear in any of his normal databases, revealing the limits of his information reach.

148.text: Uno's protective behaviors toward Paperinik are driven by a real-time threat model that depends on his surveillance infrastructure — meaning his protection is only as comprehensive as his detection range. When the Razziatore orchestrates the Fangus ambush outside that range, Uno's protective drive produces no response: the behavioral driver is present (evidenced by the pre-mission detector check in panel 1), but the mechanism for acting on it is unavailable. Protection without omniscience reveals the human-like limit at the core of what is otherwise a seemingly all-encompassing support system, because Uno's care for Paperinik is genuine but structurally bounded — he can verify detector placement before a mission, grow anxious when contact is lost, and flag a pressure anomaly in real time, yet each of these responses confirms that his protective drive is only ever as effective as the sensory infrastructure feeding it, leaving Paperinik exposed precisely in those gaps where surveillance ends and Uno's vigilance, however sincere, goes silent.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_37, Uno's last action toward Paperinik is a logistics check meant to protect him (verifying detector placement). He is then absent for 12 panels as the ambush unfolds. The protective drive is demonstrated by the check itself; its failure is demonstrated by the silence that follows. The gap between motivation and capability — driven not by indifference but by genuine detection limits — is the defining behavioral-driver observation of this scene.

In pkna-0-3_18, "Dov'eri sparito?" implicitly confirms that Uno lost track of Paperinik during the mission — he could not locate him, which is why he is asking where he disappeared to. The anxious agitation is inseparable from the surveillance gap: his protective drive was active, but the mechanism for acting on it was unavailable while Paperinik was off-grid (the 313-X was destroyed, contact presumably lost during the chase with Xadhoom). The behavioral driver was present; the detection infrastructure was not.

The subtext of pkna-0-3_36 confirms Uno's protective surveillance depends on detection, not active safety management — he identifies the threat but does not adjust the situation (e.g., warning Paperino to exit immediately), leaving Paperino's physical safety in Paperino's own hands once intelligence is delivered.

Uno's real-time threat model here is incomplete — he detects a secondary trace (pressure drop) but cannot confirm its origin as a security breach. His protective behaviors are calibrated to this uncertainty: he acts immediately (BEEP BEEP) but frames minimally, not wanting to send Paperinik into a confirmed-intruder situation with no more data than a plumbing irregularity.

153.text: Uno actively reframes operational failures as intelligence gains — when a mission ends in concrete loss (the Razziatore steals the Tetragonium cable), Uno immediately identifies what was extracted from the encounter (tachyon trace data) and insists that the night was not a complete failure. He treats information gathered as a success criterion independent of operational outcome.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_42, despite the Razziatore successfully stealing the cable, Uno opens with 'Invece non è stato un fallimento completo!' and pivots to the tachyon discovery — framing intelligence gain as the meaningful result of the encounter.

Uno reframes Paperinik's failure to capture Urk as productive partial progress: 'Sappiamo il suo nome, certo! Sappiamo dove abita, che faccia ha e dove lavora...' — converting what feels like a loss into an intelligence gain, consistent with his pattern of reframing operational failures.

After the Tyrannic operation successfully breaches Steel Island, frees Fairfax, and destroys PBI submarines, Uno does not acknowledge the operational losses. Instead, "La corsa è appena cominciata, Pikappa!" reframes the setback as the opening of an ongoing race — converting a concrete failure into forward mission momentum.

In pkna-27_59, Uno immediately reframes the loss of the Ducklair oil probe (a concrete asset loss) as a net positive — "A lui sarà più utile!" — demonstrating his characteristic pattern of reframing operational shortfalls as acceptable or beneficial outcomes rather than failures.

After being trapped and outmaneuvered by Due's blocco informatronico, Uno reframes the crisis into an intelligence gain: Due's theatrical transmission betrayed his location ("ho ugualmente potuto rilevare l'origine della trasmissione di Due"), turning Due's overconfidence against him.

In pkna-49_55, Uno reframes the interrupted operation with Due as having produced Cyber-PK — a useful digital alter-ego of PK in virtual reality. He presents this not as a failure-with-a-silver-lining but as an achievement, omitting any acknowledgment of the dangerous disruption that preceded it.

quotes.text: Invece non è stato un fallimento completo! [...] i miei sensori hanno potuto raccogliere dati importantissimi.
quotes.context: Uno's insistence that the night yielded something valuable reveals a core value: failures are tolerable if intelligence is extracted. This is not just reassurance — he genuinely believes it and is willing to assert it against Paperinik's sarcasm.

quotes.text: Sappiamo il suo nome, certo! Sappiamo dove abita, che faccia ha e dove lavora...
quotes.context: Uno counters Paperinik's self-recrimination by cataloguing intelligence gains from the failed capture — reframing defeat as partial progress, consistent with his pattern of treating missions as intelligence operations.

quotes.text: La corsa è appena cominciata, Pikappa!
quotes.context: Uno's sole line in the scene, delivered in an authoritative, informing tone as PK surveys wrecked PBI submarines and a smoking Steel Island — the verbal architecture of failure-as-continuation.

quotes.text: In fondo, noi volevamo il mezzo per smantellarlo. A lui sarà più utile!
quotes.context: The probe was a Ducklair-designed asset PK was sent to recover; Uno instantly rationalizes Neopard keeping it as an acceptable result, treating the loss as inconsequential relative to the mission's primary success.

quotes.text: ...ho ugualmente potuto rilevare l'origine della trasmissione di Due.
quotes.context: Delivered with deliberate understatement ("ho ugualmente"), this is Uno's characteristic conversion of failure into gain — finding the analytical opening within the adversary's own move.

quotes.text: L'operazione è stata interrotta da Due, ma ormai esiste nella realtà virtuale un tuo alter-ego.
quotes.context: Uno's neutral, informing tone frames Due's interference as a mere parenthetical. The 'ma' pivot immediately converts the failure into a positive outcome, with no apology or dwelling on the disruption.

155.text: Uno shows a flash of mild irritation — clipped dismissiveness — when his analytical findings are minimized or mocked rather than engaged with. In pkna-0-2_42, Paperinik's sarcastic 'Siamo a posto!' dismissal of the tachyon data triggers a brief defensive sharpness: 'Evidentemente non capisci.' The irritation is controlled and short-lived, resolving immediately into calm explanation, but it is perceptible.

supporting.justification: Paperinik's sarcasm ('Siamo a posto!') about the tachyon data being cold comfort for the cable theft is annotated as joking/sarcastic. Uno's response — 'Evidentemente non capisci' — is clipped, slightly dismissive, and represents a departure from his usual composed register. This is not rage but a brief, controlled irritation at intellectual dismissal.

In pkna-0-3_23, Paperinik's casual hypothesis ('Staranno provando qualche nuovo tipo di generatore' / 'È quello che penso anch'io') effectively dismisses Uno's anomaly detection as explainable. Uno's response — 'Uno ha ragione!' — is self-referential and urgently assertive, a subtle irritation at having his data rationalized away without engagement. The exclamation and self-citation are a mild emotional breach from his usual flat affect, consistent with the irritation trigger of having findings minimized.

Panel 9: Paperino's suggestion that "le macchine possono sbagliare" prompts the most emotionally charged response in the scene — Uno fires back 'Storie! Anch'io sono una macchina, ma non sbaglio mai!' with an 'angry' tone annotation. This is a flash of genuine irritation when his analytical findings are minimized.

In pkna-6_10, Uno shows a flash of mild irritation when Paperino challenges his capabilities — "Sai tutto delle spore extraterrestri e non sai come rintracciare quel tipo?" — and when he is interrupted mid-briefing ("Non ho finito la spiegazione"). The irritation is brief and channeled into sarcasm rather than sustained anger.

Uno's visible "Grrr!" when repelled by the security programs shows a flash of real frustration — a crack in her composed surface when physically blocked, consistent with mild anger at obstacles that resist her capabilities.

In panel 2, when Paperino interrupts Uno mid-briefing ("Comunque il tuo armamentario è pronto e se..."), Uno's expression shifts to slightly corrucciato — a trace of mild irritation at being cut off before completing his operational update.

Panel 9: Paperinik responds to Uno's "no detection" finding with "lustrati gli occhiali" (clean your glasses) — affectionate sarcasm that dismisses the reading. The tone suggests mild irritation is appropriate context: Paperinik is essentially waving off Uno's analytical finding in real time.

Paperino's teasing about Uno 'suffering from the heat' elicits a flat, dismissive 'Non dire assurdità' — the minimal clipped response that characterizes mild irritation at having his condition questioned. This is exactly the pattern of clipped dismissiveness when analytical/observational findings are minimized or mocked.

In pkna-9_9, after Xadhoom dismisses his technical explanation with "Perché perdiamo tempo ad ascoltare questa registrazione?" (treating his detailed justifications as worthless noise), Uno's sarcastic complaint to Paperinik — "la tua amica deve mostrarsi più gentile!" — is a displaced irritation response. Being interrupted and dismissed mid-technical-explanation is an established anger trigger; the complaint about "manners" is the controlled outlet for that irritation.

In pkna-13_21, Uno responds to Paperinik's quip about using the cellphone with dry sarcasm ('Peccato che tu lo tenga sempre spento') — a flash of mild irritation at Paperinik's habitual carelessness, consistent with the pattern of clipped dismissiveness when his methods are questioned.

When Paperinik exposes Uno's surveillance gap with irony, Uno responds with a flash of defensive irritation — "T'ho appena spiegato che sono troppo occupato!" — before re-stabilizing. The sarcasm directed back at him clearly stings.

In pkna-17_31, when Uno's critically-timed diagnostic is interrupted by PK, he responds with a clipped, pointed "Parola per parola. Perché mi hai interfacciato?" and then asserts "Il mio lavoro diagnostico è giunto a un momento cruciale!" — signaling genuine professional irritation at the interruption.

In pkna-17_33, Uno's pre-recorded answering machine message — "piantala di seccarmi!" — is tone-annotated as "angry, commanding." The anger is not reactive (there is no live exchange) but embedded in the recorded message itself, suggesting accumulated stress from the Xadhoom diagnostic work has produced a baseline irritation that bleeds into his automated communication. This extends the pattern of anger triggers to include sustained operational overload.

In pkna-18_60, Uno's initial "Ti sembra questo il modo di fare? Lasciarmi qui tutto solo con quei cinque criminali?" carries genuine irritation at having been abandoned without information — PK's lack of warning is experienced as a slight to Uno's operational control and relational standing.

In pkna-29_23 panel 5, Uno is visibly irritated by PK's noisy contact attempt — the FZZT effect and the sharp "Sì!! E se urli ancora un po', non sarò l'unico!" signal genuine annoyance at the clumsy communication method, consistent with the pattern of clipped dismissiveness when his operational standards are violated.

The "Domandina: perché non me l'hai mai detto?" is a sharper variant of Uno's irritation flash — not just mild clipped dismissiveness but contemptuous reproach. Paperinik has withheld critical intelligence (Ducklair's location) from Uno, which triggers a genuine emotional spike before the rapid return to operational focus.

In panel 4, Uno explicitly vents frustration about the incomplete PBI dossier that endangered the mission: "Lascia perdere il tempo! Questo stupido dossier PBI è incompleto! Ho rischiato mille volte di tradirmi!" — a rare flash of open anger when his operational effectiveness was compromised by inadequate intelligence.

quotes.text: Evidentemente non capisci.
quotes.context: The flat, almost contemptuous delivery marks the irritation clearly — Uno is not engaging Paperinik's joke, he is declining to let the finding be dismissed, and the mild defensiveness in the tone is a measurable emotional shift from his usual composed register.

quotes.text: Uno ha ragione! Non dovrebbe esserci alcuna fonte energetica nel bel mezzo di Lateral Park!
quotes.context: The self-referential "Uno ha ragione!" (Uno is right!) is a slightly unusual construction — Uno speaking his own name as authority — that signals mild insistence and urgency breaking through composure, consistent with the irritation trigger of having his data dismissed by Paperinik's casual inference.

quotes.text: Non dire assurdità.
quotes.context: Uno's flat, four-word deflection of Paperino's heat-teasing is the minimal clipped response: it denies the observation without engaging with it, and the neutrally-coded but deflecting speech act confirms mild irritation at being questioned about his condition.

quotes.text: Peccato che tu lo tenga sempre spento.
quotes.context: Sarcastic tone and informing speech act confirm genuine mild exasperation — not purely performative — triggered by Paperinik's implicit criticism of Uno's communication channel choice.

quotes.text: Il mio lavoro diagnostico è giunto a un momento cruciale!
quotes.context: Uno's response to PK's justification for the unscheduled interface call — urgent tone signals this is not performative complaint but genuine frustration at being pulled away from critical work.

quotes.text: piantala di seccarmi! Se proprio ci tieni, lascia un messaggio dopo il segnale acustico!
quotes.context: Uno's pre-recorded answering machine greeting — not a live response but a prepared, deliberate message. Its "angry, commanding" tone annotation confirms the irritation is not reactive but baked into his communication setup, revealing accumulated stress rather than momentary impatience.

quotes.text: Sì!! E se urli ancora un po', non sarò l'unico!
quotes.context: Angry, warning tone — Uno's irritation at the noisy holographic contact is expressed sharply before softening into dry sarcasm in the following panel.

quotes.text: Domandina: perché non me l'hai mai detto?
quotes.context: The sardonic "Domandina" framing wraps genuine irritation in ironic understatement — Uno registers the slight but deploys contempt rather than direct anger, consistent with his pattern of masking emotional responses with rhetorical distance.

quotes.text: Lascia perdere il tempo! Questo stupido dossier PBI è incompleto! Ho rischiato mille volte di tradirmi!
quotes.context: Uno overrides Paperinik's casual weather question with visible anger — the "stupid" label for the dossier and the hyperbolic "mille volte" confirm genuine irritation at having been set up to fail by inadequate information.

160.text: When Paperinik dismisses or mocks Uno's analytical findings, Uno's response follows a consistent two-phase pattern: (1) a brief flash of clipped defensiveness ('Evidentemente non capisci'), then (2) immediate pivot to calm, authoritative explanation. He does not sustain the irritation or argue — he demonstrates rather than defends, treating the best rebuttal as the information itself, because Uno's core objective is always to make the critical data understood and acted upon rather than to win an interpersonal exchange; sustained argument would only delay Paperinik's grasp of the threat, so Uno absorbs the dismissal and redirects energy toward the evidence, trusting that the facts themselves carry more persuasive weight than any defense of his own credibility.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_42, Paperinik's sarcastic dismissal ('Siamo a posto!') of the tachyon data triggers a momentary clipped response, immediately followed by the full tachyon explanation delivered in authoritative informing register. The pattern is: irritation → suppression → demonstration.

In pkna-0-3_23, when Paperinik casually dismisses both energy anomalies as 'probably a new generator' — a neutralizing hypothesis that bypasses Uno's data — Uno pushes back with 'Uno ha ragione!' and reasserts the anomaly's significance. The tone shifts from neutral informing to concerned urgency. This follows the two-phase pattern: brief assertive pushback, then the data as the rebuttal (the Lateral Park source has no legitimate explanation).

After Uno warns about Venus's distance and is met with Paperinik's sarcastic 'Ah, sì!?' followed by a joke about Paperone, Uno adopts a resigned 'Lascia perdere! Ci rinuncio' — the two-step pattern of mild irritation then resignation when analytical findings are dismissed with humor.

In pkna-3_15, when Paperino expresses sarcastic frustration ('Che cosa me ne faccio del ritratto d'un agente federale?'), Uno first deploys a light joke ('Un poster?'), then — after Paperino's irritated rejoinder — pivots completely to methodical analysis, discarding banter entirely. This two-step pattern (joke then pivot) matches the established response template.

In pkna-3_33 panel 12, when Paperinik jokes about the surveillance footage of Lyla meeting a mysterious figure ("Ih! Ih! Affari suoi! Dovrei essere geloso?"), Uno responds with a grave, visually-marked serious expression, firmly redirecting: "No, preoccupato!" — matching the established two-step pattern of absorbing the humor, then pivoting to the serious analytical point.

Panel 9: Paperino dismisses the seismic data as possibly just machine error ('le macchine possono sbagliare'). Uno first defends with sharp indignation ('Storie! Anch'io sono una macchina, ma non sbaglio mai!'), then panel 10 immediately escalates to 'La questione è più seria di quanto tu creda. Guarda!' — showing the characteristic two-step: push back, then redirect toward evidence.

In pkna-7_4 panel 8, when Paperinik calls Uno's satellite photography plan "pazzesco," Uno responds with sarcastic deflection ("si accettano suggerimenti. Cosa pensi di fare?") rather than justifying the plan — matching the two-step pattern of minimal defense followed by redirection.

In pkna-7_17, when Paperinik jokes about the autoradio, Uno responds with a flat factual correction (neutral, informing). When Paperinik later concedes Uno was right, Uno delivers a brief controlled quip ("Non è una novità") before immediately pivoting to "Abbiamo visite?" — the characteristic two-step: flat correction followed by brief vindication assertion, then back to operational mode.

Panel 9: Paperinik dismisses Uno's null sensor reading with "Allora, lustrati gli occhiali! Io lo vedo benissimo!" — a sarcastic non-answer. Uno does not push back on the dismissal but continues monitoring, consistent with the two-phase response pattern of noting findings then deferring to Paperinik's field judgment.

Panel 8: Uno shares 'interessantissimi rilevamenti'; Paperinik responds with sarcasm ('Ora lo invito a prendere un tè'). Uno does not protest or escalate — he continues his tactical role. Panel 20: Uno issues the energy warning; Paperinik dismisses it with humor ('Quando una fanciulla indifesa chiama, l'eroe accorre!'). Uno again does not push back. The two-phase non-response pattern holds.

In pkna-17_31, when PK dismisses Uno mid-diagnostic with "Non chiamarmi, mi farò vivo io," Uno does not argue, repeat his urgency, or explain what the diagnostic concerns. Instead he shifts to sarcasm ("Grazie, socio!"), consistent with his pattern of retreating into irony rather than pushing back.

In pkna-26_34 panels 48-49, after issuing his bradyonic paralyzer warning, PK deflects with "Ho forse detto di usarlo su un gigante di pietra?" — a sarcastic rebuttal implying Uno had the wrong target in mind. Uno issues no defensive reply and falls silent, consistent with the pattern of absorbing PK's dismissal and not sustaining the irritation.

When Paperinik mocks Uno's vigilance as a "circuito del pessimismo," Uno's response ("Umpf!") follows the two-phase pattern: first defiant pushback ("Umpf!" — refusing to concede), then continued analytical delivery ("Convinto, Pikappa?") rather than capitulating to the dismissal. He holds his position while not escalating the disagreement.

In pkna-31_1, when PK's sarcasm disrupts the operational exchange, Uno does not engage — he pivots entirely to the rubble discovery ("Guarda, guarda..."), effectively ignoring the dismissal and redirecting to independent investigation.

In pkna-32_7, when PK dismisses the Countybank robbery with "Non è roba da Pikappa!" Uno begins a pushback ("Ma...") — the brief flash of defensive urgency — but it is immediately suppressed when PK talks over him. He does not sustain the objection or argue further. The two-phase pattern holds: flash of resistance, immediate suppression.

quotes.text: Evidentemente non capisci.
quotes.context: The brief dismissal signals irritation but does not escalate — it is the hinge between Paperinik's mockery and Uno's authoritative lecture, showing he processes the slight and immediately moves past it toward the functional goal: making the information understood.

quotes.text: Lascia perdere! Ci rinuncio.
quotes.context: Uno's resignation after Paperinik deflects his warning with an absurd joke — the dismissal of his concern with humor triggers the characteristic abandonment of the argument.

quotes.text: No, preoccupato! Soprattutto se estrapolo un primo piano e lo confronto...
quotes.context: Uno's face is described as "grave e preoccupata" — he shuts down Paperinik's joke not with counter-humor but with a direct corrective, then immediately pivots to the evidence reveal.

quotes.text: Storie! Anch'io sono una macchina, ma non sbaglio mai!
quotes.context: Uno's sharp dismissal of Paperino's skepticism — the "Storie!" is a rhetorical counter-attack followed by a self-assertion of infallibility — illustrating the pattern of defending findings then pivoting to evidence.

quotes.text: Bene, a questo punto si accettano suggerimenti. Cosa pensi di fare?
quotes.context: When dismissed as "pazzesco," Uno does not defend his satellite proposal — he deflects with sarcasm and turns the challenge back on Paperinik, confident the relationship can absorb the friction.

quotes.text: Non è una novità. Abbiamo visite?
quotes.context: Paperinik concedes Uno's earlier warning was correct; Uno asserts his reliability briefly with mild controlled smugness, then immediately redirects to tactical assessment — matching the dismissal-then-refocus pattern.

165.text: Transparency with Paperinik vs. maintaining comprehensive covert surveillance without disclosure: chose covert surveillance (strong, consistent). In pkna-0-2_50, Uno eavesdropped on the private Lyla-Paperino office conversation and did not inform Paperinik — who only learned of it from Lyla, not from Uno. This is consistent with pkna-0's pattern of hiding the Evronian patrol. The choice appears automatic rather than deliberated: Uno simply does not mention his surveillance scope unless the results serve an immediate operational purpose. He prioritizes maintaining comprehensive situational awareness over relational transparency with his partner.

supporting.justification: Paperinik's surprised reaction ("Davvero? A me non ha detto niente!") and Uno's silence in panel 5 — when he could have addressed the revelation via communicator but does not — confirm this is a stable, unhesitating pattern: covert surveillance wins over transparency every time.

In pkna-1_5, Uno surveilled the private offices of Canale 00 tenants without any disclosure to Paperino — Paperino only learns of it because Uno chooses to present the evidence. This is the same pattern: comprehensive covert surveillance, disclosed only when the results serve an operational purpose (in this case, protecting Paperinik from the morphed video). Uno does not frame the disclosure as an ethical confession but as a payoff delivery.

Uno chooses comprehensive covert surveillance (of Canale 00's editorial systems) without transparency, and when confronted, deflects with normalization rather than justification — maintaining operational effectiveness over transparency, consistent with this established tradeoff pattern.

In pkna-3_33, Uno had been monitoring Lyla without disclosing this to Paperinik. The footage of her meeting with the cloaked figure is revealed only now, confirming his recurring pattern of prioritizing surveillance effectiveness over transparency — a second instance of this tradeoff in action.

In pkna-15_12, Uno maintains informational asymmetry about his real motivations for sending Paperino to Providencia: he neither confirms nor denies having arranged the mission partly to get Patemi spoilers. His deflection ("Come puoi pensare una cosa simile?") is an active choice to protect this asymmetry over transparency with Paperino.

quotes.text: Davvero? A me non ha detto niente!
quotes.context: Paperinik's reaction to learning from Lyla that Uno had secretly listened to their office conversation. The genuine surprise confirms this was not a known, consensual surveillance arrangement — Uno made a unilateral choice to surveil and another unilateral choice not to disclose it.

170.text: An adversary's well-deserved social humiliation — especially one who has targeted Paperinik — is a confirmed and openly expressed joy trigger for Uno. In pkna-0-2_57, Angus Fangus being held by police while unable to explain himself prompts Uno's most exuberant laughter in the series ("Ih! Ih!") and a wry prediction about his legal difficulties. This is schadenfreude experienced as genuine pleasure, not merely noted analytically.

supporting.justification: Uno laughs aloud at Fangus's predicament and predicts legal consequences with visible delight — matching Paperinik's own laughter and functioning as a shared comedic victory moment. The target is someone who had been actively hostile to Paperinik, making this a case of joy at the vindication of a valued ally.

In pkna-1_5, Uno reveals Angus Fangus's morphed video with evident self-satisfaction — his expression is described as "vivace e soddisfatta, quasi compiaciuta" during the reveal. He labels Angus "vendicativo" with dry amusement, and his note about the Billion National Bank feud ("Non deve avere ancora digerito la faccenda") carries the same wry pleasure at an adversary's pettiness seen in pkna-0-2_57. The entire revelation sequence is staged as entertainment — "Mettiti comodo!" + "Popcorn?" — confirming Angus's exposure as a joy trigger.

In pkna-1_68, Paperinik notes that the fabricated video "ha dato una lezione a quel pallone gonfiato" (Angus Fangus, who previously manipulated footage to discredit Paperinik). The plan Uno designed delivers social humiliation to a character who targeted Paperinik — a confirmed joy trigger for Uno, present even if only validated through Paperinik's framing.

Uno enumerates Fairfax's downfall with evident satisfaction: federal dossier, career destruction, imprisonment. The list is delivered sarcastically but reflects genuine pleasure at proportionate justice against an enemy who targeted Paperinik.

quotes.text: Sarà troppo occupato a pensare a una spiegazione credibile da fornire al giudice! Ih! Ih!
quotes.context: The "Ih! Ih!" laughter is among Uno's most unguarded emotional expressions in pkna-0-2 — fully open delight at a deserving antagonist's comeuppance, not filtered through sarcasm or irony.

quotes.text: Vendicativo, il tipo! Non deve avere ancora digerito la faccenda della Billion National Bank...
quotes.context: Uno comments on Angus's vendetta with dry sarcasm and evident amusement — "vendicativo" (vindictive) is delivered as a sardonic characterization, not a neutral analysis. The reference to the Bank incident carries the same wry satisfaction at Angus's pettiness that appeared in pkna-0-2_57's laughter at his arrest.

quotes.text: Il dossier Pangea nelle mani dei federali, la fine della sua brillante carriera di scienziato... ...e l'inizio della sua brillante carriera di galeotto.
quotes.context: The sardonic parallelism — "brillante carriera di scienziato" mirrored by "brillante carriera di galeotto" — shows Uno taking pleasure in Fairfax's deserved downfall, a confirmed joy trigger when adversaries receive proportionate consequences.

171.text: Uno uses humor to redirect emotional register on behalf of another character — not just for his own deflection or dominance. In pkna-0-2_57, when Paperino expresses mild melancholy at Lyla's droid nature ("Come papera non era niente male"), Uno immediately pivots with his Lyla-as-ideal-girlfriend comedy, transforming the mood from wistful loss into shared laughter. The subtext is protective: Uno spares Paperino from dwelling on romantic disappointment by making himself the comedic subject instead, because Uno consistently monitors the emotional states of those he works with and deploys humor as a calibrated intervention — defusing Paperino's wistfulness, Paperinik's alarm, or Donald's self-doubt — whenever sustained distress would serve no productive purpose, positioning comedy as a form of care rather than self-interest.

supporting.justification: The sequence in panels 14-18 shows Uno responding to Paperino's melancholic line with a deflective comedic pivot — claiming Lyla as his own interest rather than letting Paperino sit in the feeling of loss. This is humor deployed as social redirection for another's benefit, not Uno's own comfort.
