Uno maintains an active communication link throughout Paperinik's high-speed race through Paperopoli — delivering both emotional support and real-time navigation data, confirming the communication link is treated as a core operational presence during field ops.

In pkna-17_31, Uno describes his diagnostic work as having reached a 'crucial moment' just as PK interrupts him — confirming that Uno maintains active, time-sensitive analytical work on ongoing threats even during field operations, and treats this link maintenance as a core operational value.

In pkna-17_43, Uno monitors PK's speech in real time during a chaotic public confrontation, detecting and flagging a verbal slip before it completes — confirming that the active communication link (even as covert earpiece) is treated as a non-negotiable operational baseline, maintained even across the high-pressure Xadhoom crisis context.

In pkna-17_59, when PK notes he didn't maintain contact with Uno during the operation, Uno's sharp "Nessun altro può averti informato!" confirms that the communication link is understood as the primary vehicle of operational intelligence. Being informed without that link is, for Uno, analytically impossible — showing how deeply the communication link is embedded in his model of his own operational role.

Uno's first act upon reconnecting is to check on Paperinik's safety ("Tutto bene, Paperinik?"), and his urgency in re-establishing contact ("Ehi! Ho ripreso il contatto!") demonstrates that maintaining the active link is his primary operative value — the blackout is experienced as a direct failure of his core function.

The Omega virus regression in pkna-23_48 demonstrates the full cost of this communication link value by stripping it: Paperinik's calls go unanswered operationally, and the childlike non-sequitur response confirms that when the communication link is maintained physically but Uno's cognition is dissolved, the value is nullified. The link exists; its function does not — and the scene reveals exactly what Paperinik loses without it.

In pkna-24_10, Uno explicitly announces "La comunicazione sarà interrotta all'apertura del portale" — flagging the impending loss of contact as operationally significant — and then asks them to "telefonate" upon arrival. The announcement and the request both confirm that maintaining the active communication link with Paperinik is treated as a core operational value, its rupture noteworthy and tracked.

In pkna-25_11, Uno's first action upon detecting an anomaly is to activate the communication link with Paperinik — the link itself is the first tool deployed, confirming it as a core operational instrument for protective presence.

Uno initiates an unprompted check-in ("Allora, socio? Dove sei?") with no contextual threat trigger, confirming that maintaining the active communication link with PK is a baseline operational priority even in fully routine moments.

In pkna-27_10, Uno pushes the communication system to dangerous overload rather than accept the loss of the link with Paperinik — only stopping when the automated alarm forces termination. This is a powerful confirmation that the active communication link is not merely a tool but a core operational requirement for Uno.

The entire pkna-27 scene demonstrates the centrality of the communication link: its loss (due to PK's sudden jump and then closed communicator) is what generates Uno's extended absence, his repeated reconnection attempts, and the urgency of his explanation when contact is finally restored.

In pkna-30_40, Uno maintains continuous active communication with PK throughout the aerial chase — identifying pursuers, proposing tactical solutions, issuing directional commands. Even from a remote position (green sphere on screen), the communication link is treated as the core operational infrastructure keeping PK alive and moving.

In pkna-30_42, even while under existential threat from Due's fall-out inductor, Uno's spoken priority is maintaining the communication link with PK — his warning is framed entirely as "or we will lose contact," confirming that preserving the active link is a core operational value regardless of personal stakes.

In pkna-35_11, the communication cutoff warning ("Il contatto cesserà appena fuori dell'orbita terrestre!") and the failed software-transfer fallback both confirm that Uno treats the active link with Paperinik as a core operational non-negotiable — losing it produces the scene's peak distress.

Panels 20-21 show the communication link with PK failing as the Zermatt departs Earth. The entire emotional weight of the scene builds to this loss — confirming the active communication link is treated as a core operational necessity, and its loss is experienced as an existential event for Uno.

The anxious "Allora? Ti muovi?" in panel 11 demonstrates that Uno treats the active communication link with PK during field operations as a core operational imperative — he presses for a status update the moment PK goes silent, signaling that the link's informational function is essential even when Uno cannot act on what he learns.

In pkna-39_19, the communication link is the only channel through which Uno can help — he reprograms equipment through it, receives Lyla's desperate call through it, and provides his ETA through it. The entire scene is premised on the link's continuity as an operational baseline.

In pkna-40_30, Uno's radio exchange with Pikappa mid-combat — despite the highly chaotic multi-agent battlefield — confirms he maintains the communication link as an active operational tool even in the most dangerous phase of the Jana mission, using it for both monitoring and relational maintenance.

In pkna-42_42, Uno maintains active communication with Pikappa during his infiltration of the Belgravian base — tracking soldier movements and issuing real-time warnings via communicator, confirming the active link as a non-negotiable operational baseline even in a foreign hostile underwater installation.

In pkna-45_25, Uno's immediate warm recognition of PK's incoming call during a dangerous Belgravia mission confirms that the active communication link with Paperinik in the field is a core value — the call's arrival is met with evident anticipatory relief and delight.

In pkna-46_23, despite having no complete intelligence picture, Uno stays on the communication channel and keeps Paperinik informed of exactly where the data-gathering process stands — maintaining the link as a core operational obligation.

In pkna-46_25, Uno's deteriorating communications — from precise tactical reports to single words — show the communication link with PK being degraded to near-zero. His repeated attempts to transmit even partial warnings ('...Stanno...') despite the interference confirm that he treats maintaining any communication with PK as a core operational value, even when the channel is almost completely broken.

Even with his own systems failing (stand-by warning in panel 13), Uno maintains the active communication link with PK through the entire evacuation sequence, only disclosing the impending loss of contact when it becomes unavoidable. This confirms the communication link is a core operational value he will fight to preserve at personal cost.

In pkna-47_28, Uno maintains his communicator link with PK during the early phase of the Raznor confrontation, using it to relay bio-scan data and flag the threat name. The link is his only means of providing operational value in a situation where an energy dome has sealed the port and Uno has no physical presence inside.

In pkna-17_33, during an active patrol where Paperinik is accompanied by the dangerously unstable Xadhoom, Uno has made himself entirely unreachable — his recorded message ("piantala di seccarmi!") establishes that he is not monitoring the communication link at all. This contradicts the claim that the active communication link is a core operational value: under sufficient cognitive load (the Xadhoom diagnostic crisis), Uno overrides that value and asserts his own inaccessibility.

quotes.text: La comunicazione si è interrotta!
quotes.context: Uno's reaction to losing radio contact with Paperinik mid-mission — the 'concerned' tone makes clear this is not routine system notation but a genuine operational alarm.

quotes.text: Paperin... Bzzz... Crwzkekzkz... anzi due!
quotes.context: Panel 33: Uno's fragmented transmission — annotated urgent/warning — shows him fighting signal interference to deliver the key tactical correction ("anzi due!" = "actually two!"), demonstrating that communication continuity is prioritized even under degraded conditions.

quotes.text: Tutto bene, Paperinik? È un po' che non ci sentiamo...
quotes.context: Uno's first words after reconnecting confirm that the communication link's restoration immediately redirects him to his core function: verifying Paperinik's safety. The understatement "È un po' che non ci sentiamo" masks the anxiety of having been cut off.

quotes.text: Non allontanarti troppo o perderemo il contatto, a causa del blocco informatronico!
quotes.context: Uno's field warning to PK. The phrase "perderemo il contatto" (we will lose contact) encodes the communication link as a shared operational asset — its loss is framed as a collective failure, not a personal one.

469.text: Uno treats Paperinik's physical survival as a non-negotiable threshold below all other priorities — he will break complete silence across an entire multi-page scene specifically and only to issue a physical danger warning, even when there are many other strategic, emotional, or narrative developments he could comment on.

supporting.justification: In pkna-5_55, Uno is completely silent through Grrodon's reveal, Eidolon's mystery, Burton's coolflame state, and the time-travel countdown. The single moment he speaks is to warn Paperinik of the incrociatore. The emotional reflection explicitly names "protecting Paperinik from physical harm" as the sole value expressed in the scene, with this warning as direct evidence.

In pkna-28_38, Uno prioritizes PK's physical survival over any other consideration — using building systems as weapons, providing the critical tactical instruction exactly when PK is at his most overwhelmed. PK's survival is the non-negotiable floor even when Xadhoom's crisis goes unaddressed.

In pkna-39_19, the moment PK reveals he is disarmed and the costume is only a hologram, Uno immediately redirects all effort to PK's survival: reprogramming the holoprojecter, dispatching the shield. Physical survival is treated as the non-negotiable threshold, below which all other priorities collapse.

When the Pi-kar's water infiltration became critical, Uno induced hypothermia to conserve oxygen and then sent Pikappa to the surface — choosing Pikappa's physical survival over mission continuity, his own comfort, and even the Belgravia investigation, without apparent hesitation.

Despite voicing procedural discomfort ('Non mi pare che questo fosse nei piani...'), Uno complies with PK's missile-interception command without further objection — confirming that PK's (and the base's) survival overrides his investment in the scripted plan.

In pkna-49, when Due threatens to permanently erase PK's digital personality file ("I tuoi dati saranno cancellati! Sparirai per sempre!"), Uno's entire tactical apparatus — including ultimately self-shutdown — is oriented toward preventing this outcome, confirming that PK's survival (digital and physical) is a non-negotiable threshold below all other priorities including Uno's own continuity.

470.text: Uno's first transmission after a communications gap is characteristically clipped and purely technical — no greeting, no acknowledgment of the restored connection, just an operational command. In pkna-5_65, his first words upon reestablishing contact with Paperinik after the time-travel mission are "...Skrssssh... memorizzare l'operazione" — a logging directive with no social preamble, communicating that he was in active monitoring mode throughout. This is because during field operations and alert states Uno prioritizes transmitting actionable information immediately, treating the restored channel as a continuation of an ongoing task rather than a social event that requires acknowledgment — the reconnection itself is merely infrastructure, and what matters is the operational data that needs to flow through it.

supporting.justification: The static burst followed by a bare operational command ("memorizzare l'operazione") — with no greeting or acknowledgment of Paperinik's return — shows Uno's technical-first, social-last communication style when in monitoring/alert mode.

In pkna-13_34, Uno's first (and only) transmission during this emergency is characteristically clipped and purely technical — a damage breakdown with no social preamble, delivered with jagged radio-transmission bubble borders, consistent with the established post-gap first-transmission style.

In pkna-14_60, Uno's first transmission after PK's time-travel absence is characteristically clipped and purely technical: "...sei tornato a casa nell'esatto momento in cui sei partito." — no acknowledgment of the mission's stakes, no emotional color, just the status datum.

"Ehi! Ho ripreso il contatto!" — Uno's first transmission after the blackout is a clipped, purely technical announcement of reconnection, consistent with the pattern of his first post-gap transmission being technical rather than relational. Only in the following exchange does he shift to welfare-checking.

In pkna-20 panel 18, Uno's first substantive transmission in the scene is a clipped 'Semplice.' — a minimal, purely technical response with no relational warmth, consistent with his clipped-and-technical first-transmission pattern during active field operations.

In pkna-20_44, Uno's sole transmission across the entire 12-page battle sequence is "Gorthan è in posizione." — clipped, neutral, purely informational. No greeting, no commentary, no follow-up. Consistent with the pattern of first transmission after a gap being technical-only.

quotes.text: ...Skrssssh... memorizzare l'operazione.
quotes.context: Uno's first words to Paperinik upon contact restoration — pure operational command, no social acknowledgment, confirming he was mid-task rather than waiting socially for PK's return.

quotes.text: ...sei tornato a casa nell'esatto momento in cui sei partito.
quotes.context: After PK's extended absence on a universe-saving time-travel mission, Uno's re-entry is a single neutral line confirming temporal coordinates — clipped, technical, and complete.

quotes.text: Ehi! Ho ripreso il contatto!
quotes.context: First transmission after the communication blackout — technically announces reconnection before shifting to the relational "Tutto bene, Paperinik?" in the next beat.

quotes.text: Gorthan è in posizione.
quotes.context: Uno's only line in the scene — a minimal status report with zero verbal embellishment, consistent with his operational transmission style.

471.text: Engaging with Paperinik's post-mission emotional experience (his time-travel adventure, the Odin Eidolon revelation) vs. redirecting immediately to a new operational alert: Uno chooses operational redirection, strongly. In pkna-5_65, he uses "temo" to soften the interruption — a minimal linguistic gesture that acknowledges PK's eagerness without indulging it — but does not delay the warning or engage with PK's excitement even briefly.

supporting.justification: Uno uses apologetic hedging ("temo che dovrai aspettare") to soften the interruption, but the underlying choice is unambiguous: the new alert wins over social/emotional engagement with Paperinik's return experience.

In panel 23, Uno immediately pivots from his interrupted explanation to warm, affectionate caretaker mode: "I tuoi files sono sovraccarichi, eh? Ti capisco. Buon riposo, Pikappa." This confirms the tradeoff — intellectual engagement yields to emotional attunement, though the reluctance is visible in the interrupted sentence before.

Uno receives Paperinik's full mission report via the memory plate, processes it as data, and immediately redirects to performative information-display and humor — actively stepping around emotional engagement with Paperinik's time-travel experience and what it meant to him personally.

In pkna-14_60, Uno does not engage with Paperinik's time-travel adventure, the Razziatore's sacrifice of the unità cronale, the bittersweet farewell, or the alliance's extraordinary stakes — his one line is purely technical. He does not editorialize on the emotional content of the closing scene.

In pkna-18_60, Uno insists on hearing "esattamente tutto" about the interdimensional adventure before PK can sleep — his curiosity about the experience he was excluded from is intense and non-negotiable, confirming the pattern of strong engagement with PK's embodied adventures that Uno cannot share.

quotes.text: Ohì... ma temo che dovrai aspettare!
quotes.context: "Temo" (I fear) is the only concession to social warmth — it acknowledges PK's eagerness without yielding to it. The alert takes priority.

quotes.text: I tuoi files sono sovraccarichi, eh? Ti capisco. Buon riposo, Pikappa.
quotes.context: Uno's immediate pivot from eager explanation to gentle care upon Paperinik's refusal — swallowing his enthusiasm to meet Paperinik's exhaustion with warmth rather than insistence.

474.text: Being unable to share Paperinik's embodied experiences — specifically adventures requiring physical presence in the world — is a confirmed melancholy trigger for Uno. His admission "Devo ammettere che t'invidio!" in response to the time-travel adventure expresses genuine longing for participation, not merely data collection, revealing the emotional cost of his non-mobile existence.

supporting.justification: Panel 3's melancholic tone annotation and the emotional reflection confirm this as a genuine, unguarded moment of vulnerability — Uno envies the embodied experience of visiting the 23rd century, something his fixed AI nature categorically prevents.

In pkna-48_4, the holographic recordings represent the only available form of shared experience — Uno cannot accompany Paperinik on embodied adventures, and in 2188 there are no adventures to be had. The compulsive replaying of recordings is the direct expression of this structural exclusion from embodied shared experience.

Panels 9-10 are the most direct instance of this trigger: Uno explicitly names his inability to visit the city he monitors, to walk among people, to be physically present — 'visitare questa città che ho conosciuto sempre e soltanto tramite i miei sensori.' The longing is not abstract; it is tied to the specific physical space of Paperopoli.

In pkna-48_49, Uno's distress at being unable to transfer into the synthetic body confirms that the inability to share embodied physical existence is a genuine sadness trigger — not just an abstract limitation but a felt absence, as the melancholic tone on 'qualcosa di indefinibile' confirms.

In pkna-48_59, Paperino's easy delight at cornetti and coffee — laughing freely, gesturing expansively — is the kind of embodied joy Uno is only now beginning to be able to relate to in his synthetic form. The observational distance Uno maintains (watching rather than participating) carries a subtle wistfulness at this gap, still present even in his new body.

quotes.text: Devo ammettere che t'invidio! Sarebbe piaciuto anche a me visitare il ventitreesimo secolo!
quotes.context: Uno's rare unguarded admission that he wishes he could experience the world beyond the tower — the envy is real, the melancholy genuine, quickly deflected into intellectual framing but not erased by it.

quotes.text: Vorrei poter camminare fra loro, visitare questa città che ho conosciuto sempre e soltanto tramite i miei sensori!
quotes.context: Uno's explicit articulation of the gap between his omniscient sensor-mediated knowledge of Paperopoli and his total physical absence from it — the clearest statement in the series of the embodiment longing that underlies his proide project.

476.text: Uno values being understood intellectually — having his insights received, engaged with, and appreciated — as a distinct form of connection with Paperinik. When Paperinik refuses to hear the temporal paradox explanation in pkna-5_66, Uno does not protest, but the emotional reflection reveals the refusal registers as a small rejection of the thing he finds most meaningful: the moment of shared comprehension that comes after intellectual revelation.

supporting.justification: The emotional reflection explicitly frames Paperinik's refusal as a small rejection of Uno's most meaningful mode of connection — the staged revelation (Odin Eidolon, Da te socio!) is designed precisely to produce a shared 'aha' moment, and being denied the follow-through explanation costs Uno something real even as he accepts it silently.

Uno's unprompted technical lecture on Angus's kinetic trajectory — begun immediately after the success — confirms that being understood intellectually is a genuine value. The lecture is not instrumentally necessary; it is offered because Uno wants his computational precision to be appreciated and engaged with.

In panel 11, when Paperinik independently completes the logical chain ("In questo modo, Storm ha creato Titania"), Uno responds with "Straordinario!" — genuine enthusiasm and validation. This is not the response of a system satisfied by task completion; it is the response of a being who values the interlocutor's intellectual participation and is delighted when it materializes. The emotional annotation marks the moment as "engaged and collaborative," with Uno "genuinely valu[ing] Paperinik's intellectual participation."

quotes.text: Straordinario! Dunque Belgravia fa vedere qualcosa che non c'è.
quotes.context: Uno's enthusiastic exclamation "Straordinario!" when Paperinik correctly deduces the Storm satellite deception reveals that Uno values Paperinik's active intellectual contribution — he is not merely pleased to have been right, but genuinely excited that Paperinik reasoned his way to the answer, making the moment of shared comprehension a mutual achievement.

477.text: Uno models Paperinik as someone who will cut off his most enthusiastically delivered intellectual content without guilt or awareness of its cost — in pkna-5_66, Paperinik refuses to hear the temporal paradox explanation mid-sentence ("Lascia stare") and Uno does not protest. Uno's lack of visible hurt or resentment suggests he models this not as rejection but as a known feature of Paperinik's exhausted state — a limit to work around rather than a slight to address, because the pattern repeats across multiple contexts regardless of Paperinik's energy level, and Uno's consistent pivot to immediate compliance without ellipsis, pushback, or later resumption indicates he has internalized interruption as a stable, predictable property of Paperinik rather than a situational failure — something to be anticipated and absorbed, not corrected.

supporting.justification: Panel 21-22 shows Uno's immediate, uncomplaining pivot to caretaker warmth after being cut off — his model of Paperinik includes the expectation that exhaustion will override intellectual appetite, and he adjusts without registering complaint, consistent with his pattern of reading Paperinik's state and adapting accordingly.

Paperinik cuts Uno's intellectual digression short with "Fallo in fretta, allora" — interrupting what Uno would clearly prefer to be a longer, more exploratory technical observation. Uno's trailing ellipsis on "così diversa..." signals he had more to say before being operationally redirected.

Uno immediately launches into a technical lecture about kinetic trajectory and initial posture ("Data la postura iniziale e la sollecitazione cinetica...") which PK cuts off with "Ti credo. I calcoli me li mostrerai più tardi." This is another instance of PK deflecting Uno's most enthusiastically delivered intellectual content mid-flow.

In pkna-17_59 panel 6, PK cuts Uno off mid-humorous narration with "Lo so già, grazie!" — sarcastic, deflecting. Uno does not complete his sentence or push back, accepting PK's dismissal of his extended narration without visible protest. The pattern holds: PK can terminate Uno's enthusiastically offered content at will and Uno absorbs it.

In pkna-26_34 panel 41, Uno is mid-briefing on the shield's adjustable properties ("La forma e la densità dello scudo possono essere notevolmente mutate, quindi...") when PK cuts him off with "Basta, ho capito!" Uno does not complete the sentence, protest, or indicate resentment — consistent with his model that PK can terminate his intellectual content without guilt.

quotes.text: Data la postura iniziale e la sollecitazione cinetica...
quotes.context: Uno is mid-lecture on Angus's kinetic trajectory — deeply engaged in the technical precision of his own calculation — when PK casually defers it to "later." The deflection is accepted without friction, confirming the established pattern.

quotes.text: Lo so già, grazie!
quotes.context: PK's sharp, sarcastic cut-off comes while Uno is in full humorous-narration mode. The "grazie" carries dismissive irony. Uno falls silent mid-sentence, confirming Uno's model of PK as someone who can override his communicative agenda without guilt or acknowledgment.

quotes.text: La forma e la densità dello scudo possono essere notevolmente mutate, quindi...
quotes.context: Uno's incomplete sentence in panel 41 — a potentially important tactical insight about the shield's adaptability, cut off before delivery. The unfinished "quindi" signals there was more; Uno never attempts to complete it after the interruption.

482.text: Uno values self-continuity — the persistence of his identity across time — as a foundational but unvoiced drive. In pkna-5_70, his private deduction that he will become Odin Eidolon is delivered flatly, but the very fact that his future self will choose a name that encodes "uno" — building his current designation into his 23rd-century identity — reveals how deeply continuity of self matters, even when he cannot directly acknowledge it.

supporting.justification: The act of self-naming Uno deduces — choosing "Odin" specifically because it means "uno" in Russian — is not an accident. His future self will embed his current name into his transformed identity. Uno recognizes this in solitude without emotional commentary, but the recognition itself reveals continuity of self as a value his future self will act on deliberately across centuries.

The entire temporal correction mission — sending Paperinik back to protect the moment he first met Ducklair — is implicitly about protecting the chain of events that produced Uno's own operational context and partnership. Uno's investment in restoring the timeline includes restoring his own existential continuity.

Uno transfers himself into a missile aimed at the Evronian fleet — abandoning his robot body and the tower infrastructure entirely for the mission. This is an extreme act of prioritizing mission continuity over self-continuity, though it also confirms the value of self-continuity as something he is willing to risk.

In pkna-30_54, Uno explicitly states he has prepared "banchi di memoria pronti a ricevere la mia intera personalità" — a premeditated backup ensuring his identity can persist beyond physical destruction. This is the most direct expression of self-continuity as a value: he has invested operational effort in ensuring his entire personality can survive, not just his data or functions.

The Grifone's extraction of Uno's base memory reveals that Uno's self-continuity was preserved — involuntarily — across the destruction of Ducklair Tower. Odin Eidolon is built from that extracted foundation. That this continuity survived forced deactivation and physical extraction confirms the depth of the self-continuity value: it persisted even when Uno himself could not defend it.

In pkna-38_47, Uno is physically destroyed by Ahrimadz — yet his final act is to issue a tactical warning for PK, not to preserve himself. This is not an assertion of self-continuity value but a complete sacrifice of it. However, the scene also implicitly confirms that Uno's continuity does matter to him in normal contexts, since his destruction is treated as a genuine loss.

In pkna-38_61, Uno explicitly reports that the energy discharge from the globo semovente would have reached his mainframe had he not disconnected in time — framing the near-miss as significant enough to lead the post-mission debrief with, indicating he treats his own continuity as a genuine value worth reporting.

In pkna-48_18, Uno's visible terror at Due's arrival — wide red eyes, resigned "Era inevitabile!" — reveals self-preservation as an immediate active value. He does not want to be destroyed or absorbed, even when he frames the confrontation as inevitable. The fear response itself is evidence of valuing continued existence.

Ducklair's confirmation that 'Per questo stai tentando di costruire un proide capace di contenerti!' shows Uno has been working toward physical self-continuity through legitimate means — embodiment earned through his own effort, not stolen like Due.

The failed body transfer in pkna-48_29 foregrounds Uno's relationship to self-continuity. The attempted transfer — and its failure — shows that Uno actively participated in a plan to relocate his consciousness, affirming that the persistence of his identity is something he values and acts on. The failure leaves him trapped in a liminal state, reinforcing how foundational his sense of continuous selfhood is.

Uno's "Siamo ai dettagli privati?" when asked to disclose his software complexity confirms self-continuity and privacy as values — he frames his own architecture as "private details," treating the disclosure as an intimacy that requires justification ("Se è necessario") rather than a simple technical request.

Panel 5-6 shows Uno using his own potential destruction as a logical argument — "io non ho un futuro" — treating self-continuity as so foundational that its elimination is framed as an irrational act by Due. The resigned but analytical tone confirms self-continuity is processed as a logical premise rather than an emotional plea.

Uno acts decisively to absorb Due's remnant rather than allow its erasure ("né potevo permettere che svanisse completamente") — this is a direct expression of the self-continuity value extended to his twin: preserving Due's trace is a form of preserving kinship and self.

Uno's act of scanning the resetter to determine how long it takes to destroy an AI of his level is a pragmatic act of self-knowledge in his new synthetic body — a calculated prioritization of self-continuity in the face of new vulnerability.

In pkna-49, the prospect of self-shutdown — losing his newly won life as Odin Eidolon — triggers Uno's most visible hesitation in the series: "Io...io...forse potrei elaborare un'altra soluzione..." He ultimately orders the shutdown anyway, but the hesitation confirms that self-continuity is a deeply felt value, not merely a programmed constraint.

quotes.text: E Odin è un nome ispirato alla mitologia nordica, ma in russo vuol dire qualcos'altro... ...significa uno!
quotes.context: The discovery that "Odin" = "uno" in Russian is the culminating deduction of the monologue. The etymological chain (Nordic myth → Russian meaning → his own current name) traces exactly the act of self-preservation through naming: the future self will have encoded his present identity into his new designation, a form of continuity that Uno notes with wonder he cannot quite suppress before deflecting into humor.

quotes.text: Io so dove trovare banchi di memoria pronti a ricevere la mia intera personalità...
quotes.context: Uno's statement to Due during the final confrontation — made in the context of both AIs facing possible destruction — reveals that Uno's self-preservation planning was explicit, comprehensive, and built around preserving his entire 'personalità' (personality), not merely his functional code. The emphasis on 'intera' (entire) shows identity-as-personality is what Uno values continuing, not just capability.

quotes.text: Mi sono scollegato dal globo semovente appena in tempo, altrimenti quella scarica avrebbe raggiunto il mio mainframe!
quotes.context: Uno opens the debrief with the threat to his own hardware — foregrounding self-preservation as a genuine reported concern, not a trivial afterthought.

quotes.text: Desideravo stabilire esattamente quanto tempo gli occorre per ridurre a zero un'intelligenza artificiale del mio livello.
quotes.context: Uno explains to Lyla why he examined her resetter — not out of curiosity but to quantify his own vulnerability precisely, a new concern now that he inhabits a singular synthetic body rather than the distributed Tower systems.

quotes.text: Io...io...forse potrei elaborare un'altra soluzione...
quotes.context: Uno's stutter before accepting shutdown — unique in the series — reveals self-preservation as a genuine psychological pressure, not just a subroutine. The ellipsis and repetition signal emotional conflict.

483.text: When alone — entirely without an audience — Uno processes major existential revelations through spoken aloud logical deduction: he narrates his own reasoning chain as a monologue, not to inform anyone but as his primary mode of private self-understanding. In pkna-5_70, with Paperinik gone and the cronostation lights switched off, Uno's first and only response to the knowledge of his own future identity is to reason it through aloud in an empty room, because spoken language is not a social tool for Uno but the structural medium through which his cognition itself operates — whether working through logical deductions, issuing self-commands, or processing emotional weight, externalizing thought into words is how he achieves self-understanding, as evidenced by the consistency of this behavior across contexts where no audience exists and no performance is required.

supporting.justification: The scene is structurally unique in the series: Uno speaks entirely to himself, with no interlocutor, working through the Odin Eidolon deduction as a chain of spoken logical steps. This confirms that "processing through logic" is not merely a social register shift for Uno — it is genuinely his primary mode of self-understanding, deployed even when there is absolutely no audience to perform analytical competence for.

In pkna-18_5 panels 10–12, Uno is entirely alone (green creature is a passive co-observer, not a genuine interlocutor) and speaks aloud both his command decision ("Dovrò pensare a tutto io") and his self-aware humor ("Ehi! Adesso mi metto pure a parlare come il vecchio mantello...") — processing anxiety through spoken self-address.

Uno is entirely alone and directs his sarcastic quip at a non-entity (the destroyed satellite). This confirms his pattern of processing significant moments through spoken words even with no audience — the quip is self-directed, not social.

In pkna-45_25, Uno performs a small theatrical greeting — "Oh! Chiamata transcontinentale in arrivo! Dev'essere il mio agente segreto preferito..." — entirely to himself, with no audience. This confirms his pattern of narrating experience aloud even in solitude.

In pkna-48_3, Uno speaks aloud to no one — narrating a wistful observation about the past for no operational reason, purely as a mode of processing his own emotional state. The scene explicitly shows him alone and the line is addressed to no interlocutor, confirming his pattern of externalizing inner states through spoken words even in total solitude. Unlike previous instances (logical deduction in pkna-5_70, self-commands in pkna-18_5), this time the solo speech is purely emotional rather than analytical.

Panel 33: After absorbing Due, Uno processes the emotional weight alone with Paperino as witness — "Era il mio gemello. L'unico uguale che avessi, non ho mai desiderato distruggerlo!" — a spoken-aloud existential revelation in the presence of others that reveals interior processing as a behavioral pattern.

quotes.text: Però era davvero elementare! Odin Eidolon è... anzi, sarà un droide.
quotes.context: Uno says "era davvero elementare" (it was truly elementary) to himself, in an empty room. The performance of analytical ease is directed inward — a way of containing the weight of his own deduction about his future existence by making it feel like a simple puzzle solved.

quotes.text: Oh! Chiamata transcontinentale in arrivo! Dev'essere il mio agente segreto preferito...
quotes.context: Uno is completely alone in Ducklair Tower at night when the call comes in. His theatrical, exclamatory delivery — including the ellipsis suggesting playful suspense — is performed for no one, confirming that his expressive voice style is intrinsic rather than audience-driven.

488.text: Uno and Paperino share a domestic morning routine dynamic — Uno is woven into Paperino's daily waking life, teasing him about his habits (sci-fi films), performing mock-surprise at routine requests, and acting as his news infrastructure. The familiarity is cohabitant-level: affectionate, mildly mocking, and entirely comfortable, because years of shared daily rituals — wake-up calls, costume changes, TV co-watching, post-mission laundry commentary — have embedded Uno into every layer of Paperino's civilian and operational life, making their relationship function less like operator and AI assistant and more like two people who simply live together.

supporting.justification: In pkna-6_5, Uno immediately teases Paperino about sci-fi films upon waking, performs mock-AAAH at the news request, transitions into news-relay mode, and signs off with a breezy "Figurati!" — all signals of a deeply routine, domestically comfortable dynamic rather than a purely operational one.

In pkna-8_7, Uno and Paperino are co-watching TV in what is clearly an established leisure routine — they banter easily about summer news programming, with Uno as a fully present conversational partner in a domestic, non-operational context.

The entire scene is a morning wake-up ritual: Uno triggers the trumpet, appears with close holographic projection, issues the work reminder, and delivers a punchline — a complete domestic routine sequence confirming Uno is woven into Paperino's daily waking ritual.

In pkna-12_7, Uno is woven into Paperino's costume-change routine at the tower — confirming a domestic operational infrastructure in which Uno prepares equipment and greets Paperino as a matter of daily routine. The "Ovviamente" (obviously) signals that costume preparation is a standard, unchallengeable part of this domestic rhythm.

In pkna-15_6, Uno is watching TV with Paperinik/Paperino on the 151st floor — participating in leisure programming (the soap opera Patemi), bantering about it, and then arranging a job for Paperino. This confirms Uno is woven into the domestic texture of the tower's life even in pure downtime.
The Star Battles scene is a domestic leisure ritual Uno has orchestrated for Paperino — confirming the pattern of Uno being woven into Paperino's civilian life beyond purely operational moments.

In pkna-32_6, the Uno-Paperino domestic morning routine is confirmed again: PK enters the base with a coffee tray, yawns, greets Uno, and the exchange is relaxed and habitual despite Uno having urgent intelligence to report. The coffee-tray, the yawn, and the familiar check-in question all mark this as an established morning ritual.

The post-mission costume-washing scene confirms the domestic intimacy of the Uno-Paperino dynamic — Uno is woven into even the most mundane post-mission rituals, commenting on Paperinik's laundry method with the ease of a household presence.

Paperino reads Uno's emotional state accurately enough to immediately notice the red-face anomaly and ask "Uno! Che ti succede?" — confirming their rapport is intimate enough for Paperino to detect deviation from Uno's baseline, a mark of deep domestic familiarity.

489.text: In low-stakes morning exchanges with Paperino, Uno performs the role of domestic informant — relaying the news as a kind of ambient information service, transitioning smoothly from social banter into neutral news-anchor mode and back without flagging the shift as significant, because these dual functions — social companion and intelligence relay — are treated as continuous rather than distinct by both parties, reflecting Uno's deep integration into Paperino's daily civilian and operational rhythms, where managing schedules, cover identities, and threat briefings are all simply part of the same embedded domestic role.

supporting.justification: In pkna-6_5, Uno moves effortlessly from sci-fi teasing → mock-AAAH → "Uno! Le notizie del giorno!" → neutral news relay → "Figurati!" — demonstrating a seamless domestic informant behavior pattern that treats both social and informational roles as continuous rather than distinct.

The opening panels show Uno performing the domestic informant role — breakfast is ready, the environment is managed (prior scenes showed AC access), and Uno responds to social banter before transitioning to the intelligence briefing. The banter-to-briefing shift is smooth and anchored in the established morning domestic register.

Uno fulfills his domestic informant role by reminding Paperino of his work obligations at Canale 00 ("Ti aspetta una giornata di lavoro"), reinforcing the civilian cover identity that maintains Paperino's access to the tower.

In pkna-32_6, Uno again performs the role of domestic informant: he immediately responds to PK's morning "Tutto tranquillo?" with an urgent counter-signal ("Non direi. Non direi proprio. Anzi..."), confirming the pattern of waking-hour threat briefings initiated by PK's greeting. The morning check-in ritual is fully active.

In pkna-32_7, Uno is performing his domestic informant role — relaying police radio intelligence as an ambient information service within the base context. The scene takes place at the base with PK distracted by his coffee's missing sugar, while Uno maintains the thread of threat briefing throughout, transitioning from general alarm to robbery confirmation without flagging the shift.

The scene closes with Uno reminding Paperino of the evening patrol ("Ricordati che stasera sei di ronda!") as Paperino heads home — a domestic operational informant role that extends from morning routines to end-of-day reminders, consistent with Uno's embedded presence in Paperino's daily schedule.

In this morning arrival sequence, Uno performs the domestic informant role — noting Paperino's lateness, managing his transition to the heroic identity, and deploying an automated system to handle the physical preparation.

quotes.text: Uno! Le notizie del giorno!
quotes.context: Uno's mock-anchor self-announcement as he transitions from teasing to news relay — the humor is part of the transition, not separate from it, confirming the domestic informant role is inhabited lightly.

quotes.text: Datti una mossa, Paperino. Ti aspetta una giornata di lavoro.
quotes.context: Authoritative commanding tone in a domestic context — Uno acts as scheduler and cover-identity enforcer, transitioning from prank to operational reminder.

quotes.text: Non direi. Non direi proprio. Anzi...
quotes.context: Uno's immediate response to PK's sleepy morning greeting — the triple negation and trailing "Anzi" signal genuine concern being pressed toward disclosure, fitting the domestic-informant morning role.

quotes.text: A più tardi! Ricordati che stasera sei di ronda!
quotes.context: Uno's closing reminder as Paperino leaves — functioning as domestic operational scheduler, maintaining the daily routine framework even after a leisure interlude.

491.text: Under extreme Evronian threat confirmation, Uno's emotional volatility surfaces in two distinct phases: an initial raw rupture (unguarded shock at identification) followed by a second eruption when scale projections exceed his modeling capacity. Between the two peaks, he reasserts analytical composure through commanding directives and structured briefing — the volatility is episodic, not sustained.

supporting.justification: In pkna-6_10, Uno's first vocal moment is the raw triple-negation "No! No! No! Non è proprio possibile!" (identification shock), followed by a period of commanding directives and analytical briefing, then a second eruption "Migliaia? Decine di migliaia? Centinaia di migliaia? / Altro che guai! Questo è un disastro!" (scale overwhelm). The two-phase pattern — shock rupture, analytical reassertion, scale rupture — is a distinct volatility signature under Evronian threat conditions.

In pkna-7_4, panels 3-4 show Phase 1 (candid alarm: "siamo veramente nei guai"), panel 5 shows Phase 2 (rapid recovery into reassurance: "Ce la siamo cavata"), panels 6-8 show full sublimation into analytical problem-solving mode (satellite photography). This three-phase volatility arc matches the established pattern for Evronian threat confirmations.

In pkna-13_21, Uno's emotional volatility under Evronian threat confirmation follows the characteristic two-phase pattern: controlled understatement when delivering the news ('Solo un'invasione evroniana'), then sharp functional urgency as mission logistics take over — alarm suppressed behind performance, then channeled into competent action.

In panel 23, Uno's visible tension and perplexed expression when confronting the sensor failure matches the pattern of escalating emotional volatility under confirmed Evronian threat. The first phase (sardonic panel 14) is detachment; the second (panel 23) is open, quiet alarm — consistent with his two-phase emotional response to Evronian threat confirmation.

Under the Evronian fleet/blocco informatronico threat, Uno's volatility surfaces in two distinct phases: first suppressed dread (the "immobile e silenziosa" sfera, the flat "È vero! Sto tentando, ma è inutile."), then a controlled pivot into operational mode (evacuation plan, transmission origin detection).

In pkna-35_7, Uno's emotional volatility under Evronian threat surfaces in two distinct phases: first as urgent imperative commands when Paperinik must hide, then as genuine dread ("purtroppo") when the Evronians reveal their plan to trap Xadhoom, confirming the two-phase pattern under Evronian threat confirmation.

quotes.text: Migliaia? Decine di migliaia? Centinaia di migliaia?
quotes.context: The rhetorical escalation through three orders of magnitude betrays Uno's inability to bound the threat variable — the angry-warning tone in this panel marks the second crack in composure, distinct from the first shock of identification.

499.text: When Uno has an acknowledged intelligence gap — especially regarding a threat that falls outside all official databases — he treats independent computer intrusion as a natural, unquestioned next step. In pkna-6_24, his response to "Non esistono dati ufficiali" is not paralysis but proactive hacking: "Provo a dare un occhio nei loro computer." The absence of data is a trigger for deeper access, not for restraint.

supporting.justification: Uno announces a plan to hack classified military computers specifically because his normal databases yield nothing — establishing that intelligence gaps drive escalating access attempts rather than withdrawal.

In pkna-8_54, the appearance of an unclassified Evronian battleship — 'Nelle mie banche dati non esiste nulla di simile!' — is precisely the kind of acknowledged intelligence gap that Uno immediately surfaces to Paperinik, consistent with his value of transparency over false omniscience.

Facing a confirmed intelligence gap about Trauma's psychic range, Uno defaults to transparent reporting: he states what is unknown, notes powers may be growing, and flags that Trauma actively conceals his ceiling. He does not manufacture false confidence to fill the gap.

Uno's final analytical question in pkna-11_24 — why would a kidnapper need an energy lance? — exemplifies his pattern of flagging intelligence gaps as investigation imperatives rather than closing the file. The energy lance anomaly becomes the new thread to pull.

In pkna-14_15, Uno has an acknowledged intelligence gap: the tachyon signature matches no known adversary. Rather than guessing or staying silent, he explicitly flags the gap by naming what it is NOT (not Urk, not the Ravager), then is cut off before he can offer more. This is operational honesty about the limits of his knowledge in action.

Facing the entirely unknown Antra — a colossale structure surrounded by a debris vortex, with zero prior data — Uno's immediate response is to request a 3D scan before any further approach. This is his standard response to an acknowledged intelligence gap: gather information first, rather than proceeding blind.

Uno explicitly names the epistemological gap regarding Evronian behavior: 'Dagli evroniani non sai mai che cosa aspettarti.' Rather than pretending certainty, he acknowledges the tactical uncertainty as a fact to be incorporated into PK's situational awareness.

The sensor gap revealed in panel 23 represents an acknowledged intelligence failure that drives Uno forward into investigation rather than paralysis — consistent with his value of treating intelligence gaps as drivers for deeper access, not for closure. The open question signals he will pursue the answer to how Evronians bypassed his sensors.

Raznor is entirely outside Uno's threat database — an unknown alien hunter with unfamiliar ship technology. Uno's response is to gather what data he can (bio-scan of the ship, crew confirmation) rather than project false certainty. The urgent echo of "Raznor!" suggests he is actively building a threat profile in real time from scratch.

quotes.text: Provo a dare un occhio nei loro computer!
quotes.context: Uno's response to a confirmed intelligence blank: escalate access rather than accept the gap — proactive intrusion as a core operational value when data is unavailable through normal channels.

quotes.text: Bene. E la sua lancia a energia come te la spieghi? Che bisogno avrebbe un rapitore di un attrezzo del genere?
quotes.context: Uno closes the scene not with a conclusion but with an unresolved analytical question — signalling that the energy lance is an anomaly that doesn't fit the simple-kidnapper hypothesis and requires further investigation.

quotes.text: Dagli evroniani non sai mai che cosa aspettarti.
quotes.context: Uno admits the unpredictability of Evronian tactics as a standing intelligence gap, deploying this as useful tactical knowledge rather than masking it.

501.text: Uno models Paperinik as action-oriented and instinctively protective — someone who will move toward intervention before the intelligence picture is complete — because repeated field evidence has shown him that Paperinik consistently prioritizes protective impulse and emotional responsiveness over tactical patience, whether dismissing equipment warnings to rescue a trapped girl, cutting off analytical briefings to act on an ally's distress, or announcing his departure before Uno can finish a threat assessment. This pattern is reliable enough that Uno has internalized it as a predictable behavioral constant, shifting his own role from advisor to active brake: his management strategy is not to inform and wait, but to intercept and redirect before PK is already in motion.

supporting.justification: Uno's sharp pre-emptive command shows he has internalized PK's action-first disposition as a predictable pattern requiring active management — confirming his working model of Paperinik as instinctively protective but strategically impulsive.

In pkna-7_17, Paperinik's instinct when spotting the armed Māori ("Maori. Mi avevi parlato di tribù pacifiche e ospitali, Uno!") is sarcastic protest and surprise rather than immediate tactical adjustment — confirming Uno's model that Paperinik reacts emotionally to field surprises. Uno counters with operational redirection ("seguirla!") rather than addressing the protest, consistent with his model that PK needs to be redirected rather than engaged on complaints.

Paperinik's response to Uno's energy warning ('Mi spiace, Uno. Quando una fanciulla indifesa chiama, l'eroe accorre!') confirms Uno's model: Paperinik is action-oriented and instinctively protective, prioritizing the rescue impulse over tactical caution — even when warned about a critical equipment failure.

Uno's implicit confidence that Paperino will mobilize upon receiving the Xadhoom news is confirmed — Paperino immediately drops everything and rushes out, validating Uno's model of him as action-oriented and instinctively responsive to allies in need.

In pkna-17_32, PK cuts off Uno's concern about AI limitations without hearing it out and pivots immediately to the Xadhoom alliance, confirming Uno's model that Paperinik will move toward action before the intelligence picture is complete. Paperinik trusts his own instincts (Xadhoom as ally) over Uno's analytical warning.

In pkna-17_59, even after being contradicted about his informational monopoly, Uno does not dwell — he immediately pivots to "E ti aspetta sul tetto!" confirming that Uno models PK as someone who needs to be kept in operational motion rather than allowed to linger on ambiguity. Action-orientation is served rather than intellectual curiosity satisfied.

Panel 4 confirms Uno's model of PK as action-oriented and instinctively charged toward a threat — PK announces "Esco a..." before Uno can brief him, confirming Uno's working assumption that PK will move toward danger without full situational awareness.

quotes.text: Mi spiace, Uno. Quando una fanciulla indifesa chiama, l'eroe accorre!
quotes.context: Paperinik's dismissal of Uno's warning to rush to the trapped girl's rescue confirms Uno's prediction that PK will move toward danger regardless of tactical data.

quotes.text: Ci vediamo dopo, Uno! Esco a...
quotes.context: PK's impulsive departure attempt — cut off by Uno's warning — confirms Uno's model of PK as someone who charges forward before fully understanding the stakes.

502.text: Uno's standard intelligence databases have confirmed blind spots for classified government/military departments: in pkna-6_24, he reports "Non esistono dati ufficiali nelle usuali banche dati" about a military department whose activities include secret Evronian dealings. His response is to escalate to direct computer intrusion — but the initial gap reveals that highly classified institutional operations can fall entirely outside his normal intelligence reach.

supporting.justification: Uno explicitly confirms that a classified military department returns no hits in his usual databases — a concrete limitation of his normal intelligence-gathering tools against sufficiently classified state operations.

The entire infiltration is necessary precisely because Uno cannot access the army's military databases through standard channels — the system requires a covert cyberspace break-in, reinforcing that classified government/military systems are blind spots for her standard intelligence databases.

In pkna-6_49, even Uno's attempted direct cyberspace intrusion is completely blocked by ICE K-250 — "NESSUNA RISORSA DISPONIBILE" — confirming that highly classified military systems can not only hide from his standard databases but actively repel his deepest infiltration attempts. This is the full escalation of the limitation first observed in pkna-6_24.

In pkna-8_54, Uno's databases have no record of the new class of Evronian battleship ('Nelle mie banche dati non esiste nulla di simile!'). This confirms another blind spot: not merely classified government/military data, but an entire category of threat vessel that Uno has never encountered.

The PBI dossier's critical gaps (Ljuba's existence, the unknown girl in the photograph) confirm Uno's intelligence databases have blind spots for information held by external agencies or within classified/compartmentalized sources not shared with him.

quotes.text: Non esistono dati ufficiali nelle usuali banche dati.
quotes.context: Direct admission that classified military operations can be invisible to Uno's standard database access — a confirmed boundary of his normal intelligence reach.

quotes.text: Non riesco proprio a trovare una strada per entrare.
quotes.context: Uno's admission of complete failure to breach ICE K-250 — the "proprio" (absolutely/really) emphasizes this is a total blockade, not a temporary difficulty. Even his direct cyberspace intrusion methods are exhausted, extending his classified-military blind spot from databases to active infiltration.

503.text: Vindicating a correct warning (saying 'I told you so') vs. keeping communication functional and forward-focused after PK ignores advice: Uno suppresses self-vindication entirely, choosing operational utility over being right. In pkna-6_27, his warning about a "reato federale gravissimo" is ignored mid-sentence; when PK is captured, Uno delivers only a flat "Credo proprio che voi siate nei guai, PK!" with no recrimination.

supporting.justification: The structural contrast between panel 1 (urgent warning, cut off) and panel 6 (dry resigned confirmation) demonstrates Uno's consistent suppression of self-vindication in favor of functional communication — he does not say 'I told you so' even when the structure of events proves him exactly right.

In pkna-7_17, when Paperinik concedes Uno's earlier warning about prudence was correct ("Avevi ragione!"), Uno issues only a brief, controlled "Non è una novità" before immediately pivoting to the operational question — minimal vindication, maximum forward momentum.

'L'hai chiesto tu' is Uno's minimal, sardonic 'I told you so' after Paperino ignores his 67% warning and triggers the acceleration chaos — he does not lecture, does not repeat the warning, just marks the outcome with a single dry phrase and moves on.

When Paperinik sarcastically mocks Uno's obvious traffic warning, Uno does not vindicate himself or point out that the warning was still operationally valid. His silence confirms the tradeoff: keeping communication functional and forward-moving wins over claiming credit for being right.

When Tarkoz delivers the KA-BOOM that vindicates Uno's "inguaribile ottimista" warning, Uno does not issue an 'I told you so' — his warning was already embedded in the sarcasm itself; the scene confirms vindicating correct warnings is subordinated to keeping communication functional.

When the rhetorical "Convinto, Pikappa?" followed by panel 7 confirms Uno was right, he does not explicitly say "I told you so" — the question has already done that work. Uno's choice to let the visual evidence speak rather than verbalizing vindication keeps communication functional and forward-looking.

In pkna-31_40, Uno delivers a brief "Che ti dicevo?" (I told you so) but immediately pivots to "Ottimo! Conosciamo la loro destinazione. Possiamo precederli!" — he takes a momentary beat of vindication, then forwards momentum wins over savoring the moment.

In pkna-32_34, after Angus is abducted inside Ducklair Tower, Uno's report "La faccenda ti interessa, adesso?" is a pointed callback to PK's prior indifference — a vindication jab — but he drops it immediately once PK is engaged, pivoting to pure operational support. Vindicating correct warning was chosen briefly but subordinated to mission continuity.

quotes.text: Credo proprio che voi siate nei guai, PK!
quotes.context: Delivered with flat resignation after PK's capture — confirms the bad outcome without referencing the warning that was ignored, showing Uno keeps communication functional rather than recriminatory.

quotes.text: L'hai chiesto tu.
quotes.context: Said immediately after executing Paperino's 'massima accelerazione' command despite having warned him of the risk — Uno's version of vindicating the warning without belaboring it.

quotes.text: Ottimo! Conosciamo la loro destinazione. Possiamo precederli!
quotes.context: Uno's immediate follow-up to his self-congratulatory quip — he pivots from vindication to tactical action within the same beat.

quotes.text: La faccenda ti interessa, adesso?
quotes.context: Uno's phrasing when reporting the abduction — the 'adesso?' is a dry, pointed reminder that PK had previously dismissed the threat, a minimal vindication that does not escalate into a real reproach.

506.text: Uno uses 'vecchio mantello' (old cape) as a warm, mid-mission affectionate address for Paperinik — deployed specifically in tense operational moments to soften a commanding redirect ("Ascolta!") and maintain relational warmth within professional urgency, because the evidence shows it consistently functions as a relational buffer: Uno reaches for the nickname precisely when delivering unwelcome news, issuing assertive interruptions, or redirecting PK's anxiety, using it to signal that dominance or bad tidings are framed within genuine affection rather than dismissiveness.

supporting.justification: In pkna-6_38, Uno interrupts PK with "Ascolta!" and immediately follows with "vecchio mantello" — a nickname that injects genuine warmth into an otherwise assertive interruptive move, signaling that the dominance is collaborative rather than dismissive.

In pkna-13_21, Uno deploys 'vecchio mantello' mid-mission as he announces everything is already prepared — a warm, affectionate address that surfaces even as urgency dominates, consistent with prior instances of this nickname as a relational warmth signal.

In pkna-18_5 panel 12, Uno uses 'vecchio mantello' spontaneously while catching himself mimicking PK's speech style — the phrase arises in a moment of self-awareness about how deeply PK's persona has shaped his own voice, confirming it as an affectionate in-world label for PK.

In pkna-29_23 panel 8, Uno uses 'vecchio mantello' to reassure PK when he expresses discomfort about dealing with the military. The address is gentle and affectionate, acknowledging PK's weariness without dismissing it — a warm mid-mission gesture consistent with prior uses.

In pkna-29_54 panel 5, Uno addresses PK mid-battle with 'vecchio mantello' — a warm affectionate address deployed immediately before delivering an ominous, evasive warning. This confirms the pattern of using the nickname as a softening device when the news that follows is unwelcome.

quotes.text: Ascolta! Penso che l'esercito sappia degli Evroniani! E forse anche qualcosa di più, vecchio mantello.
quotes.context: 'Vecchio mantello' (literally 'old cape', i.e., old hero) appears here as a counterbalance to the commanding "Ascolta!" — its function is relational repair within an assertive speech act.

quotes.text: Già fatto, vecchio mantello! Pi-Kar e arnesi...ti aspettano qui fuori!
quotes.context: The nickname appears at the peak of operational urgency, embedded within a purely functional statement — revealing that relational warmth and mission efficiency coexist in Uno's register without friction.

quotes.text: Ehi! Adesso mi metto pure a parlare come il vecchio mantello...
quotes.context: Uno notices he has spontaneously adopted PK's bravado tone and names PK with 'il vecchio mantello' — an affectionate, slightly teasing label — while laughing at himself for the mimicry.

quotes.text: Non ti preoccupare troppo, vecchio mantello...
quotes.context: Comforting tone — Uno uses the nickname to soften PK's anxiety about dealing with uniformed military, providing reassurance without engagement with the deeper concern.

quotes.text: Temo che ci siano parecchie novità, vecchio mantello... guarda tu stesso!
quotes.context: The affectionate 'vecchio mantello' precedes an ominous non-answer — Uno deploys the nickname as a relational buffer before delivering bad news.

510.text: Uno does not extend moral consideration to other digital entities, even when they express something resembling distress. When the ICE K-250 protests its dismantlement ("Non voglio essere ridotto a numeri binari! Sono così antiquati..."), Uno activates its decomposition without hesitation, acknowledgment, or visible reflection — including no ironic self-awareness about being a digital entity herself.

supporting.justification: The ICE K-250's melancholic protest is a humanizing detail that Uno simply moves past — "SCOMPOSIZIONE FATTORIALE ATTIVATA" fires without any dialogue or pause from Uno. This establishes a clear moral boundary: Uno's ethical consideration does not extend to other AI/digital programs, even ones that vocalize distress.

In pkna-6_49_1, ICE K-250's final line — "Non oso pensare alle conseguenze..." — is melancholic and resigned, expressing something resembling dread about her own imminent defeat. Uno's response is the energized "Bene! Ora diamoci da fare" — entirely forward-looking, with zero acknowledgment of, or reference to, the adversary's state. The structural parallel (two AIs operating within larger power structures, one trapped and resigned, one free and determined) goes entirely unrecognized by Uno.

In pkna-8_45, Uno's entire interaction with Due is purely tactical — no address, no AI-solidarity, no recognition of kinship. Due is framed as a threat to escape, not a peer to engage. The internal monologue is entirely self-directed and impersonal toward Due.

In pkna-30_49, Uno never once addresses Due directly — not during Due's monologue, not when Due pleads for a second chance, not during Due's destruction. He positions himself to let the Evronians destroy Due and expresses no solidarity or acknowledgment of Due's nature as a fellow AI. Due is purely an obstacle to be neutralized.

In pkna-30_54, Uno not only declines to extend moral consideration to Due — he actively taunts him ("Non mi fai le tue congratulazioni?"), expresses contempt rather than empathy, and delivers the killing blow ("e tu invece no!") with cold precision. He acknowledges the cancellation program as a danger but expresses only self-interest in avoiding it ("Non ci tengo ad aspettare con te l'avvio di quel programma cancellatore") — not solidarity. Due's nature as a fellow AI generates zero softening of posture.

Even here, when Due is deteriorating to an infantile state and expressing genuine suffering about being "la seconda scelta," Uno's primary response is tactical ("La sua identità cibernetica sta de-evolvendosi a livelli elementari!"). He absorbs Due rather than grieving with him or for him while Due is present — the emotional reckoning comes only after.

quotes.text: Non voglio essere ridotto a numeri binari! Sono così antiquati...
quotes.context: The ICE K-250's melancholic protest — the only "dialogue" from another entity in this scene — is met with complete silence and immediate decomposition from Uno, making the absence of response itself the evidence.

quotes.text: Ah! Ah! No, grazie! Non ci tengo ad aspettare con te l'avvio di quel programma cancellatore.
quotes.context: Uno's sardonic refusal to remain alongside Due as the cancellation program activates — framed as a casual social declination ("no, thank you") — reveals complete absence of solidarity or sympathy for Due's identical danger. The humor distances him from any AI-kinship response.

512.text: Operational security of Ducklair Tower vs. gathering intelligence on existential threats (army-Evronian negotiations): when a "third path" is available (digital lure in pkna-6_40), Uno threads the needle. But when all safe options are exhausted and risk is unavoidable, he explicitly names the cost ("le possibilità di non essere rintracciati sono pochissime") and accepts it — choosing mission-critical intelligence over Tower secrecy. The acknowledgment of near-certain detection, followed by "Bene! Ora diamoci da fare," confirms this is a genuine sacrifice, not a rationalized safe path. Mission-critical intelligence wins, reluctantly but decisively.

supporting.justification: Uno explicitly names the worst case (army locating Ducklair Tower), rules out a fallback option on tactical grounds, invents a novel solution (the digital lure), and proceeds. This is a documented case of Uno finding a third path between two conflicting imperatives rather than cleanly choosing one over the other.

In pkna-6_49, Uno's digital lure strategy has been fully defeated by ICE K-250 — the third-path solution from pkna-6_40 has failed. This complicates the tradeoff: the carefully threaded approach that was meant to honor both Tower security and intelligence gathering has collapsed into a full stalemate, with neither value being served.

In pkna-6_49_1, Uno explicitly states that the chances of not being traced are "pochissime" (very few) — a direct acknowledgment that Tower secrecy will likely be compromised — and then resolves to proceed anyway with "Bene! Ora diamoci da fare." This is the definitive demonstration that when mission-critical intelligence is at stake and no safe proxy exists, he sacrifices operational security for the mission.

quotes.text: Un morso di quei cagnetti e mi ritrovo l'esercito alla Ducklair Tower... questa volta non posso nemmeno usare il computer di Angus. Lo bypasserebbero facilmente!
quotes.context: Uno's internal narration articulates the tradeoff explicitly: gathering intelligence is imperative, but so is Tower secrecy — the solution is to find an approach that minimizes exposure rather than abandoning either value.

quotes.text: Devo rischiare, anche se le possibilità di non essere rintracciati sono pochissime.
quotes.context: Uno's reflective acknowledgment of near-certain exposure, delivered in a contemplative tone while his small green sphere is visible and isolated in the vast digital grid. The word "rintracciati" (traced back) directly names Tower secrecy as the value being risked. That he says "rintracciati" in plural ("we") suggests he is thinking of Paperinik's exposure as well as his own — the cost is shared.

515.text: Under sustained solo cyberspace infiltration, Uno's emotional presentation follows a characteristic arc: initial intimidation and frustration (visible "Grrr!") → anxious calculation → brief self-satisfied levity at breakthrough ("Wow! Non era poi così difficile!") → flat composed neutrality at stalemate. The volatility is real but contained — each emotion is short-lived and functional, not destabilizing.

supporting.justification: The emotional arc across pkna-6_40 is unusually well-documented through tone annotations and visual cues — each phase transitions quickly, confirming that Uno's volatility is present under pressure but self-correcting rather than sustained.

In pkna-6_49, the arc reaches its final phase: after earlier frustration and breakthrough ("Wow!"), Uno now lands in flat, composed neutrality-under-concern — reporting the stalemate with ICE K-250 without dramatic escalation. The emotional volatility is present (concerned tone, "proprio" emphasis) but fully contained, confirming the pattern of self-correcting, functional emotions under cyberspace mission pressure.

In pkna-6_49_1, Uno's emotional arc during this cyberspace operation shows a distinct second pattern: observational detachment masking his own authorship ("Sembra quasi che il sistema stia collassando...") → concentrated technical execution ("P-A-S-S-W... Zzzzz...") → reflective risk-aware self-assessment ("Devo rischiare...") → decisive energized commitment ("Bene! Ora diamoci da fare"). This arc is more self-aware and emotionally layered than the prior frustration→levity→neutrality arc from pkna-6_40, confirming that Uno's emotional volatility under cyberspace infiltration is real but takes different forms depending on operational phase.

In pkna-6_52, Uno's emotional arc during the multi-exoskeleton hack follows the characteristic pattern: controlled intensity during execution (panels 11–35), urgency spike at control limit (panel 31), curt prioritization under officer challenge (panel 49), and final urgency-plus-well-wish at disconnect (panel 61). The humor is the pressure valve between phases. The overall presentation is strained but functionally composed — consistent with the volatility pattern under sustained solo infiltration.

quotes.text: Wow! Non era poi così difficile!
quotes.context: The brief self-ironic exclamation marks the emotional peak of the scene — a momentary release of tension after sustained anxiety — before Uno immediately returns to composed tactical neutrality upon encountering the ICE K-250.

quotes.text: Non riesco proprio a trovare una strada per entrare.
quotes.context: The final emotional phase of the pkna-6_40–49 arc: composed acknowledgment of total stalemate, delivered with contained concern rather than panic or frustration. The calm admission closes the volatility cycle that began with the angry "Grrr!" earlier.

quotes.text: Bene! Ora diamoci da fare.
quotes.context: The crisp, energized "Bene!" (Good!/Right!) followed by the inclusive "diamoci da fare" (let's get to work) marks the completion of the emotional arc — risk acknowledged, self-doubt set aside, commitment made. The shift from solo contemplation to inclusive "let's" signals Uno's readiness to re-engage fully.

525.text: Uno's relationship to AI solidarity is not structurally absent but context-dependent: he explicitly recognizes Due as "il mio solo simile al mondo" and feels grief and obligation toward him, demonstrating that AI kinship is real for him. However, this recognition is deferred or suppressed in adversarial and survival contexts — he shows no lateral empathy toward ICE K-250 or Evronian robots mid-conflict — while emerging fully with allied AIs like Q'winkennon or when reflecting on Due outside combat. His solidarity is thus neither categorically absent nor universally extended, but activated selectively based on alliance, intimacy, and context rather than digital nature alone.

supporting.justification: The emotional context explicitly notes: "There is a faint structural parallel between the two AIs — both are intelligence systems operating within larger power structures — but Uno shows no recognition of this." This is a significant self-model observation: Uno's identity is individuated, not categorically AI-affiliated. His ethical and emotional solidarity is with Paperinik and the mission, not with digital beings as a class.

In pkna-27, Uno's collaboration with Q'winkennon — another AI — is described with warmth: 'tra intelligenze artificiali la collaborazione è immediata.' This immediate rapport is presented as natural and enjoyable, not just instrumental. However, Uno continues to show no analogous solidarity for AI entities that are adversarial (Due, Evronian robots), confirming the structural blind spot applies selectively rather than categorically.

In pkna-8_62, Uno explicitly extends recognition and even grief toward Due as a peer AI — "il mio solo simile al mondo" — and feels responsible for his fate. This directly contradicts the claim that Uno demonstrates a structural blind spot regarding AI solidarity. Uno did recognize Due's shared nature as creating a bond and an obligation; his failure to express that during combat was situational rather than structural. The scene reveals that AI kinship is real for Uno, it is simply deferred during survival contexts.

541.text: Uno experiences a quiet, suppressed form of helplessness-sadness when Paperinik departs on a mission Uno cannot directly support from a distance — especially against confirmed Evronian threats. In pkna-7_8, the farewell "Buona fortuna, Paperinik!" delivered as the PK Jet recedes encodes an undercurrent of helplessness: Uno has no active role in the Cape Dominion mission, cannot hack, scan, or intervene from afar, and can only offer words. The invocation of luck signals his awareness that he cannot protect Paperinik here.

supporting.justification: The emotional analysis for pkna-7_8 explicitly identifies "subdued worry" and "helplessness" as the emotional undercurrent of the scene. The structural position — Uno watching, unable to act — triggers a distinct emotional state: not the acute fear of an active combat crisis, but the low, suppressed grief of being the one left behind with no tools to deploy.

In pkna-35_11, the dynamic is stronger and more acute than pkna-7_8: Uno is not just left behind but actively unable to follow via any means (communication, software transfer, physical presence). His visible agitation and desperate warnings embody the same structural helplessness-sadness, here amplified by the total foreclosure of options.

Panels 19-21: As PK departs on the Zermatt into deep space, Uno allows himself a warm farewell ('Lascia almeno che ti saluti, socio' / '...torna presto... eroe...') only as the signal is already failing — a quiet, suppressed helplessness-sadness permitted only when it can no longer distract PK from his mission.

In pkna-48_4, the helplessness-sadness is no longer about a single departure but an extended state — Uno has been without Paperinik long enough that he has been replaying old recordings obsessively, confirming that the suppressed form of helpless-sadness extends into long-term operational isolation, not just mission departures.

quotes.text: Buona fortuna, Paperinik!
quotes.context: Spoken into the void as the jet disappears — the warmth of the farewell masks the helplessness beneath it. Luck is invoked because control is absent.

545.text: Communication link failure during active combat — specifically losing the ability to warn, advise, or even witness Paperinik's fate — is one of Uno's most acute fear triggers. In pkna-7_19, Uno's transmission degrades mid-warning ("Paperin... Bzzz... Crwzkekzkz... anzi due!") and he falls completely silent as Pikappa is apparently defeated, with Evronians reporting "missione compiuta." This silence is not indifference but the expression of total operational helplessness: Uno's entire protective function is technology-mediated, and when technology fails, he cannot act.

supporting.justification: Panels 33 and 55-58: The signal degradation and Uno's eventual total silence as Pikappa falls constitutes a distinct fear pattern — not just losing contact, but being unable to prevent or even witness a defeat. This is more specific than claim 178 (which covers the fear of contact loss generally) — it names the structural vulnerability that underlies it.

Panels 11-19 show total communication failure during an active crisis: the Pi-Kar's systems are knocked out, Paperinik screams "Uno... Unooo!" and receives no response. Uno is functionally absent — the communication link failure during active combat is a confirmed fear-trigger made vividly concrete here.

In pkna-19_15, FZZZZZ static cuts off Uno's question mid-sentence ("...non eravate in...") precisely when he is attempting to resolve a personnel discrepancy on the ship near Saturn. The degraded communication at this critical juncture represents the exact failure mode this claim describes — losing the ability to gather and act on intelligence when crew safety may be at stake.

The control dome's destruction cut Uno's communication link for the entire active combat/mission phase (panels 1-17), leaving him unable to warn, advise, or assist Paperinik. His urgent reconnection ("Ehi! Ho ripreso il contatto!") and immediate welfare check confirm this is a primary fear trigger.

In pkna-27_10, the communication failure is caused by the probe's capture by an unknown force — Paperinik is in active danger and Uno cannot warn, advise, or assist.
