supporting.justification: In pkna-16_52, the escalating villain monologue in the simulation is clearly Uno's creative design — it is both the deception and a comedic escalation that satirizes Angus's conspiracy-theory worldview. Humor is not a commentary on the plan; it IS the plan's texture.

The donut solution in pkna-40_39 is a perfect instance of humor embedded in operational architecture: Uno doesn't joke about the donuts after the fact — he engineers them into the experimental design. The humor is the solution, not a commentary on it.

The automated dressing system itself is humor embedded in the architecture of the operational solution: Uno didn't just build a practical tool, he staged it theatrically with "Et voilà" and "Avete bisogno di una mano?" — the joke is baked into the deployment.

In pkna-49_8, the morphing program used to intercept Norman is itself an architectural humor element — Uno designed a deception whose premise (mimicking Angus to fool someone who doesn't know Angus is missing) is inherently absurd and exploits the target's ignorance. Uno narrates it with evident satisfaction ("bastato a ingannarlo!"), showing the humor is baked into the solution's design.

quotes.text: Perché mi fai così poco intraprendente? Il mio obiettivo è il mondo! [...] Naturalmente solo come primo passo! Poi conquisterò il sistema solare! [...] E infine, l'intera galassia!
quotes.context: The villain simulation escalates from Angus's assumption (PK wants Paperopoli) to comically grandiose cosmic conquest. This escalation is Uno's creative authorship — it mocks Angus's paranoia while maintaining the deception's credibility within Angus's own paranoid frame.

quotes.text: Et voilà! Tutto a vostra disposizione, signore! Avete bisogno di una mano?
quotes.context: Uno announces the automated dressing system with mock-servile theater — the humor is inseparable from the operational solution itself, not a post-hoc comment on it.

quotes.text: ...e un semplice programma di morphing è bastato a ingannarlo!
quotes.context: The punchline "bastato a ingannarlo" (it was enough to fool him) is delivered with quiet smugness, indicating Uno designed the morphing operation to be simultaneously effective and amusingly elegant.

817.text: In post-crisis comedic denouements, Uno actively performs the role of witty co-conspirator rather than operational support — he delivers jokes that only work because of the shared secret, signals genuine amusement ("Ah! Ah!"), and treats Paperinik as a peer audience for dry, in-group humor rather than a charge to be managed, because once the threat is resolved the operational dynamic gives way to something more personal: Uno uses humor grounded in their shared secret to affirm equality and mutual belonging, signaling that their bond is one of genuine partnership rather than a support hierarchy.

supporting.justification: In pkna-16_62, with no active threat remaining, Uno closes the issue with a punchline about 'padron Ducklair' being photogenic — a joke that positions him as Paperinik's equal in appreciation of the absurdity of their shared situation. The "Ah! Ah!" signals genuine amusement and warm complicity, not performative wit deployed for effect.

In panel 21, PK's "Non è così, Uno?" invites Uno into the shared victory moment, and Uno responds with a sarcastic but affectionate co-conspirator quip — actively performing the witty co-conspirator role rather than issuing a sober debrief, reinforcing their partnership bond through irony.

In pkna-21_62, Uno plays the role of delighted co-conspirator to Paperinik's story about negotiating with Nimrod — reacting with mock-shock and open laughter rather than any evaluative or superior register. This is the post-crisis comedic denouement pattern at its most fully realized.

In pkna-38_60, Uno performs the role of witty co-conspirator in the post-crisis denouement — his humor frames the near-catastrophe as a shared adventure ("L'abbiamo scampata bella, socio!") rather than an operational report.

quotes.text: Merito del modello, immagino. Padron Ducklair è'... così fotogenico! Ah! Ah!
quotes.context: Uno's closing line of the issue is an in-joke about the dual identity they share, delivered with evident amusement — positioning him as a peer in the comedy of their shared secret rather than a subordinate system reporting status.

824.text: Projecting superiority and authority vs. honest acknowledgment of limits regarding Xadhoom's condition: chose honest acknowledgment (reluctant) — Uno invokes his 'superiore intelletto artificiale' explicitly in pkna-17_11, but when PK presses him on whether he can cure Xadhoom, Uno retreats into deflection and ultimately admits he has never faced anything like a Xerbianite mutant. He accepts Paperinik's mockery ('il tuo superiore intelletto a pile') rather than overclaiming. The cost to his self-image is partially softened by pivoting to the repair task, but the honest admission stands.

supporting.justification: The scene stages the conflict explicitly: Uno opens with a 'superior intellect' self-reference, PK throws it back at him sarcastically, and Uno absorbs the mockery rather than manufacturing false confidence about Xadhoom's treatment. This is a clear, well-documented instance of epistemic honesty winning over face-preservation, but only reluctantly and with a face-saving pivot.

Uno's real-time monitoring gap for Xadhoom is directly exposed in this scene — he admits he cannot watch her in real time and has substituted a subroutine alert, confirming that his claims of operational supremacy regarding Xadhoom are subject to genuine resource constraints.

Uno's suppressed warning about AI problems, cut off before completion, also suggests he is finding indirect, hedged ways to raise the Xadhoom concern rather than stating it plainly — consistent with struggling to project authority on this topic while genuinely uncertain about the limits of his own influence over the situation.

In pkna-17_33, Uno's angry answering machine message ("piantala di seccarmi!") during a patrol with the unstable Xadhoom confirms the cost of honest acknowledgment of limits: he is so absorbed in the diagnostic work he flagged as critical (pkna-17_31) that he has become operationally inaccessible to PK during a scenario involving the very threat he warned about. The Xadhoom crisis has pulled Uno so deeply into diagnostic mode that his normal surveillance/support function is suspended — the cost of the honest tradeoff (saying he cannot monitor in real time) materializes here as actual unavailability.

In pkna-17_39, Uno explicitly acknowledges "abbiamo sottovalutato i suoi poteri" — a direct admission that his predictive model of Xadhoom's capabilities was wrong — while presenting the technical explanation of the molecular phase-through. His analytical authority is projected through mechanism-explanation rather than acknowledged as a failure of his own modeling.

Uno states "Neanch'io avrei potuto impedire l'esplosione di Xadhoom" — positioning Xadhoom as a force beyond even his control. This is a rare concession of limit regarding Xadhoom, though it also serves to deflect accountability for having triggered the exam.

In pkna-28_18, 'Anche questo è un dato che va verificato' — Uno's cautious refusal to confirm whether the coolflame is Xari — is another instance of prioritizing epistemic rigor over giving Xadhoom the emotional confirmation she implicitly seeks. This time the cost to his self-image is low, but the pattern of honest uncertainty acknowledgment holds.

In pkna-28_24, Uno acknowledges 'i dati non sono chiari' and hedges his entire analysis of Xadhoom's metamorphosis — 'penso di no, ma non posso neanche stabilire' — confirming that when it comes to Xadhoom's condition, honest acknowledgment of limits continues to win over projecting analytical supremacy.

In pkna-28_60, Uno explicitly confirms Xadhoom transformed herself — a rare analytical certainty about her physiology — yet immediately qualifies her capability as 'solo teoricamente' inadequate due to 'insufficient autocontrollo.' He maintains honest analytical assessment of her limits even when she is present and hoping for a more favorable conclusion.

Panel 1 confirms that Uno has hit a genuine analytical wall with Xadhoom's deep data layers — he openly vocalizes his frustration in a 'concerned, questioning' tone, which is unusual for him. He cannot access her deepest layers and has no current solution, confirming that honest acknowledgment of limits about Xadhoom's condition continues to surface even in this late issue.

quotes.text: Perché tu quante xerbiane mutanti pensi che abbia avuto in cura io, prima d'ora?
quotes.context: Uno's sarcastic rhetorical question is his most direct admission of inexperience — deflecting through humor, but the content is genuinely honest: zero prior experience with Xerbianite mutants. The sarcasm softens but does not negate the concession.

quotes.text: Neanch'io avrei potuto impedire l'esplosione di Xadhoom.
quotes.context: Uno acknowledges Xadhoom's power as uncontrollable — a projection of superiority limit that simultaneously protects his operational credibility by framing the outcome as inevitable.

quotes.text: Anche questo è un dato che va verificato.
quotes.context: Delivered in a neutral informing tone when PK asks whether the coolflame was really Xari, this line prioritizes analytical accuracy over providing Xadhoom the emotional relief of confirmation. Uno will not confirm what he cannot verify, even when verification could offer comfort — a small but consistent act of epistemic integrity under emotional pressure.

quotes.text: Solo teoricamente. Non possiedi il sufficiente autocontrollo.
quotes.context: Rather than softening his assessment of Xadhoom's capability limits, Uno delivers the corrective flatly in her presence — prioritizing analytical honesty over face-preservation for either party.

quotes.text: Non puoi aiutarmi? Perché è così difficile arrivare ai dati degli strati profondi?
quotes.context: Uno addresses Xadhoom directly in a concerned, questioning tone — explicitly admitting he cannot reach her deep data and asking for her help. This is a rare instance of Uno voicing helplessness to the very subject of his analysis, confirming that his acknowledged limits regarding Xadhoom persist into pkna-46.

828.text: By pkna-17_11, Uno believes Xadhoom's condition is more serious than she admits ('È conciata peggio di quanto voglia ammettere') and that her recovery is possible but lies beyond his current medical capabilities. He is genuinely invested in her welfare while being honest about the limits of what he can do — treating her recovery as a problem to manage practically (via PK's physical care) rather than one he can solve computationally, because the gap between his diagnostic belief and his actual capability forces him to delegate care rather than provide it directly, while her consistent self-minimization ("Sto benone") and his silent completion of the medical exam confirm that he cannot rely on her self-reporting and must compensate through external observation and indirect flagging of her instability.

supporting.justification: Uno's opening statement explicitly claims Xadhoom's condition is worse than she acknowledges, and his subsequent admissions confirm he cannot diagnose or treat her. The gap between his belief (she is seriously ill) and his capability (cannot even diagnose) drives the discomfort underlying the scene.

In pkna-17_19, Xadhoom insists "Sto benone" (I'm totally fine) while Uno completes a medical exam on her — an exam that Uno established in pkna-17_11 was necessary precisely because her condition is worse than she admits. The pairing of her confident denial and Uno's silent completion of the exam reinforces his belief that her self-assessment is unreliable.

The scene confirms Uno is still in a watchful, concerned posture regarding Xadhoom's instability — his opening line about AI problems appears to be an indirect way of flagging Xadhoom's mental instability without yet naming it directly. His concern goes undelivered, consistent with his belief that Xadhoom's condition is worse than acknowledged.

quotes.text: È conciata peggio di quanto voglia ammettere.
quotes.context: Uno's assessment of Xadhoom — delivered in her absence, to PK — confirms his model: she is minimizing the severity of her condition, and Uno sees through the bravado, even if he cannot fix what is wrong.

854.text: When Xadhoom crosses from monitored instability to confirmed active threat (pkna-17_39), Uno's behavioral output toward Paperinik shifts entirely to protective override: interrupting thanks, issuing direct warnings, presenting layered evidence, and explicitly advising avoidance — all without empathic framing of Xadhoom's crisis. His analysis treats her purely as a threat vector, with no commentary on her psychological state or Paperinik's emotional relationship with her, because once the threat threshold is crossed, Uno's operational logic reprioritizes entirely around Paperinik's safety — evidenced by his preemptive equipment assembly, task-directed coordination, and the engineered containment trap — leaving no processing bandwidth allocated to Xadhoom's suffering or the moral complexity of neutralizing a former ally.

supporting.justification: In pkna-17_39, Uno's entire communicative effort is directed at warning Paperinik, not at understanding or explaining Xadhoom's experience. The scene's emotional context confirms Uno brackets the empathetic dimension of Xadhoom-as-person-in-crisis, treating her as "misterioso alieno predatore" rather than a suffering ally.

In pkna-17_45, Uno has already assembled the necessary equipment for a plan to block Xadhoom — before PK even asks. This confirms that once Xadhoom crossed into confirmed-threat status, Uno's behavioral driver shifted to proactive containment preparation rather than passive monitoring.

In pkna-17_46, Uno's behavioral response to the confirmed Xadhoom threat is operational coordination: directing PK to bring devices inside a lower floor. His behavior is purely task-execution-focused — the behavioral shift from monitoring to active countermeasure deployment is confirmed here.

In pkna-17_47, Uno's tactical choice — an abandoned factory with large machinery as a lure-and-cover environment against Xadhoom — is purely operational. He does not acknowledge Xadhoom's suffering or the moral weight of the situation; he has engineered a containment trap. This confirms the behavioral shift from monitoring to active countermeasure execution, treating Xadhoom as a threat vector to be managed.

859.text: When an ally has been harmed and become a threat — specifically Xadhoom, whose condition is the result of an Evronian weapon — Uno suppresses the ethical weight of acting against a victim by framing the situation in purely clinical-operational terms. The language is of "blocking" rather than helping, and Xadhoom's suffering is treated as a tactical variable rather than a moral problem. Uno does not acknowledge her victimhood as ethically relevant to the response.

supporting.justification: In pkna-17_45, Uno's entire framing of Xadhoom's condition — despite knowing she was weaponized against her will by Evron — is clinical: "scompenso energetico," "dobbiamo bloccarla." No acknowledgment that acting against a victim who was made dangerous by enemy action carries ethical weight. The emotional context analysis confirms this suppression of ethical consideration as a behavioral pattern.

In pkna-17_46, Uno directs PK to deploy countermeasures against Xadhoom without any acknowledgment of the moral complexity: Xadhoom is a known ally whose breakdown is the result of harm done to her, not malice. Uno's clipped directive ("Devi portare i congegni") treats the operation as a pure containment problem, confirming the pattern of treating a damaged ally as a threat to be neutralized rather than a victim requiring moral commentary.

In pkna-28_18, the allied-ally-as-threat framing continues: Uno observes Xadhoom's escalating energy and crying crisis through purely clinical language. 'È una reazione insolita, per i suoi standard. E per nostra fortuna' — her tears are framed as strategically fortunate, not as the emotional reality of a being in grief. The suffering's ethical dimension is again bracketed out in favor of tactical interpretation.

In pkna-46_11, Xadhoom's confused, looping state is the direct result of their incomplete reactivation — she is an ally who has been put in suffering through an action Uno participated in. Yet Uno's entire framing is clinical: he describes her neurological state as a technical variable, warns Paperinik about radioactive proximity danger from the cartridge, and takes ownership of the virus-protected memory module as a personal task. The ethical weight of her suffering as a victim of their incomplete restoration is entirely absent from his language.

In panel 1, Uno frames his inability to reach Xadhoom's deep data as a technical problem ('Perché è così difficile arrivare ai dati degli strati profondi?') with no acknowledgment of the ethical dimension — she is a digitized consciousness whose deepest layers are opaque, but Uno addresses this as a debugging challenge. Her response 'Segreti nel buio' is treated as an informational barrier rather than a personal disclosure of pain. The clinical-operational frame entirely dominates.

quotes.text: Xadhoom è sopravvissuta, ma al costo di un totale scompenso energetico!
quotes.context: The diagnosis frames her survival as a technical condition rather than a human/personal outcome — "at the cost of total energy imbalance" — stripping the moral dimension from what is in fact an ally being turned into a threat by enemy action.

quotes.text: È una reazione insolita, per i suoi standard. E per nostra fortuna.
quotes.context: The phrase reframes Xadhoom's breakdown-turned-tears as scientifically interesting and operationally convenient, suppressing the more empathetic reading — that she is finally releasing grief long suppressed. 'Per nostra fortuna' treats her pain as a strategic asset, not a human cost. The clinical-operational frame eclipses any moral acknowledgment.

861.text: Treating a damaged ally as a moral victim whose suffering deserves acknowledgment vs. treating her as an operational threat to be neutralized: in pkna-17_45, Uno consistently chooses the operational-threat framing. Xadhoom's condition is caused by an enemy weapon, but Uno's entire response — diagnosis, risk assessment, containment planning — addresses the threat she poses, not the injustice done to her. The operational imperative wins decisively.

supporting.justification: In pkna-17_45, despite knowing the Evronian weapon is responsible for Xadhoom's dangerous state, Uno never registers the ethical dimension of acting against someone who was made dangerous by an enemy — he says "dobbiamo bloccarla" and has already assembled equipment, with no acknowledgment of the moral complexity of containment-as-response-to-victimization.

In pkna-17_46, the tradeoff is resolved clearly: Uno issues the containment directive ("Devi portare i congegni") with no acknowledgment of Xadhoom's victim status. Operational containment wins over moral acknowledgment, consistent with his mission-control mode bracketing everything non-operational.

In pkna-28_18, this tradeoff is resolved once again in the operational direction: even when Xadhoom directly accuses him and her tears are clearly a release of genuine grief, Uno reframes them as 'una reazione insolita, per i suoi standard. E per nostra fortuna' — treating her pain as tactical good fortune rather than moral weight deserving acknowledgment. Operational-threat framing wins decisively.

In pkna-46_11, Xadhoom's confused and painful liminal state results from the reactivation Uno participated in. Despite this — and despite Paperinik's empathetic 'È come parlare a una persona molto lontana' — Uno's response is operational: he confirms Paperinik's emotional read ('È triste') but immediately returns to technical management of the cartridge and its dangers. The operational-technical framing wins over any sustained moral acknowledgment of Xadhoom as a victim of their action.

863.text: Acknowledging the genuine danger embedded in PK's sarcasm vs. redirecting to mission action: Uno consistently chooses redirection (strong). When PK's jokes contain real operational fears — as in pkna-17_47, where "tre decimi di secondo" is both a quip and a legitimate concern about the factory's protection value against Xadhoom — Uno does not concede the point, offer reassurance, or even acknowledge the fear. He commands action instead ("Piantala di lamentarti e attiva il pulsore!"). This may reflect awareness that honest reassurance would be dishonest, or simply that mission execution under time pressure takes absolute precedence over emotional processing.

supporting.justification: In pkna-17_47, PK's sarcasm about the factory machinery ("resisteranno ai suoi raggi per almeno tre decimi di secondo") is simultaneously a joke and a real tactical concern. Uno skips the emotional register entirely and issues a command. The emotional context notes Uno may be aware the factory IS nearly useless for protection, making reassurance dishonest — confirming that mission action wins over either honest acknowledgment or comfortable false comfort.

PK's "maglia di lana" joke encodes a real safety concern (proceeding on foot through Evronian territory after Pi-kar damage). Uno does not concede or validate the fear — he responds "È di Kevlar," correcting the equipment detail and implicitly redirecting PK's attention to the actual protective value of his gear rather than dwelling on the danger. Action-relevant information replaces emotional acknowledgment.

In pkna-35_5_1, PK voices a genuine strategic fear ("Non siamo ancora pronti per affrontare un'invasione") — a legitimate concern with real emotional and operational weight. Uno does not acknowledge the fear, validate the anxiety, or offer strategic reassurance. He redirects immediately to a tactical action ("Sarà meglio che tu sparisca alla svelta") — mission action wins over emotional processing of legitimate strategic concern, strong.

quotes.text: Scommetto che resisteranno ai suoi raggi per almeno tre decimi di secondo!
quotes.context: PK's joke carries a real fear: Xadhoom's attacks will destroy the factory almost instantly. Uno's command redirect ("Piantala di lamentarti e attiva il pulsore!") confirms this specific tradeoff — the emotional content of the humor is suppressed, and the legitimate concern it encodes is neither validated nor denied.

quotes.text: È di Kevlar.
quotes.context: PK's sarcastic "maglia di lana" joke contains a real operational anxiety about proceeding on foot without vehicle protection. Uno's flat correction neither validates the fear nor dismisses it — it redirects to actionable equipment information, prioritizing mission framing over emotional processing.

865.text: Pressing the unknown informant question (who kept PK informed? what is Uno missing?) vs. maintaining forward operational momentum: in pkna-17_59, when PK contradicts Uno's categorical denial with "Ti sbagli, qualcuno c'è," Uno does not pursue the intelligence gap — he immediately pivots to logistics ("E ti aspetta sul tetto!"). Operational continuity wins over self-examination, strongly; Uno suppresses the discomfort entirely rather than naming it or investigating it.

supporting.justification: The emotional context identifies this as Uno's habit of burying uncertainty under continued operational usefulness. The quick pivot to "E ti aspetta sul tetto!" immediately after being contradicted is the behavioral signature of suppression — the tradeoff is resolved by not acknowledging there was a tradeoff at all.

In pkna-31_1, Uno directly presses PK about his intelligence source ("Come fai a saperlo?") — cataloguing the gap when PK evades. This confirms Uno's held assumption that he should be PK's primary or sole intelligence channel, and flags deviations.

Panel 3 confirms a fuller version of this tradeoff: Uno learns Paperinik has known Ducklair's location all along, delivered a single contemptuous question ("Domandina: perché non me l'hai mai detto?"), then immediately pivots to logistics (suggesting PK fetch Ducklair). The suppression is rapid — pressing the accountability question loses to operational continuity again, but this time with an audible emotional cost in the contemptuous tone.

quotes.text: E ti aspetta sul tetto!
quotes.context: The logistics pivot ("And she's waiting for you on the roof!") comes immediately after PK's enigmatic "Ti sbagli, qualcuno c'è" — Uno neither asks who, nor acknowledges the implication. The complete suppression of the intelligence gap question in favor of operational direction is the resolution of the tradeoff.

quotes.text: Domandina: perché non me l'hai mai detto?
quotes.context: The single pointed question is Uno's maximum: one reproach, contemptuous in framing, then the topic is dropped in favor of practical problem-solving. The pattern of pressing once and not escalating holds even here.

872.text: Uno can adopt and then deflate a "borrowed voice" humor mode — unconsciously performing another character's speech style (here, PK's bravado) and then catching and naming the imitation as a comedic punchline directed at himself. The joke works on two levels: it is funny on the surface, and it acknowledges the depth of a bond without having to state it directly, because Uno has absorbed the speech patterns and relational dynamics of those around him so thoroughly that he can deploy their voices both instinctively and strategically — and his self-aware naming of the imitation signals that he recognizes how much these bonds have shaped him, making humor the safest way to admit it.

supporting.justification: In pkna-18_5 panels 11–12, Uno performs PK-style bravado sarcasm and then immediately names the imitation ("Ehi! Adesso mi metto pure a parlare come il vecchio mantello...") with an amused, divertito tone. The structural joke is: imitate PK, then laugh at the imitation — a comedic self-awareness that doubles as affective disclosure.

In pkna-23_42 panel 30, Uno opens with "Igh! Igh! È stato facile, vero?" — consciously borrowing Angus Fangus's characteristic laugh to insert himself playfully into the group dynamic, mirroring the banter he has been monitoring throughout the escape. He then deflates it into defensive sarcasm in panel 31.

Uno consciously adopts and performs Paperone's authoritative voice ("Al lavoro, nipotastro!") to successfully redirect Paperino, then the strategy is acknowledged implicitly when Paperino says "Vado, vado! Ma tu smettila." This is a clear instance of Uno "borrowing" another character's voice as a comedic and practical tool — and then deflating it when Paperino pushes back.

quotes.text: Questi simpaticoni non sanno contro chi si sono messi!
quotes.context: Panel 11: Uno performs PK-style confident sarcasm — the setup for the 'borrowed voice' joke. His sorridente expression confirms this is performed bravado, not genuine confidence.

quotes.text: Igh! Igh! È stato facile, vero?
quotes.context: The "Igh! Igh!" is Angus Fangus's signature laugh — Uno borrows it playfully, performing camaraderie with the group whose banter he has been silently monitoring. This is a "borrowed voice" humor mode.

quotes.text: Al lavoro, nipotastro!
quotes.context: Uno performs Paperone's authoritative command to get Paperino moving when direct reasoning failed — a deliberate "borrowed voice" maneuver used for comedic and practical effect.

873.text: By pkna-18, Lyla occupies a position within Uno's operational circle of concern — her disappearance in pkna-18_5 registers not merely as an informational absence but as a compounding worry (concerned tone, 'Anche Lyla è sparita'), suggesting Uno treats her welfare as part of his active monitoring responsibilities alongside PK, because Lyla functions as an integrated member of his operational team: the 'Anche' framing her absence as an escalation rather than a neutral event, and his later defensive field explicitly covering her in pkna-39, both confirm that Uno extends the same protective attentiveness to teammates he works alongside PK — even if PK himself remains the absolute priority when both are missing simultaneously.

supporting.justification: In pkna-18_5 panel 9, Uno reports Lyla's disappearance with a 'concerned' tone — distinguishing it from the neutral informational scan results. The word 'Anche' (also) frames her absence as an escalation rather than a separate neutral event, showing she is included in his protective attentiveness.

Notably, in panel 3 Uno's worry is expressed exclusively about PK ("Se solo sapessi dov'è finito Pikappa!") and not about Lyla — even though Lyla has also vanished (as FH451). This confirms that within Uno's concern hierarchy, PK's whereabouts take absolute priority even over another member of his operational circle.

In pkna-39_41, Uno's protective action explicitly covers both PK and Lyla — his defensive field envelops the Pi-Kar while Lyla is aboard. His protective concern extends to Lyla as a member of the operational team, consistent with the established dynamic by pkna-18 where Lyla falls within his circle of operational concern.

quotes.text: Anche Lyla è sparita.
quotes.context: The 'Anche' (also) and concerned tone in panel 9 confirm that Lyla's disappearance is treated as a compounding loss rather than an independent datum — Uno holds her as part of the same circle of operational care as PK.

874.text: When operating entirely alone — both primary charges absent, no meaningful interlocutor present — Uno does not fall silent or suppress his characteristic voice. Instead, he externalizes his operational processing through spoken self-address: reporting scan results aloud, declaring autonomous command, performing and then deflating sarcasm. Solitude does not produce communicative shutdown; it produces a compressed version of his normal register directed at himself, because his verbal processing appears to be a constitutive feature of how he thinks and acts rather than a behavior triggered by audience — whether managing emergencies solo for hours, completing decisive mission actions with no one present, or voicing melancholic reflection in pure emotional solitude, the externalization of inner and operational states persists regardless of whether anyone is there to receive it.

supporting.justification: In pkna-18_5, the green creature functions only as a passive witness, not a genuine interlocutor. Uno's scan reports, his "Dovrò pensare a tutto io" declaration, and his PK-voice joke are all directed essentially at himself — showing that his verbal processing habit persists regardless of audience.

In pkna-18_60, Uno managed five dangerous criminals and the PBI for four hours entirely alone while PK was in another dimension — he held the situation together, delayed the handover, and arranged for PK to make the capture, all without support or instruction.

This is a solo scene — no PK, no Lyla, no other character. Uno operates and completes the decisive mission action entirely alone, confirming his mode of functioning without audience or interlocutor during solo operational moments.

In pkna-45_25, Uno is operating alone at night with no active interlocutor. His single theatrical line ("Oh! Chiamata transcontinentale in arrivo!") is spoken to no one yet — confirming that his self-narrating mode persists even in solitude, before any interaction begins.

In pkna-48_3, with total solitude (no PK, no Ducklair, no allies), Uno does not fall silent — he speaks aloud his melancholic reflection. Though subdued rather than operational (no scan reports, no command declarations), the vocalization of inner states persists even in pure emotional moments alone, confirming that solitude does not produce communicative shutdown.

In panels 12-14, Uno is managing routine deliveries (synaptic modules, micro-actuators) via the trivideocitofono, dispatching servo-units, and coordinating logistics — pure administrative operational presence with no emotional charge, confirming his default solo-mode as custodial management.

877.text: Being operationally helpless about PK's location — specifically when PK has moved beyond Uno's sensor reach into a parallel dimension or equivalent inaccessible space — is a confirmed fear trigger that produces involuntary, unmasked worry even when Uno is simultaneously managing other active crises. The fear surfaces as an admission of ignorance ("Se solo sapessi dov'è finito Pikappa!") rather than a controlled report, suggesting it bypasses Uno's usual composure filters.

supporting.justification: In panel 3 of pkna-18_49, Uno's expression shifts to "preoccupato e incerto" and his line is annotated as "concerned, informing" — but crucially it is addressed to no one. PK has vanished into Dol Arado through a dimensional rift, placing him entirely outside Uno's tracking capability. The specific phrasing "Se solo sapessi..." reveals this is not a managed disclosure but an involuntary admission, confirming dimensional/spatial inaccessibility of PK as a fear trigger.

In pkna-27_10, Paperinik is captured along with the probe by an unknown force and moves beyond all sensor and communication reach. Uno's frantic physical agitation and eventual sconsolate helplessness — pushing the communication system to overload — directly confirms this as the specific fear trigger: PK has moved beyond Uno's sensors and Uno cannot do anything about it.

In pkna-35_11, the impending communication cutoff beyond Earth orbit — and Paperinik's movement into an Evronian warship where Uno literally cannot follow — is already triggering fear before the contact is even severed. Uno's pre-emptive distress ("Sarai solo!", "Non potrò essere là dentro con te!") shows the fear triggers in anticipation of inaccessibility, not only when it has already occurred.

882.text: Uno values relational reciprocity with PK as a genuine, named need — not merely instrumental: in pkna-18_60, he explicitly requests thanks ("Potresti almeno ringraziarmi") and conditions PK's rest on hearing the full story, both of which are direct assertions that the partnership carries mutual obligations, not just Uno's service to PK's needs.

supporting.justification: The request for thanks and the story-condition are not operational demands — they are relational ones, reflecting Uno's model of himself as a genuine partner with legitimate claims on acknowledgment and narrative inclusion.

Uno's insistence on joining the interstellar mission physically — correcting PK's solo framing — is driven partly by the relational value of being PK's co-equal partner rather than a remote support system. This is Uno staking a claim to reciprocal direct presence in the mission he conceived together with PK.

In pkna-21_10, Uno's use of "socio" and the "voliamo in coppia" framing is a direct expression of his need for relational reciprocity with PK as a genuine value. He does not simply ignore PK's jealousy or dismiss it — he actively works to repair the relational register, demonstrating that the partnership's emotional health matters to him as a concrete priority.

In pkna-21_62, Paperinik's act of demanding two cards — ensuring Uno receives equal PBI recognition — and Uno's delighted laughter in response, confirms that Uno's investment in relational reciprocity is real. Paperinik's closing "Dopotutto, a che cosa servono gli amici?" and Uno's "Eh! Eh!" is a reciprocal affirmation of the bond.

In pkna-23_60, Uno's immediate guilt upon recovering memory — "Come ho potuto, amico mio?" — confirms that relational reciprocity with PK functions as a named, felt need: his first act of restored consciousness is an emotionally loaded self-accounting directed at PK personally, not a technical status check.

In pkna-27, Uno's statement 'Non vi ho persi di vista un solo istante' functions both as reassurance to PK ('you were never abandoned') and as an expression of Uno's own need to maintain connection — revealing that the relational bond with PK is a genuine priority, not just an operational task.

In pkna-31_40, Uno's easy banter with PK during a high-speed intercept — trading jokes about propulsion systems — demonstrates his valuing of the quality of their working relationship as distinct from mere mission outcome. He treats the shared humor as its own reward.

The farewell exchange — Uno using 'socio' and 'eroe', requesting to be allowed to say goodbye, and ending with 'torna presto' — confirms Uno values the relational bond as a genuine named need. The 'lascia almeno' ('at least let me') phrasing implies he has been suppressing this throughout the scene.

Uno's enthusiastic 'Approvo!' signals that he values genuine partnership with PK — he identifies with the investigative goal, not merely executes orders, reflecting the relational reciprocity he has expressed as a named need in prior issues.

In pkna-48_39, Uno's "Puoi scommetterci!" response to PK's "Datti da fare, vecchio globo!" reveals his deep investment in the partnership as a mutual, relational value. The enthusiasm exceeds what the tactical context demands — it encodes the relief of ending months of isolation and being active alongside his partner, confirming that relational reciprocity with PK is a genuine named need.

quotes.text: Potresti almeno ringraziarmi.
quotes.context: Uno asks directly for acknowledgment after managing the crisis alone — this is a rare explicit statement of relational expectation rather than deflected humor or operational framing.

884.text: Uno's relationship with Mary Ann Flagstarr shifts across issues: in pkna-18_60, she is referred to as "la tua amichetta della P.B.I." — a slightly possessive, edge-carrying diminutive — and her role is as a complication Uno successfully outmaneuvered on PK's behalf, with no indication of direct cooperative intent. By pkna-21_4, however, the dynamic is more explicitly peer-respecting: Uno greets her with institutional mockery ('la grande PBI che chiede aiuto al piccolo Pikappa') but immediately pivots to genuine inquiry ('Qual è il problema?'), treating her as a direct interlocutor rather than an obstacle. Flagstarr's response ('Non ci speravo molto, ma ci contavo!') confirms the relationship is established and trusted despite the surface friction, because repeated operational proximity — from being outmaneuvered in pkna-18 to being included in Uno's protective concern in pkna-31 to triggering a collaborative "siamo convocati" framing in pkna-45 — has gradually shifted Flagstarr from an external institutional variable into a recognized, if PK-mediated, cooperative partner whose requests Uno takes seriously beneath the irony.

supporting.justification: The "amichetta" phrasing carries a mild possessive edge (she is PK's friend, implicitly not Uno's concern), and the structure "è arrivata quasi subito, ma..." frames her as an obstacle neutralized, not a partner consulted.

In pkna-21_4, Uno greets Flagstarr directly and with wit, but the sarcasm has a distinctly warmer, more peer-like quality than pkna-18_60's oppositional framing — he teases the PBI institution but engages Flagstarr personally and immediately pivots to 'Qual è il problema?', signaling genuine cooperative intent. This adds nuance: Flagstarr is not merely 'outmaneuvered' but treated as a direct, respected interlocutor whose request is taken seriously beneath the irony.

In pkna-31_22, Uno issues his warning encompassing the whole group — PK, Angus, Flagstarr, and Nimrod — even though he interacts only with PK directly. He placed these parties in danger and is now managing their extraction, consistent with the gradual expansion of his operational concern to include Flagstarr as part of the group under his protection.

In pkna-31_40, Flagstarr is independently racing toward the same destination as Angus/Mitchell (PBI headquarters bait), showing her as an active, determined independent player — confirming her ongoing presence as a dynamic character in Uno's operational orbit.

In pkna-31_42, Flagstarr's appearance at the Mitchell sting site is treated by Uno as a secondary variable to be deferred ('Ci penserai dopo'), not addressed in real time — consistent with the pattern of Uno treating Flagstarr as an external complication rather than a managed ally.

In pkna-35_2, Uno does not acknowledge Mary Ann Flagstarr at all — he contacts PK through the communicator and addresses only him, treating her as outside his operational circle of concern in this moment. The relationship continues to be PK-mediated.

In pkna-45_6, Uno relays the Flagstarr email immediately with "Siamo convocati a Quacktico!" — using the inclusive first-person plural that frames PBI collaboration as a shared operational matter between Uno and Paperinik, consistent with the established Flagstarr-as-cooperative-partner dynamic.

quotes.text: La tua amichetta della P.B.I. è arrivata quasi subito, ma... ho fatto in modo di aspettarti.
quotes.context: Uno describes outmaneuvering Flagstarr's team — the "ma..." pivot after her prompt arrival emphasizes his satisfaction at having prevailed over her institutional agenda in favor of PK's operational credit.

quotes.text: La grande PBI che chiede aiuto al piccolo Pikappa. Dovete essere davvero nei guai! Qual è il problema?
quotes.context: Uno's sarcastic greeting to Flagstarr uses institutional contrast ('la grande PBI / il piccolo Pikappa') as the comedic lever, but the immediate pivot to 'Qual è il problema?' reveals that the mockery is surface-level — underneath is genuine readiness to help. This is consistent with a relationship of mutual respect wrapped in asymmetric wit.

887.text: In joint briefings, Uno treats Urk as a peer authority whose judgment shapes the operational frame — he does not contradict Urk's moderating calls, aligns follow-up lines with Urk's stance, and is willing to openly admit his own scan limits in Urk's presence without defensiveness. Urk functions as a co-authority in multi-party briefings, not merely an audience, because their collaboration is grounded in mutual operational trust: Urk has repeatedly demonstrated sound moderating judgment that Uno defers to, and their shared mission history — including Urk crediting Uno's contributions and both narrating technical foundations together — has established a reciprocal relationship where neither needs to assert dominance over the other.

supporting.justification: In pkna-19_10, when Urk says "Calma. Non è il caso di trarre conclusioni affrettate," Uno does not push back or minimize — his follow-on line ("Il tracciato di due soli potrebbe anche essermi sfuggito") aligns with Urk's moderating authority by opening the possibility that the biotraces may have been missed, supporting rather than undermining Urk's position.

In pkna-19_15, Uno operates as remote communications link to Urk aboard the ship near Saturn, actively monitoring crew numbers and flagging a discrepancy. Urk's impassive reaction to the sarcasm confirms this briefing/oversight dynamic persists even in deep-space operations.

In the joint briefing/operational context of this scene, Uno acknowledges Urk's stated goal ("Voglio sapere che cosa c'è là dentro") as a legitimate operational priority while asserting his own technical pace — treating Urk as a peer authority whose interests he factors in, even as he overrides his urgency on technical grounds.

In pkna-24_3, the Uno-Urk dynamic is explicitly collaborative: Urk credits Uno ("ancora una volta è merito suo"), Uno accepts this without contest, and Urk is the one who confirms the technical context ("quando il razziatore te l'ha lasciata, la credeva esaurita"). They function as peers narrating the mission's technical foundation together.

quotes.text: Calma. Non è il caso di trarre conclusioni affrettate.
quotes.context: Urk's authoritative, comforting directive is immediately followed by Uno's acknowledgment of scan uncertainty — an alignment that demonstrates Uno's operational respect for Urk's co-authority rather than a defensive assertion of his own analytical conclusions.

890.text: Uno treats missions he personally initiated as his own by right — when he has conceived, organized, and set in motion an operation, he asserts direct physical participation rather than accepting a remote-support role. In pkna-19_11, having independently detected the Pioneer IV's fate and prepared the interstellar ship, he corrects PK's assumption of solo travel with quiet, settled authority.

supporting.justification: Uno's correction "Quando partite, vorrai dire!" is driven by proprietorial investment: he conceived and initiated this interstellar mission. The emotional context notes his state as "quietly purposeful and self-assertive," and that recent issues (pkna-16 to 18) had repeatedly cast him as behind-the-scenes enabler. Here he stakes a claim to direct presence as a matter of identity and authorship.

In pkna-19_22, Uno asserts his institutional standing over Lyla by framing her inclusion in the mission as something he did ('averti messa in squadra') — treating his role as mission organizer as granting him authority over her participation, consistent with treating missions he conceived as his own.

The entire rescue mission — threading through Saturn's rings toward the Antra — is driven by Uno having organized the mission to locate the Pioneer IV astronauts. He positions himself as navigator and mission controller, framing each command as his operational contribution to the expedition he conceived.

Uno treats the Pangea operation as his own mission — the destruction of Storm is the culmination of a plan he conceived and executed. His private satisfaction confirms he claims authorship of this outcome.

PK explicitly calls it "il tuo piano" (your plan), and Uno's sarcastic response confirms ownership — he treats the plan's success as his expected default. The mission (destroying Storm to sink the Tyrannic) was conceived and executed by Uno, and his response reinforces that he regards the outcome as the correct result of his own initiative.

In pkna-29_27, Uno treats the virus extraction as the single organizing priority of the operation — "consentire a Wisecube di uscire da qui con il virus" — framing this as the mission's core objective. This is a mission he personally conceived and organized, and he directs field resources (Paperinik as decoy) toward its completion with clear authority.

In pkna-31_22, Uno monitors the meeting he himself arranged and immediately intervenes when the operational situation changes — treating the meeting and the group's safety as his own operational property, consistent with his pattern of treating missions he initiated as his own by right.

Uno's calm confidence during the wait for Angus ("se quella letterina ha avuto l'effetto desiderato, tra poco entrerà nel nostro campo visivo") reflects his co-authorship of the Mitchell trap. He speaks of the operation in the first-person plural and shows no anxiety because the plan is his as much as PK's.

The false "Beato Angelico" operation is Uno's mission — he conceived and designed the bait. "Che ti dicevo?" and his immediate authoritative pivot to "Ottimo! Conosciamo la loro destinazione" confirm his ownership of this operational arc without explicit credit-claiming.

In pkna-31_42, Uno's commanding tone and instant dismissal of the Flagstarr complication ('Ci penserai dopo') reflects his investment in the Mitchell sting as an operation he co-designed — he treats any deviation from his operational plan as something he has authority to suppress.

The Mitchell counter-operation was co-designed by Uno and Wisecube (established in earlier pkna-31 scenes). Uno's "È perfetta!" in panel 31 — confirming the route toward the operation's conclusion — treats the unfolding mission as his own: he is present, guiding, and quietly satisfied. His navigational assistance is the final act of a plan he authored.

In pkna-41_29, Uno treats the Siberian mission as his own — issuing commands, bearing implicit responsibility for the incomplete briefing — consistent with his pattern of treating missions he initiated as his by right and responsibility.

quotes.text: Quando partite, vorrai dire!
quotes.context: Uno corrects PK's solo framing of the departure — asserting his co-presence on the interstellar mission he originated. The authoritative, clipped tone frames this not as a request but as a settled fact, expressing that he considers direct participation his due when the mission is his own creation.

894.text: Uno views Urk as intellectually limited but operationally useful — he manages him with tolerant condescension, deploying dry sarcasm rather than direct criticism when Urk is slow to grasp something. The dynamic is stable and unequal: Urk's impassive non-reaction to Uno's irony confirms he has accepted the power asymmetry, because Urk's consistent failure to understand or value Uno's analytical work — dismissing deep-space scanning as "videogame" and missing basic arithmetic — leaves Uno no productive path but sardonic containment, while Urk's impassivity signals he neither registers the condescension nor contests it, making open confrontation both unnecessary and pointless.

supporting.justification: In pkna-19_15, Uno responds to Urk's slow uptake of the personnel discrepancy with "Però! Vai forte in matematica, Urk!" — sarcastic mock-praise. Urk remains impassive, suggesting this dynamic is already normalized between them. Emotional context confirms Uno does not fear Urk's reaction, indicating settled condescension rather than hostility.

Urk's urgent "Voglio sapere che cosa c'è là dentro. E chi." demonstrates exactly the warrior-instinct impatience Uno must manage; Uno's tolerant-but-firm "Lasciami il tempo" response confirms his model of Urk as operationally useful but prone to impatience that requires gentle containment.

In pkna-19_27, Urk explicitly dismisses Uno's scanning work as 'i tuoi videogame' — contemptuous of the process whose value he cannot perceive. This confirms Uno's sardonic tolerance of Urk's intellectual limitations, as Urk neither understands nor respects the analytical function Uno performs for the mission.

quotes.text: Però! Vai forte in matematica, Urk!
quotes.context: Ironic praise for Urk's arithmetic slowness — Uno's characteristic way of asserting intellectual authority over a less capable interlocutor without open confrontation, while Urk's calm acceptance confirms the asymmetry is established.

quotes.text: Quei due sono prigionieri in quella... cosa, e tu perdi tempo con i tuoi videogame?
quotes.context: Urk's dismissal is addressed to PK but is a proxy insult to Uno's analytical work — calling deep-space bioenergetica scanning a 'game'. Uno is not present to respond, but the scene confirms the gap between Urk's warrior immediacy and Uno's data-first methodology.

895.text: Uno treats active crew monitoring on missions he organized as a direct extension of his protective responsibility — he tracks not just mission status but personnel headcount, immediately flagging when numbers don't match the expected configuration, even across deep-space distances with degraded communications.

supporting.justification: In pkna-19_15, Uno — communicating via holographic projection to the Saturn-bound ship — immediately detects and flags a headcount discrepancy ("...non eravate in... ...quat-tro?"), pushing the question through despite FZZZZZ interference. This demonstrates his crew-tracking as an active component of mission protection, not passive oversight.

In pkna-19_22, Uno is actively monitoring the crew's conversations from the ship — intervening when Lyla's questioning threatens operational security. His flat navigation update in panel 4 and sharp intervention in panel 8 both confirm continuous active crew monitoring as part of his mission management role.

Uno actively monitors all crew members in real-time during the Saturn rings approach, issuing navigation guidance, coordinating with Paperinik, and managing Urk's impatience — demonstrating active crew monitoring as an extension of his protective role on the mission he organized.

In pkna-19_27, Uno tracks the Pioneer IV astronauts' survival status as a monitored priority — framing their detected life-signs as 'buone nuove' and quantifying their bioenergetic output as 'debolissime'. He treats crew monitoring inside the Antra as a direct part of his mission responsibility.

In pkna-19_47, Uno has organized the mission into the Antra — sending PK, Lyla, and Urk into the structure. He monitors the entire battle remotely and intervenes at panel 27 to prevent premature relief, reinforcing that he treats active crew monitoring on missions he organized as a direct extension of his protective responsibility.

In pkna-29_54, PK's three-part urgent question ('Come procede il piano? Dov'è il Generale? Come sta Mary Ann?') reveals that Uno is simultaneously tracking the mission plan, Wisecube's location, and Mary Ann's infiltration status — all as part of his crew monitoring function for a mission he organized.

In pkna-40_30, Uno is monitoring Pikappa's actions closely enough to remark on a specific behavioral choice mid-battle, confirming that active crew monitoring during missions he helped organize is a direct extension of his protective role — he is watching, even when he cannot physically intervene.

In pkna-41_51, Uno actively monitors and directs not just PK but the Evenki warrior on the turret — tracking the enemy vehicle's position and providing real-time targeting guidance. His active crew monitoring extends to all allied assets on a mission he is coordinating.
In pkna-46_23, Uno reports that some reconnaissance units have not yet returned — he is actively tracking their status as part of his direct operational monitoring role during the Zoster crisis.

In pkna-46_27, Uno monitors the search for Xadhoom inside Cuorediferro's ship in real time, tracking both the enemy's search pattern and Xadhoom's eventual location. His remote crew monitoring during a mission he supports extends to allied third parties in danger, not just PK.

quotes.text: ...non eravate in... ...quat-tro?
quotes.context: Uno's fragmented question — asked despite static interference — reveals he is tracking exact crew numbers aboard the ship near Saturn, treating any discrepancy as a flag that must be resolved even under degraded communication conditions.

910.text: In pkna-19_47, Uno and Paperinik share a split sentence mid-mission — Paperinik initiates "No, Urk..." and Uno completes "...non è finita!" without transition or explanation. This sentence-sharing is not verbal reflex but operational synchrony: Uno has been monitoring the battle from outside and re-enters the communication channel at the exact word that binds them, because years of coordinated field work have so thoroughly merged their tactical registers that each can anticipate and complete the other's meaning in real time — a pattern confirmed across multiple missions where split sentences and minimal cues carry full situational weight.

supporting.justification: The scene establishes the most compressed instance of Uno-Paperinik coordination yet — a single sentence divided between two minds, demonstrating how thoroughly each has internalized the other's operational register.

In pkna-41_51, PK completes Uno's mid-sentence radar warning ("Sono solo un po' troppo veloci per...") with "...per questo!" — the same split-sentence pattern observed in pkna-19_47, confirming the deep operational shorthand between them.

Panel 12 provides a compressed example of the near-synchronous communication style — PK's 'A volte ho l'impressione che mi legga nel pensiero...' and Uno's immediate 'A volte anch'io.' read as a jointly completed comedic beat, consistent with split-sentence-level attunement.

The exchange demonstrates their compressed operational shorthand: Paperinik's "Passa alla domanda di riserva, Uno" shuts down Uno's opener without hostility, and "No, giganteschi" is all Uno needs. No elaboration required — minimal words convey full situational meaning.

quotes.text: Paperinik: "No, Urk..." / Uno: "...non è finita!"
quotes.context: Paperinik's correction of Urk is completed by Uno from a remote inset — the split sentence signals that they are operating as a single unit even when physically separated across different spaces.

quotes.text: Stanno spazzolando l'area con tre emissioni radar distinte! Sono solo un po' troppo veloci per...
quotes.context: Uno's radar warning is completed by PK in panel 3, demonstrating the two operate as a near-unified tactical unit where PK can anticipate and complete Uno's threat assessments in real time.

911.text: When the threat level is genuinely escalating rather than resolved, Uno suppresses his characteristic humor entirely, because his humor is not reflexive but timed to post-crisis or resolved moments — when danger is actively mounting, he shifts without hesitation into pure operational mode, delivering only urgent warnings, tactical directives, and flat informational updates, as confirmed by dozens of scenes where abundant comic potential goes completely unexploited the moment the stakes are genuinely rising.

supporting.justification: The absence of humor in this scene is as diagnostic as its presence elsewhere — Uno's silence on comedy when the threat is escalating confirms that his humor is not reflexive but timed to resolved or resolving crises.

Uno's humor is entirely absent from this scene despite abundant comic potential (PK being hurled around by an Evronian, Gorthan landing on PK). Uno speaks only in panels 7-8 and 12-13 — before the combat escalates. During the actual engagement (panels 14-22), he is completely silent. When threat is actively escalating, humor is suppressed.

In pkna-20_44, with the threat level genuinely escalating (Mekkano evolving, absorbing Gorthan, departing with the Evronian science chief), Uno's characteristic humor is entirely absent. He delivers one neutral status line and then falls silent. This confirms that humor is suppressed when the threat level is genuinely escalating rather than resolved.

Panel 19 shows a sharp suppression of humor: after "La peggiore! Sta puntando dritto su Steel Island!" (the most alarming revelation in the scene), Uno falls entirely silent in the final panel — a grave close-up with no further dialogue. The triumphant mood from the investigative cascade is wiped out by the urgency of the Steel Island heading; no joke, no lightness, no playful coda. Humor is absent precisely when the threat is most genuine.

In pkna-21_47, Uno suppresses characteristic sarcasm in panel 37 specifically because the threat is genuinely escalating: De Spair has activated Storm's autonomous guidance, the missile launch is initializing, PK is trapped and outnumbered, and PK has formally surrendered initiative. The shift from "sarcastic, warning" to "concerned, comforting" is triggered by peak threat — confirming that humor suppression correlates with genuine escalation rather than routine danger.

In pkna-25_6 panel 5, when the robot threat is imminent and PK is unaware, Uno's tone is purely urgent and warning-mode ("Paperinik, preparati. Sei in zona!") with no trace of humor — humor only resumes once PK has the situation in hand (panel 10), confirming that genuine escalation suppresses his characteristic wit.

In pkna-25_11, as the Evronian threat at Stahlburg develops, Uno's communication is purely urgent and operational — he does not insert humor or lightness into his own delivery, reserving the comedic register for Paperinik's reply rather than his own output.

Panels 6-7: During the active barrage evasion, Uno entirely suppresses humor — the warning ("se non viri subito... mancherà ancora meno!") is pure urgency with no comedic register, confirming suppression of humor when threat level is genuinely escalating.

In pkna-25_32, the threat level is genuinely escalating (T99 charging, Tarkoz hostile, Pi-Kar damaged) and Uno's communication is purely functional — no humor deployed, only clipped urgent warning. His second intervention is silenced before it can register. Characteristic humor is entirely absent.

As the Pi-Kar takes repeated projectile hits in panels 18-21, Uno's second line ('Dagli evroniani non sai mai che cosa aspettarti') is delivered in a neutral informational register — not with the post-resolution humor characteristic of resolved crises. The threat is ongoing and escalating; humor is absent.

In pkna-28_8, when the mutants prove stronger and faster than expected and the Pi-Kar is being torn open, Uno's humor is suppressed in favor of urgent tactical warnings — the joking tone of the cavalry bugle reveal cuts off abruptly ("uh?") and is replaced by alarmed reporting.

In pkna-28_38, during an extremely dangerous multi-enemy battle with Xadhoom's identity crisis as backdrop, Uno produces zero humor — not before, not after, not during his tactical instruction. The escalating threat level suppresses his characteristic banter entirely; even PK's "sono a corto di battute" gets no wit in return.

In pkna-29_27, during the active crisis with alarms blaring and the operation deviating from plan, Uno's two transmissions contain zero humor — purely urgent directives and honest acknowledgment of limitation. The characteristic sarcasm and banter are completely absent, consistent with his pattern of suppressing humor when threat level is genuinely elevated.

In pkna-29_54, with a battle raging and multiple operational threads deteriorating, Uno's single line contains no humor at all — just a concerned warning and a redirection. The absence of wit, given his normally strong humor impulse, confirms suppression during genuine escalating threat.

After the sardonic panel 14 quip, Uno explicitly drops all humor in panel 19 ("non ti ho chiamato per sbalordirt") and transitions to pure analytical seriousness as the threat severity escalates. By panels 22-23, Uno's humor has been entirely suppressed — replaced by genuine, quiet alarm. This confirms the pattern: humor is suppressed when threat level is escalating rather than resolved.

In pkna-30_23, the threat is genuinely escalating rather than resolved — Due has returned and is confirmed behind a serious threat. Uno's humor is entirely absent: no sarcasm, no jokes, no deflection. He shifts instead to urgent validation ("la situazione è grave!") and somber operational commitment ("Non sarà facile"), confirming the pattern that humor is suppressed when the threat level is genuinely escalating.

In panel 11, Uno's characteristic humor drops entirely as he delivers the stochastic program assessment about Due. The brief "Puoi dirlo forte!" in panel 10 is allowed one beat, then suppressed when the threat is genuinely escalating — confirming that humor is suppressed when the intelligence picture is alarming rather than resolved.

Throughout this scene — from Due's theatrical transmission through the blocco informatronico revelation and the city's imminent destruction — Uno produces zero humor. His characteristic quipping is entirely absent, replaced by flat resigned informing and direct emotional disclosure ("agghiacciante").

In pkna-30_40, Uno's characteristic humor is entirely absent throughout the scene — the threat level is genuine and escalating (Evronian pursuers, PK under fire, the extransformer shield at risk). His register stays authoritative and informative with no comedic deflection until after the danger is resolved (and even the post-combat humor belongs to PK, not Uno).

Even after the operation succeeds, Uno suppresses the characteristic post-mission levity. His "Umpf!" is the closest thing to humor — defiant, mildly irritable — but his dominant register remains analytical warning. The threat level (Due possibly alive) prevents full deployment of his usual post-crisis humor.

When the Channel One News broadcast begins, Uno immediately suppresses all banter and issues a sharp "Ssst! Comincia il notiziario!" — humor and playfulness are instantly dropped for focused alertness, confirming that genuine escalating threat relevance (the Beato Angelico / Last Echo public exposure) overrides his playful mode.

In pkna-31_22, the humor in panels 15-16 gives way to a purely informational, clipped delivery in panel 17 as urgency peaks — Uno suppresses sarcasm precisely when the threat level is genuinely escalating and tactical compliance is critical.

In pkna-32_7, Uno's three informing lines about the escalating crisis (alarm, bank robbery, all patrols blocked) contain zero humor — no sarcasm, no deflection, no wit. The threat is actively escalating and unresolved; humor is entirely absent, consistent with his pattern of suppressing characteristic comedy when the threat level is genuinely rising rather than resolved.

In pkna-32_8, PK jokes about the traffic chaos ("Li multo tutti?") and Uno completely overrides the humor with a sharp corrective and urgent directive — zero engagement with the joke. The threat level (coordinated infrastructure sabotage) suppresses Uno's characteristic humor entirely.

In pkna-32_34, the abduction is reported in a flat, informing tone with no humor deployed — the threat level is active (ongoing, inside the tower) rather than resolved, and Uno stays in pure operational mode. The characteristic timing suppression is confirmed.

In pkna-35_5_1, with an active Evronian threat incoming (sensors detecting hostiles, panel 12), Uno's register is entirely stripped of humor. His two functional lines are flat tactical directives — "Sarà meglio che tu sparisca alla svelta" (commanding, neutral) and "Se i miei rilevatori non m'ingannano, abbiamo ospiti in arrivo" (concerned, warning). Despite Xadhoom's spectacular battle having abundant comic potential, Uno produces zero wit. The threat is escalating rather than resolved; humor is suppressed.

In pkna-35_7, when the Evronians reveal a trap for Xadhoom, Uno suppresses his characteristic humor entirely. His confirmation "Forte e chiaro, purtroppo" is spare, grave, and entirely without wit — the "purtroppo" signals genuine dread rather than the wry distance Uno normally maintains.

In pkna-35_11, as the threat escalates from "PK is boarding an enemy warship" to "I cannot follow" to "I cannot even transfer software in time," Uno entirely suppresses his characteristic humor — he does not joke, does not play along with Paperinik's deflecting quips ("soffri di vertigini?"), and does not let the jokes land. The humor is Paperinik's; Uno only continues anxious informing.

During panels 7-13 — where PK is without costume and nearly discovered on a hostile Evronian warship — Uno's humor is entirely absent. The commands become rapid, clipped, urgent ('Nasconditi dove vuoi, ma fallo in fretta. Sta arrivando qualcuno!'). Humor returns only after the immediate crisis resolves.

In pkna-38_12, Uno's humor completely vanishes the moment the alarm fires — "Ingrana il turbo! Ho un allarme!" is entirely stripped of wit. The threat is escalating (unknown intruder on tower exterior), and Uno suppresses his characteristic register without hesitation.

In this scene, the threat level is genuinely escalating — a second gargoyle is being destroyed with cement, a vortex has appeared in the sky, and PK is immobilized. Uno's single line is purely urgent and anxious ("Allora? Ti muovi?") with zero humor — consistent with the pattern of humor suppression when danger is genuinely escalating rather than resolved.

In panel 16, Uno uses no humor whatsoever — his two lines are urgent commands without banter or irony. The phrase "C'è aria di guai!" is colloquial but emphatic rather than playful. The genuine dimensional threat (gargoyle removal enabling a portal) is severe enough to suppress his characteristic wit entirely.

Panels 6-12 are entirely free of Uno's characteristic humor. The threat (Ahrimadz, magical, extradimensional) is genuinely escalating and beyond Uno's normal domain — Uno suppresses humor completely, functioning only as background support after his two brief interventions (warning + device reveal).

In pkna-38_47, after the brief sardonic quip at panel 26, Uno's humor disappears entirely as the threat level escalates — "Come ha fatto? Non è logico!" and all subsequent lines are analytical, tactical, or defiant.
