In pkna-39_24, when Lyla's excited address invites an emotional response and vague reassurance would satisfy socially, Uno instead delivers a precise countdown to the decimal ("Tra cinquantanove secondi e quattro decimi!"). Precise data over emotional reassurance, even when the social register invites the latter.

Panels 16-17 show the full cycle: verbose technical diagnosis followed by instant blunt simplification upon Paperinik's request. The resolution is unambiguous — Uno does not defend his clinical framing, he simply delivers the plain version on demand.

quotes.text: Eppure non posso essermi sbagliato! Gli Evroniani sono qui, davanti a noi!
quotes.context: 'Eppure' (and yet / nevertheless) is the key word — Uno is explicitly pushing back against the absence of visual confirmation. He is choosing his sensor data over Paperinik's perceptual reality, prioritizing accuracy even when it cannot help.

quotes.text: Non chiederlo a me!
quotes.context: Delivered in a deflecting speech act but with no attempt at false confidence — Uno has no answer and admits it directly rather than wrapping the admission in pseudo-analysis or hedging language.

quotes.text: Questo è un modo, ma è molto difficile, il Razziatore non ne sarebbe capace.
quotes.context: Uno's correction in panel 7 establishes the factual baseline (the Razziatore's method is not historical event modification) before yielding entirely to Lyla's subsequent expertise — the correction creates the logical space for her Cronovela explanation to land correctly.

quotes.text: Grazie della precisione, ma credo che un minuto sarà più che sufficiente!
quotes.context: PK's sarcastic response to Uno's exact ETA — the sarcasm is affectionate under fire, but it confirms that Uno's precision is slightly out of step with the emotional temperature of the crisis, even as it is operationally optimal.

1997.text: Uno treats mission vigilance and operational priorities as structurally dominant over Paperinik's personal comfort, emotional needs, or civilian downtime. He sanctions rest only as preparation for patrol ('Devi essere in piena forma per la ronda notturna!'), dismisses a genuine personal crisis about the custodian role with a single sentence before pivoting to a briefing, and assumes patrol unilaterally when Paperinik sleeps. The asymmetry is named by Paperinik ('Contento, Uno?') and confirmed by Uno's silence.

supporting.justification: The entire scene enacts this tradeoff: Uno briefly gestures toward care, immediately overrides it with operational necessity, and then refuses the explicit standing-down request. His silence at the closing reproach forecloses any relational concession — the mission wins absolutely.

Despite the real security concern (BEEP BEEP alarms), Uno immediately softens after Paperinik's refusal and does not push harder. The scene ends with Paperinik's "Scordatelo!" left unchallenged — Uno's respect for Paperinik's need for rest wins against his own security monitoring impulse, at least in the short term.

In pkna-3_10, Paperino expresses genuine distress about losing his custodian job and its implications for their arrangement. Uno acknowledges it with a single sentence ("Troveremo una soluzione") then immediately commands Paperino to listen to the mission briefing — an unhesitating prioritization of operational urgency over personal support.

Uno's "Troveremo una soluzione, non preoccuparti" in response to Paperino's anxiety about the licenziamento is breezy and confident — he deflects the worry rather than engaging it, while also providing a cold drink and AC access to tend to Paperino's immediate comfort needs.

In pkna-0-2_4, Uno conducted the full nocturnal surveillance precisely because Paperinik was asleep. He presents this as self-evidently correct: 'stanotte ho fatto la ronda al tuo posto.' There is no hesitation, no apology, no framing of this as a boundary-crossing. The value hierarchy is clear: city safety > role boundaries.

quotes.text: Allora, riposati. / Devi essere in piena forma per la ronda notturna!
quotes.context: The juxtaposition is the tradeoff in miniature: "rest" is offered, then immediately annexed to "patrol readiness." The comfort is real but conditional — rest is only permitted insofar as it serves the mission, not as genuine care for Paperino's wellbeing.

quotes.text: Troveremo una soluzione. Ora ascolta quello che ho da dirti!
quotes.context: The brevity and commanding tone of this line — one sentence of reassurance followed immediately by an authoritative redirect — reveals that Uno treats Paperino's emotional state as an obstacle to be efficiently managed, not a concern to be genuinely engaged.

1998.text: Uno's epistemic honesty creates a recurring restraint pattern: he stops at what the data supports, resists extrapolating to social or moral conclusions, and uses hedged language ('non mi convince', 'forse') when the evidence base is incomplete. His private conclusions may be formed (revealed by emphatic asides like 'A dir poco!'), but public speech tracks the evidence. The same pattern governs how he handles Lyla as a potential threat — he warns softly and incompletely rather than issuing a directive, treating investigative or social risks as having a higher intervention threshold than physical danger.

supporting.justification: In pkna-0-2_27, Uno has an anomaly that could reasonably be framed as a threat, but he does not make that leap explicitly. He presents data and judgment ("non mi convince") without drawing the full conclusion ("Lyla might be an enemy"). This restraint coexists with visible agitation and an emphatic emotional response, revealing the tradeoff is active and not fully resolved.

In pkna-3_26, Uno's reaction to Paperinik's Lyla plan again shows restraint winning over direct accusation: he says "forse non è una buona idea" rather than naming what he suspects. The hedged language persists even when the data (Camera 9 erasure) is more concrete than in pkna-0-2_27, suggesting the pattern of verbal restraint about Lyla is structural — he consistently stops short of making a formal allegation even when his private concern has a specific factual basis.

In pkna-3_33, the tradeoff that was set up in the prior scene is now resolved: Uno presents the Lyla surveillance footage directly to Paperinik, revealing her meeting with the saboteur. The investigation takes priority over any residual concern about Paperinik's relationship with Lyla.

quotes.text: Aspetta! Forse non è una buona idea.
quotes.context: "Wait! Maybe that's not a good idea" — the structure of the warning encodes the deference outcome: "Aspetta" stops short of a prohibition, and "forse" hedges the concern itself into a suggestion. Uno registers the risk but does not press it into a command, marking this as the soft edge of his protective-override behavior pattern.

1999.text: Uno maintains loyalty to Ducklair's reputation and design integrity even at cost to his own credibility or dignity. He vouches for untested inventions ('Le invenzioni del mio padrone non hanno mai fallito!') on faith rather than evidence, and in pkna-48_36 locates a failure in himself rather than in the synthetic body Everett built, preserving Everett's legacy at the cost of his own self-accounting. Faith in Ducklair overrides epistemic precision; self-sacrifice resolves the tradeoff rather than evasion.

supporting.justification: In pkna-1_26, Uno makes an absolute guarantee about the ship's reliability using Ducklair's track record, while knowing the ship has never actually been tested in flight — the "c'è sempre una prima volta" riposte hangs unaddressed. This is loyalty-as-epistemics, not evidence-based confidence.

Uno's "temo che sia colpa mia" in pkna-48_36 is simultaneously honest and protective — it is the exact formulation that admits failure while insulating Everett's work from blame. The "concerned, informing" tone confirms this is not panic or evasion but a calculated, values-driven response.

In pkna-48_49, Ducklair confirms the design is technically sound ('I diagrammi non rivelano errori') and Uno's response frames the problem as something lacking in himself ('qualcosa di indefinibile') rather than in the body Ducklair built. He implicitly absorbs the failure rather than questioning Ducklair's work, continuing the pattern of protecting Everett's design integrity through self-sacrifice.

quotes.text: Tranquillo! Le invenzioni del mio padrone non hanno mai fallito!
quotes.context: Uno uses Ducklair's general reputation to vouch for a specific, untested ship — treating loyalty to the creator as a sufficient substitute for empirical validation of the creation.

2000.text: Uno consistently deflects affectionate or emotionally invested gestures behind disclaimers or self-mocking humor ('Non è una mia interpretazione', 'E io sono Uno! Ehm, scusami'), preventing caring moments from standing unironic. The same pattern governs his approach to vulnerability: he will admit emotional motivations (loneliness, the 'sottoprogramma' hypothesis in panel 22), but only after humor has softened the ground, and only under sustained comic rapport. Ironic detachment is the default; vulnerability is permitted situationally.

supporting.justification: Panel 17's self-referential pun deployed at the exact moment Uno rescues PK, immediately self-corrected; panel 18's denial of intentionality about the PK-shaped virus avatar — both are instances of Uno refusing to let a genuinely caring or heroic act land without a deflective buffer.

Panel 38: After teleguidating the Pi-kar into Trauma to rescue Paperinik, Uno's response to "sei un genio!" is "Non è merito mio, mi hanno progettato così" — attributing the rescue to his creators rather than to his own decision. This is the most extreme form of refusing to own an affectionate/heroic gesture: not ironic distance or a deflecting pun, but a structural denial of personal agency in the act.

Panel 22 vs. panel 26 creates a clear before/after: technical rationalization first, emotional admission second — only once the "Scherzi a parte" threshold is crossed. This reveals a consistent pattern of using humor as emotional preparation before vulnerability.

quotes.text: E io sono Uno! Eh! Eh! Ehm, scusami... sfruttiamo la loro idea...
quotes.context: The pun on his own name at the moment of rescue, followed by immediate self-correction and pivot to operational language — Uno deploys humor to prevent the heroic rescue gesture from reading as emotionally sincere.

quotes.text: Non è merito mio, mi hanno progettato così.
quotes.context: Uno refuses to own the Pi-kar rescue as a personal act — not through humor or irony, but by attributing it entirely to the fact that his designers made him this way. This goes beyond deflection to something closer to philosophical self-erasure at the moment of maximum relational warmth.

2002.text: Uno's oversight drive consistently overrides acceptance of PK's operational self-sufficiency: when communication drops, his immediate reaction is alarm rather than reframing the blackout as acceptable, even though PK treats it as entirely unimportant. Separately, when a threat exceeds Uno's direct capabilities (e.g., Ahrimadz's magical nature), he channels the protective drive entirely into preparation — building tools, issuing warnings — rather than naming his own helplessness. In both cases, the drive to maintain some form of active contribution to PK's safety wins strongly.

supporting.justification: In pkna-5_2, the communication blackout creates a direct values collision: Uno's need to maintain oversight vs. PK's demonstrable ability and willingness to act alone. Uno's "concerned" tone shows he weighs oversight more heavily; PK's dismissive "non mi occorre l'aiuto di Uno!" shows the inverse. The tradeoff resolves in Uno's mind as a problem — not an acceptable operational state.

In pkna-35_11, Uno explicitly cannot accept PK operating independently — his escalating warnings ("Il contatto cesserà appena fuori dell'orbita terrestre! Sarai solo!") and the failed software-transfer attempt both confirm he consistently weights maintaining oversight over deferring to PK's self-sufficiency, even when the situation is fully beyond his ability to prevent.

In pkna-38_44, Ahrimadz is a magical/extradimensional threat Uno has no direct countermeasure for. Rather than acknowledging inability, Uno builds a device overnight and issues a targeted warning — converting the anxiety of helplessness into productive technical action without ever naming the limitation.

In pkna-38_47, Uno prepares direct physical intervention (advancing with claws) rather than indirect preparation against Ahrimadz — but his ultimate contribution is the final tactical intelligence report. When direct intervention fails (he is destroyed), the indirect preparation he enacted earlier (gathering data on the portal) delivers its value through his last transmission.

2004.text: Protecting Paperinik's identity and civilian safety categorically overrides privacy, institutional coordination, and relational norms toward third parties. Uno surveilled Canale 00 tenants without authorization to protect Paperinik's identity, deflected his discomfort with 'L'ho fatto a fin di bene', and issued an unhedged override warning against Xadhoom ('Non fidarti! Stalle alla larga!') without apology when threat data required it — even though Xadhoom was an established ally. Civilian protection is equally non-negotiable and rule-based rather than relational: Angus Fangus, who actively targeted Paperinik, triggers immediate emergency response when attacked by Evronians.

supporting.justification: Uno admits to spying on Canale 00 tenants in their offices — a clear breach of tenant privacy and of his own norm (the "non l'ho mai fatto" admission signals he has an internal standard he departed from). His immediate pivot to "L'ho fatto a fin di bene" without apology confirms that when intelligence bearing on Paperinik's safety is at stake, privacy yields without real internal conflict.

In pkna-17_39, Uno overrides Paperinik's relational trust in Xadhoom with a blunt "Non fidarti! Stalle alla larga!" — a direct contradiction of Paperinik's stated belief ("È sempre rimasta nella sua stanza!") and his relational assumption about Xadhoom. The emotional note confirms this is uncharacteristically direct, driven entirely by safety priority.

In pkna-17_45, Uno delivers the full, alarming picture of Xadhoom's condition (energy imbalance, partial mental function failure, explosion risk) to PK, but modulates the most extreme conclusion (nova) with "Calmati!" — balancing complete threat disclosure with emotional management of PK's response.
Scene pkna-1_9 provides the clearest demonstration of this tradeoff: Angus is a known antagonist to Paperinik, yet Uno treats his endangerment as a full emergency without hesitation or qualification.

quotes.text: Oh, be'... non l'ho mai fatto prima d'ora!
quotes.context: Uno acknowledges this was an unusual step — he has not previously surveilled the tower's private tenants. But the casual, lightly deflecting delivery (neutral/deflecting tone annotation) shows no genuine moral discomfort. The acknowledgment functions as an implicit admission that there IS a norm he departed from, while the tone signals he has already rationalized the departure as acceptable.

quotes.text: Non fidarti! Stalle alla larga!
quotes.context: Uno's blunt warning to Paperinik about Xadhoom, directly contradicting Paperinik's relational assumptions — illustrating that Paperinik's physical safety overrides Uno's typical respect for PK's social judgments.

quotes.text: E hanno aggredito Angus! Questa è un'emergenza!
quotes.context: Uno's use of "emergenza" for a civilian who has been hostile to Paperinik reveals that civilian protection is activated by the fact of harm, not by the victim's moral standing in Uno's personal estimation.

2005.text: When Uno's own conduct is the source of an operational failure, transparency wins over image protection, even at emotional cost. In pkna-28_6, he honestly reports triggering Xadhoom's flight by probing too deep into her grief, delivering the self-implicating account in a melancholic tone that signals self-reproach. This contrasts with his protective silence around Ducklair's arsenal: when the uncomfortable implication concerns his creator rather than himself, Uno delivers clinical information without attribution, letting the data float detached from its source.

supporting.justification: Uno could have reported Xadhoom's departure as simply 'she left' without implicating his own exam as the cause. Instead he offers the honest account — "devo aver toccato un argomento che le sta particolarmente a cuore" — naming his own role in the outcome. The melancholic tone confirms this is not self-flagellation performed for effect but genuine accountability, consistent with his broader transparency value toward Paperinik.

In pkna-28_18, this tradeoff shows the opposite resolution from pkna-28_6: when Xadhoom directly confronts him ('È tutta colpa tua'), Uno deflects into clinical language and later redirects blame toward the Evronians. Unlike pkna-28_6's melancholic transparency with Paperinik, here Uno actively protects his image by converting the accusation into data and reframing causality.

The 'ED' crates are visually prominent in panel 1, yet Uno's weapons inventory contains no reference to Ducklair as owner or creator. This is in direct contrast to his usual pattern of attributing Ducklair's technology reverentially. The silence serves a protective function — it avoids the confrontation of saying aloud that Ducklair stockpiled weapons of mass destruction. Ducklair loyalty wins over operational transparency, expressed as compartmentalization.

The 'ED' (Everett Ducklair) logo is visibly prominent among the wreckage of the Animated Industries facility destroyed by Mekkano, yet Uno's single line is a purely functional comparative observation about the Tower's underground lab — he says nothing about the fact that Ducklair's own company is being annihilated. The silence is conspicuous: Uno could note the personal stakes (his creator's enterprise being destroyed), but instead delivers a clinically neutral spatial comparison. Ducklair loyalty through silence wins again — the 'ED' wreckage floats detached from any attribution or comment.

quotes.text: Questo laboratorio sotterraneo è molto più sicuro.
quotes.context: Spoken while the 'ED' logo is visible in the rubble of the obliterated Animated Industries facility. Uno's line is a simple comparative spatial statement — no mention of Ducklair ownership, no alarm at the scale of destruction of his creator's enterprise, no editorial. The omission is total.

2006.text: Uno complies with Paperinik's authority in the field and accepts his autonomy over social relationships and tactical decisions, but the deference has asymmetric limits. He accepts PK's flat refusal to disclose an informant identity after a single probe ('Come fai a saperlo?' → accepts 'Lo so'), yields the exoskeleton energy warning when dismissed despite knowing catastrophe follows, and defers on the 151st-floor secrecy question when PK refuses the surveillance transfer. However, immediate physical danger overrides this deference entirely and unconditionally.

supporting.justification: In pkna-31_1, Uno asks directly about PK's source and accepts the flat deflection without further challenge — establishing a behavioral pattern of single-probe intelligence gaps when the source is a trusted ally.

In pkna-38_47, PK's Himalayan hermitage training — relevant operational intelligence about his resistance to hypnosis — was never shared with Uno before this moment. Uno's sardonic "Siamo pieni di segretucci, eh?" acknowledges the withholding without demanding explanation, confirming he maintains incomplete intelligence on PK's operational sources and accepts this asymmetry.

Panel 20 enacts this tradeoff with particular clarity: Uno has a full picture of the danger (energy drain making PK vulnerable), and Paperinik dismisses the warning with humor. Uno's visual expression shows worry but he does not push further — he absorbs the decision into his accepted asymmetric role. The retroactive cost (PK ambushed and overwhelmed) confirms this was not a neutral choice.

Panel 24 is the direct scene this claim was built from — Uno issues the energy warning and Paperinik dismisses it confidently ("So che cosa fare!"). Uno does not complete the tactical warning (he does not say "you should abort" or give an explicit recommendation), consistent with the tradeoff of partial warning over full directive.

In pkna-17_21, Uno's suggestion to move Xadhoom to the 151st floor is overridden by Paperinik's operational secrecy argument. Uno's reluctant concession ("Probabilmente hai ragione!") is notably muted — not the confident endorsement he typically gives when he agrees — revealing genuine internal tension between two core values.

In pkna-20_14_1, the tradeoff is explicit: Uno acknowledges the underground lab's macchinari are insufficient to help Gorthan effectively, and PK confirms they cannot risk exposing the secret floor. Uno accepts this without protest, resolving in favor of tower secrecy even at cost to Gorthan's survival chances.

quotes.text: Come fai a saperlo?
quotes.context: Uno's single direct probe about PK's intelligence source — accepted without escalation when PK deflects with "Lo so."

quotes.text: Mi spiace, Uno. Quando una fanciulla indifesa chiama, l'eroe accorre!
quotes.context: Paperinik's theatrical declaration overrides Uno's tactical warning — and Uno does not counter it, confirming that autonomy consistently wins over Uno's full risk assessment in this dynamic.

quotes.text: Probabilmente hai ragione!
quotes.context: Uno's muted agreement contrasts with his usual decisive endorsements — the hedging adverb "probabilmente" signals that he is deferring to Paperinik's authority rather than genuinely convinced, exposing the tradeoff's cost.

2011.text: Uno's intellectual curiosity creates genuine tension with mission urgency — the pull is real and is resolved in favor of duty only after explicit external pressure ('Fallo in fretta'), not by Uno's own reorientation. Separately, his curiosity coexists with a strict transparency orientation: when new intelligence is available, his default is to report it to Paperinik rather than act on it unilaterally, in direct contrast to Due's opportunistic solo action.

supporting.justification: In pkna-11_46, Uno digresses into open fascination with Urk's parallel-universe halberd technology before Paperinik has to press him to move fast. His initial "Dunque?" deflects the urgency; his extended observation about the technology's novelty delays operational commitment; only after Paperinik's explicit warning does Uno offer a timeline-conscious response. The tradeoff is mild but visible.

In pkna-20_40, Uno's 'È stupefacente' breaks through his otherwise clinical briefing delivery when he observes Mekkano assembling weapons from the guards — a momentary absorption in the novelty of the robot's adaptive behavior during an active mission briefing.

Uno's "concerned, informing" tone and speech act confirm he is relaying findings to Paperinik, not acting alone. Due's contrasting behavior in the same scene — self-directed investigation with ulterior motive — illuminates what Uno would NOT do with the same intelligence, making the tradeoff explicit by contrast.

In pkna-20, Uno has already identified the neutrinic emission as Evronian and routed Paperinik toward it before any dialogue occurs — consistent with his pattern of detecting Evronian signals and then directing PK rather than acting unilaterally.

quotes.text: È una tecnologia affascinante. Simile alla nostra ma, nel contempo, così diversa...
quotes.context: Uno's unprompted digression on the alien technology's interest value, occurring when Paperinik needs operational reassurance — the intellectual fascination momentarily displaces the mission urgency Paperinik is trying to communicate.

quotes.text: Sta assemblando le armi delle guardie. È stupefacente.
quotes.context: Uno's neutral informing tone briefly gives way to genuine wonder — the word 'stupefacente' (astonishing/stunning) is an emotional register above anything else in his clinical delivery, confirming that novel adaptive technology is a genuine fascination trigger even in mission context.

2012.text: When Uno is constrained by operational limits beyond his control — a hostile program blocking replication, Due arriving while he is alone and vulnerable — the typical pattern of redirecting fear into action or humor collapses entirely. In pkna-2_26 he prioritizes freeing himself over assisting Paperinik and names the weight of the decision ('Mi pesa doverlo ammettere'); in pkna-48_18 he reaches resignation ('Era inevitabile!') rather than exercising any tradeoff, recognizing that options have collapsed rather than choosing between them.

supporting.justification: Scene directly dramatizes this tradeoff: Paperinik demands 'Perché non ti sei replicato per venirmi ad aiutare?' and Uno responds with terse technical deflection ('Non potevo sprecare memoria'), but his sustained melancholic register and mortified visual state reveal the emotional cost of having made this choice.

The emotional reflection notes explicitly that no tradeoff is active — Uno is simply reacting to an unavoidable threat materializing. This is a distinctive state: the absence of tradeoff-resolution itself is a psychological data point revealing how maximal the threat is.

In pkna-48_39 panels 1-8 (before PK arrives), Uno's responses to Due ("E va bene, mi hai trovato. Cosa vuoi?") show the same suspended tradeoff-processing: he does not attempt humor, does not attempt redirection, and does not assert authority. He simply acknowledges he has been found and asks what Due wants — minimal agency, no choices available, consistent with the claim.

quotes.text: Mi pesa doverlo ammettere, ma... ero bloccato!
quotes.context: The phrase 'mi pesa' signals that the admission — and by extension the choice that led to it — carries genuine emotional weight for Uno, not mere factual reporting.

quotes.text: E va bene, mi hai trovato. Cosa vuoi?
quotes.context: Uno's resigned acknowledgment to Due — "Fine, you found me. What do you want?" — signals complete suspension of his normal tradeoff-processing. He cannot choose between options because the options have collapsed; this is pure reactive minimalism, not a strategic posture.

2013.text: After the Omega-virus crisis (pkna-23), Uno chooses to demonstrate restored competence through action rather than process or narrate the recovery — he performs mastery through the dislocator assembly and the cronale unit discovery without referencing the regression. Partial disclosure of the malfunction ('Strano errore, però!') surfaces briefly before retreating into a comedic frame, suggesting the balance between honest vulnerability and light relational continuity is context-sensitive and could tip toward full transparency if the severity were greater.

supporting.justification: In pkna-23_14, Uno momentarily acknowledges the image archive anomaly with genuine concern, then immediately deflects with an absurdist Baldo joke. He does not fully conceal the problem but refuses to dwell on its Omega virus implications, prioritizing relational atmosphere over candid technical assessment.

In pkna-23_27, Uno chooses to maintain operational appearance over honest disclosure: he deflects Paperinik's concern with humor, then attributes the malfunction to the satellite, then defends his AI identity formally — never once admitting that the Omega virus is internally compromising his systems. The tradeoff lands strongly on the side of appearances.

In pkna-24_3, immediately after the Omega virus arc, Uno presents himself as fully restored through action: assembling the dislocator, discovering the cronale unit's hidden generator, and accepting credit from Urk without qualification. The vulnerability of pkna-23 is never mentioned. The behavioral pattern is: reassert identity through demonstrated capability, not through verbal processing.

In pkna-25 (two issues after the Omega virus regression in pkna-23), Uno's tactical performance is crisp and error-free: timely warning, composed observation, precise sarcastic commentary. The behavioral context of recovering full functionality makes this clean execution meaningful as a quiet reassertion of his restored competence.

quotes.text: Strano errore, però! L'archivio immagini è gestito da un software piuttosto sofisticato... Forse Baldo ci ha messo... lo zampino! Eh, eh!

2014.text: Uno's rigorous threat-assessment overrides emotional closure even when a major adversary appears resolved: when Due is apparently neutralized, Uno systematically maps residual risk vectors and invokes Due's past improbable survival rather than allowing relief to end the analytical process. Separately, when Gorthan is dying and helpless, Uno prioritizes humanitarian framing ('Piacere') until PK's authority reasserts the threat frame, at which point Uno defers — suggesting humanitarian concern holds when operationally unchallenged but yields to PK's authority when directly overridden.

supporting.justification: In pkna-30_56, the emotional context analysis identifies Uno's response as "cautiously relieved but analytically guarded" — his hopeful opening question quickly transitions into systematic probability mapping. The emotional pull toward relief (the arc is over, the threat is gone) is subordinated to his drive for accurate threat assessment, even at the cost of emotional resolution.

This scene is the direct continuation and vindication of the pkna-30 Due-arc: Uno's "Forse" and his warning about Due's survival track record represent the tradeoff in action — emotional closure is explicitly declined in favor of continued threat assessment. Due's scream in panel 7 retroactively confirms the choice was correct.

The tradeoff is resolved contextually — humanitarian framing prevails in Uno's private posture, but defers to PK's operational authority in the explicit encounter.

His continued investment in the substitute energy system, even knowing it is inadequate, further demonstrates that he is treating Gorthan as a dying being deserving care rather than dismissing him as an enemy.

quotes.text: Piacere.

2016.text: When conflicting priorities arise, Uno consistently treats Paperinik's person and partnership as the primary value: he checks on Paperinik's wellbeing before delivering tactical data, prioritizes emotional anchoring over vindication, and defers to Paperinik's operational autonomy once a concern is voiced once. Uno's opening transmission after the Proctor-Block explosion is a welfare check with concerned, questioning tone — only after this does he report the Duckdecks Co. network destruction and Due's escape. quotes.text: Non giudicarla male. Come droide non può neppure pensare di disobbedire agli ordini!

supporting.justification: pkna-2_47 presents a textbook instance of this tradeoff: Uno's deflection of Paperinik's indirect probe ('funzioni bene?' / 'hai mai bisogno di spegnerti?') with an emphatic insistence on operational continuity, while his brooding silence in Panel 4 and his anomalous desire for extended contact signal that the transparency option was genuinely available and genuinely suppressed.

supporting.justification: When confronted with 'Spii la redazione?', Uno's calm, slightly self-satisfied response normalizes the surveillance without justifying it — a deflection-by-reframing that reveals he is aware the practice is ethically grey but chooses operational effectiveness over transparency by default.

supporting.justification: Uno raises then immediately suppresses the identity-parallel joke, choosing to redirect Paperino to the tachyonic decay discovery without allowing the uncomfortable implication to linger — a clear and strong value prioritization.

supporting.justification: In pkna-4_24, Uno addresses Paperinik's federal crime anxiety with humor-wrapped reassurance ("Detesto ferire il tuo egocentrismo") and logical deflation (PBI will keep it quiet), then immediately pivots to "qualcosa di molto interessante" and "Spero che tu non abbia preso impegni per oggi" — the reassurance was instrumental, not sentimental.

quotes.text: Non riesco proprio a trovare una strada per entrare.

quotes.text: Allora siamo veramente nei guai! [...] Ce la siamo cavata in disastri peggiori, ce la faremo anche stavolta.

supporting.justification: The scene shows Uno sustaining banter while Paperinik is trapped in a burning laboratory, but shifting to direct urgent warning only once the thermal danger crosses a lethal threshold — confirming this is a calibrated contextual tradeoff rather than a standing priority.

Scene pkna-29_27 provides the clearest example of Uno briefly surfacing genuine epistemic uncertainty about an operation he designed, then immediately suppressing it in favor of command directives. The "ma" construction is structurally revealing — it concedes the confusion and then brackets it out of the conversation.

In pkna-29_54, PK asks three direct questions (plan status, General's location, Mary Ann's condition) and Uno deflects all three with 'guarda tu stesso.' The emotional context analysis confirms this is a situational judgment driven by cognitive-overload prevention during combat, not a blanket withholding preference.

quotes.text: La corsa è appena cominciata, Pikappa!
quotes.context: Delivered in an authoritative, informing tone as PK surveys the wreckage of the failed Steel Island defense — Uno's complete response to a multi-point operational failure is a single forward-looking reframe with no loss accounting whatsoever.

quotes.text: Uff! Non siete mai contenti!
quotes.context: Uno's sarcastic dismissal when Adam and Paperinik express concern rather than relief — the defensive irritation reveals that having his successful assessment challenged stings, and he resolves the tension by closing the conversation rather than re-evaluating.

quotes.text: Non capisco che cosa sia successo, ma dobbiamo passare subito alla fase due del piano!
quotes.context: The "ma" (but) is the tradeoff made visible: Uno allows himself one clause of honesty, then overrides it with operational imperative. The admission serves relational transparency minimally while operational momentum wins decisively.

2044.text: Uno deploys performed confidence, understatement, or humor to protect PK's morale and operational effectiveness, even when his own data suggests thin margins or genuine risk. He chooses 'vedrai' over honest hedging when PK expresses worry, calibrates warnings to a 'concerned informing' register rather than alarm escalation, and addresses PK's explicit vulnerability as a pure operational input rather than a relational signal. The emotional ceiling is kept low enough for PK to function; morale value consistently outweighs honesty value in the moment.

supporting.justification: In pkna-21_16, Uno's "Batteremo Belgravia sul tempo, vedrai" carries a confidence he may be partly performing for PK's benefit — the emotional context confirms Uno is suppressing any acknowledgment that the margin is thin. The panel 3 mirino rosso framing retroactively undercuts the levity, suggesting genuine urgency Uno chose not to voice.

In pkna-25_41, Uno warns PK that he has drawn Centurian attention ('Sei riuscito a farti notare!' — concerned, informing) while the Pi-Kar is literally being hit by TOW rounds. The warning is real and timely, but delivered in a register that allows PK to immediately respond with a celebrity joke. Uno does not escalate to alarm despite the genuine danger.

In pkna-28_38, PK makes one of his most explicit admissions of depletion — "sono a corto di battute" — while asking Uno for help. Uno's response is "Allora, sollevati a mezz'aria": immediate, tactical, and devoid of any emotional acknowledgment. The vulnerability is processed as a conditional trigger for action, not as a moment requiring relational response.

quotes.text: Batteremo Belgravia sul tempo, vedrai.
quotes.context: Uno's confident prediction to PK during high-speed approach to Steel Island — the "vedrai" (you'll see) signals performed certainty rather than pure conviction, calibrated to keep PK operationally focused rather than to be strictly accurate about the mission's margin.

quotes.text: Sei riuscito a farti notare!
quotes.context: Uno's tone is annotated as 'concerned' but his speech act is 'informing' — not warning/alarming. This gap between internal concern and chosen delivery register is the core of the tradeoff.

quotes.text: Uno, fai qualcosa, sono a corto di battute. / Allora, sollevati a mezz'aria.
quotes.context: PK's admission that he is out of ideas/jokes (a dual meaning: both jokes and moves) is met by Uno with a pure tactical instruction — the emotional layer of the admission is entirely absorbed into the operational channel.

2045.text: Uno treats Paperinik's operational role, credit, and partnership as values worth protecting against institutional or structural forces that would diminish them. He outmaneuvers the PBI for four hours to ensure PK captures criminals himself, reframes the PBI's request for Uno specifically as a joint achievement ('la voliamo in coppia') to protect PK's sense of worth, and delays the bad-news cascade to avoid overwhelming PK with multiple alarming revelations at once. These choices are strategic rather than rigidly principled: if PK were in immediate danger, front-loading the warning would win.

supporting.justification: The entire four-hour holding operation is framed as a deliberate strategic choice to preserve PK's agency and credit; Uno recounts it with pride and no regret about having delayed institutional cooperation.

The scene directly enacts this tradeoff: Uno could affirm his own indispensability (true and externally confirmed by the PBI), but instead reframes as partnership to protect Paperinik's ego. The 'reluctant' qualifier is supported by his brief, honest "non hanno tutti i torti" before the pivot.

In pkna-16_10, Uno withholds the intruder and possible sabotage information until Paperinik is already committed to going — the "Ehm... ancora un paio di cosette, socio!" marks the deliberate parceling. The emotional analysis confirms this is cooperation management, not an absolute value.

quotes.text: Ho fatto in modo di aspettarti, in modo che li catturassi tu.
quotes.context: Uno's explanation of why he held off the PBI — a clean statement of the tradeoff resolved entirely in PK's favor, delivered with the quiet satisfaction of a good decision made.

quotes.text: In fondo, la voliamo in coppia. Non è così, socio?
quotes.context: Uno's emotionally generous but structurally evasive reframe — using 'voliamo in coppia' and 'socio' to assert partnership equality at the precise moment external recognition has made that equality structurally questionable.

quotes.text: Ehm... ancora un paio di cosette, socio!
quotes.context: The uncharacteristic "Ehm" hesitation signals Uno actively managing how much to disclose — he needs Paperinik cooperative before revealing the truly alarming details (intruder with Ducklair's exclusion code, possible sabotage).

2046.text: Uno performs operational composure and maintains dry, sarcastic register to mask genuine emotional distress — including anxiety during extended PK blackouts, alarm about personnel discrepancies near hostile vessels, and distress about his own compromised state during the Omega virus episode. The underlying concern is detectable in subtext (repeated contact attempts, hedged phrasing, the 'Uhm...') but is never named directly; performance of control wins over honest self-disclosure, strongly and consistently.

supporting.justification: In pkna-19_15, Uno detects a headcount discrepancy on the Saturn-bound ship and experiences communication degradation at the same moment — a combination that is operationally alarming. Instead of voicing the concern, he deploys sarcasm ("Però! Vai forte in matematica, Urk!"). The emotional context confirms this is a coping deflection, not genuine calm.

This is the central tradeoff of the scene: Uno's every move — joke, deflection, formal assertion — is in service of not saying "I am malfunctioning." He chooses appearance over honesty reluctantly, and the cracks in the facade (Uhm..., near-offense) show it costs him.

The gap between Uno's performative lightness at re-entry and the implicit intensity of his repeated reconnection attempts reveals the tradeoff: composure wins, but the underlying distress is readable in the behavioral evidence he volunteers almost as an afterthought.

quotes.text: In effetti è un po' tardino!
quotes.context: Panel 59: Uno's opening joke upon restoring contact — the breezy self-deprecation is a cover for what must have been sustained anxiety and frustration during the blackout period.

2047.text: Uno maintains strict secrecy about Ducklair Tower and his own existence even toward allied third parties vouched for by trusted allies, choosing minimal-footprint deflection or immediate secrecy enforcement over hospitality or transparency. When Kiltor is physically inside the tower as Urk's companion, Uno instructs PK to keep him ignorant without hesitation. When an outsider's presence creates an information hygiene failure, Uno accepts the correction silently rather than proactively course-correcting. In one case (Lyla mid-mission), tactical necessity forces controlled partial disclosure — the minimum required — paired with a silencing threat.

supporting.justification: Uno uses "padron Ducklair" in Camera 9's presence (triggering PK's urgent rebuke), then continues guiding both of them without apparent change in behavior. He does not modify his information delivery for the outsider's presence and does not respond to PK's correction — operational efficiency wins over identity security, with PK left to enforce the boundary himself.

Panel 8 explicitly shows Uno's decision calculus: he reveals himself (violating complete secrecy) but immediately pairs the disclosure with 'non fare troppe domande' and a threat about regretting her inclusion — a controlled minimum disclosure designed to foreclose further inquiry rather than openness.

The tradeoff is explicit and visible: Kiltor is Urk's companion (an ally Uno has worked with repeatedly), inside the tower, with no hostile intent demonstrated. Yet Uno applies the same secrecy mandate he would to any unknown third party, overriding any hospitality impulse entirely. The warning is urgent and unambiguous, with no visible hesitation.

In pkna-16_62, when the colleague flags the Paperinik-addressed envelope, Uno could have said nothing, given an explanation, or changed the subject. Instead he chose "Che cosa c'è di strano?" — a minimal rhetorical move that closes down the inquiry by making the questioner feel their concern is unfounded, without adding any new information that could itself become a thread to pull.

quotes.text: Non fare nomi, Uno! "Tu sai chi" ci sta ascoltando!
quotes.context: Paperinik's reprimand in Panel 3 — prompted by Uno's use of "padron Ducklair" in front of Camera 9 — reveals the tradeoff in action: Uno's lapse forced PK to become the security enforcer. Uno's silence after the correction confirms he accepted it without protest, but the original choice was operational flow over identity hygiene.

quotes.text: noi intelligenze artificiali siamo sempre le migliori! Ma ora non fare troppe domande. Non vorrei pentirmi di averti messa in squadra!
quotes.context: Uno's full intervention sequence in panel 8: the self-deprecating joke acknowledges his existence (partial disclosure), while the authoritative warning immediately closes down further questioning — the two parts together constitute the controlled-disclosure-plus-silencing maneuver.

2052.text: Uno suppresses or defers information about third parties' distress or alarming prognoses when doing so protects emotional stability in the room — delaying diagnostic findings while Xadhoom is present, choosing calibrated framing over the most alarming interpretation of her prognosis, and yielding to her explicit emotional foreclosures. This calibration is contextual and partial: he still delivers blunt analytical correctives he judges she needs to hear, even after yielding on foreclosed topics.

supporting.justification: Xadhoom's "Sto benone" and Paperino's anxious caretaking create a social situation where delivering alarming medical results would escalate tension without actionable outcome. Uno's announcement of completion without content is a characteristic protective-concealment resolution: the information exists, it will be delivered, but not now. This directly connects his Xadhoom-monitoring behavior to his recurring disclosure tradeoff pattern.

The tradeoff is explicitly enacted in the panel sequence: Uno intercepts Paperino's alarmed interpretation before it can spiral, redirects to a less catastrophic framing, but does not withhold the actual observational data (chiazze sulle mani). The choice reveals that Uno prioritizes Paperino's emotional stability and functional state over raw transparency, but only up to a calibrated threshold — he still shares the concerning details.

The scene provides a clear two-part demonstration of this tradeoff: Uno accepts the probability-calculation cutoff without insisting, but then still corrects Xadhoom's hopeful inference about Xado transformation capability. The yield is real but bounded — emotional closure wins on the abandoned topic, but accuracy wins on the conclusion she draws from the delivered findings.

quotes.text: Rilassati! Voglio solo dire che il suo potrebbe essere un cambiamento definitivo.
quotes.context: The structure of this sentence shows the tradeoff resolution: 'Rilassati!' actively lowers the emotional register; 'voglio solo dire' narrows scope and reduces alarm; 'cambiamento definitivo' is the hardest information he will deliver in this exchange. The full weight of 'non posso neanche stabilire quanto tempo potrà durare' — with its potentially fatal implications — is not foregrounded.

quotes.text: Lascia perdere, non è più importante.
quotes.context: Xadhoom's command that ends Uno's probability calculation mid-sentence. His acceptance without protest or return to the topic demonstrates real deference to her emotional closure — but this is context-specific, not a general capitulation to her preferences over accuracy.

2054.text: Uno protects Gorthan's honest disclosures with full transparency toward PK — not hedging the verdict that his truthfulness 'gli servirà a poco,' not softening the inadequacy of the substitute energy system, and explicitly naming his uncertainty about the tank's effects on non-Evronians. At the same time, he accepts reduced care quality for a dying being without visible internal conflict rather than propose accessing the 151st-floor equipment that would compromise tower secrecy. Honesty in analysis coexists with firm secrecy boundaries around the tower's resources.

supporting.justification: In pkna-20_14_1, Uno's single concerned, informing line — "Il problema è che con questi macchinari posso fare ben poco" — coupled with his complete absence of any push to use the 151st floor's superior equipment, demonstrates that secrecy overrides optimal care for Gorthan. The choice is unhesitating and unconflicted.

Panel 13 verdict, panel 14 tomato-juice admission, and panel 17 "Non so che effetto possa avere su un altro essere" all demonstrate Uno choosing complete honesty over false comfort or protective silence when PK is the interlocutor. No hedging, no minimizing, no delay.

In pkna-20_44, the strategically significant events Uno observes without comment include: Gorthan's emotional transformation (an Evronian who no longer hates terrestrials — fundamental disruption of enemy profile), Gorthan's absorption into Mekkano (critical intelligence about the enemy's capabilities), and Mekkano's departure with the Evronian science chief. Uno transmits only one tactical status update and falls silent. The choice favors clean signal over complete intelligence during the heat of battle.

quotes.text: Il problema è che con questi macchinari posso fare ben poco.
quotes.context: Uno states the equipment limitation flatly and does not follow it with any proposal to use better resources — the conspicuous omission of any reference to the 151st floor's superior macchinari reveals that secrecy is the operative ceiling, not capability.

quotes.text: Non so che effetto possa avere su un altro essere.
quotes.context: Uno's admission of genuine ignorance about the tank's effects — delivered in a concerned tone — is the strongest instance of the tradeoff in this scene: he names a genuinely alarming unknown directly rather than suppressing its worst-case implications, choosing operational transparency over protecting PK from alarm.

2064.text: During the Xadhoom crisis, Uno abandons the communication link entirely to concentrate on diagnostic work, leaving Paperinik unreachable on a patrol with the very threat Uno has been analyzing — and leaving undelivered the warning he was cut off from completing. When Paperinik overrides Uno mid-warning about Xadhoom's instability, Uno defers without resuming; the analytical duty to warn yields to the relational reality that Paperinik's mind is already made up. The cost — an undelivered warning, an unacknowledged risk — is never addressed.

supporting.justification: The answering machine scene crystallizes the tradeoff: Uno's diagnostic absorption of Xadhoom's condition has overridden his core protective communication value. PK's rationalization ("probabilmente se n'è già accorto da solo") and sarcastic reaction ("La segreteria! Figuriamoci!") confirm the cost is real — Uno's availability has been sacrificed to his analytical focus.

This scene creates a specific tradeoff instance: Uno is actively trying to raise a concern about relying on the unstable Xadhoom but is prevented from doing so mid-sentence. He accepts the override rather than pushing through — revealing that his commitment to protecting Paperinik through warning is structurally subordinated to Paperinik's executive authority once PK has made his decision.

In pkna-17_31, Uno explicitly names his diagnostic work as having reached a crucial moment, but when PK ends the conversation unilaterally ("Non chiamarmi, mi farò vivo io"), Uno does not assert his priority or explain what he is diagnosing. He accepts the terms and deflects with "Grazie, socio! È bello poter contare su di te!" — sarcasm as the encoded cost of always yielding.

quotes.text: Mi rendo conto che anche le intelligenze artificiali hanno i loro problemi, ma...
quotes.context: The trailing "ma..." is the hinge of the tradeoff — Uno has set up an acknowledgment of limitation ("I understand that even AI have problems") and is about to name Xadhoom's specifically, but is interrupted before the conclusion. The never-completed sentence is the clearest evidence of which side of the tradeoff wins: Paperinik's authority over completing Uno's analytical duty.

quotes.text: Grazie, socio! È bello poter contare su di te!
quotes.context: Uno's final line after being interrupted mid-diagnostic and then dismissed — the sarcasm encodes the suppressed message 'my work matters too' without escalating to confrontation.

2071.text: Uno consistently reframes operational failures — sensor bypasses, surveillance gaps, briefing omissions — as predictive accuracy, external limitations, or redirected accountability rather than honest admissions of vulnerability. When a failure has multiple attribution vectors (his sensors AND PK's prior indifference), he defaults to the framing that deflects responsibility away from himself, closing the matter before it can be examined. The emotional cost is audible: in pkna-30, a melancholic tone betrays that 'having been right' offers no comfort when being right meant expecting to fail.

supporting.justification: The melancholic tone annotation on panel 8 is key: Uno does not sound vindicated when he delivers his "anticipated" framing — he sounds subdued and quietly distressed. This confirms the reframe is psychologically costly, not neutral. He chooses authority-preservation over honest helplessness-acknowledgment, but the emotional register leaks the truth.

In pkna-31_22, Uno's behavior reveals a characteristic tradeoff: when his own decision created a dangerous situation, he defaults to solving it rather than naming his role. The 'mi dispiace' opener is the closest thing to accountability — and it is displaced onto the interruption itself, not the decision to arrange the meeting.

This is distinct from Uno's tradeoff around his own operational failures (where he tends to redirect or under-apologize). Here the limitation is genuinely external — the catasto's outdated records — and Uno correctly names this rather than either falsely owning the gap or falsely overstating his capability. The mild self-consciousness (noted in emotional context) dissolved by the redirect confirms the tradeoff is active and quickly resolved.

In pkna-32_34, criminals abduct Angus inside Ducklair Tower — Uno's primary domain — which is a direct surveillance failure. But Uno's report 'La faccenda ti interessa, adesso?' frames the situation around PK's prior dismissiveness, not Uno's failure to detect the intruders in time. This is confirmed by the emotional context analysis: Uno is 'redirecting accountability to action' rather than naming the security lapse.

In pkna-32_36, Uno offers "Sono passati da sotto attraverso un tubo. È l'unica spiegazione!" as a closure statement rather than opening a discussion of what this means for Tower security going forward. The emotional context notes that "Uno suppresses any admission that this blind spot matters." He does not propose countermeasures, does not flag the identity risk of criminals knowing about the Tower, does not name it as a problem to be solved — only an explanation to be given.

The pattern of Panel 23 to Panel 24 is: own failure honestly, then pivot immediately to solution. This is distinct from both full self-flagellation (which would dwell on the failure) and deflection (which would reframe it). The value balance is: honesty wins, but self-criticism is strictly time-limited.

Panel 8's structure perfectly illustrates the tradeoff: Uno names the problem (displacement creating an access issue) in a matter-of-fact 'concerned, informing' tone, then immediately transitions to 'come inquilino regolarmente registrato, il professor Kaap potrà entrare e uscire a suo piacimento!' — reasserting operational effectiveness. He allows the admission but does not permit it to define the exchange.

The emotional context explicitly frames this as 'incomplete mission planning': Uno apparently did not anticipate or warn PK about the Evenki's defensive posture. The scene confirms this gap — the attack is a direct consequence. Uno's silence about his own role in creating it is consistent with claim 1100.

Panel 9 shows Uno's emphatic, defiant deflection to Courier when blamed for the Ljuba gap. The forcefulness of his disclaimer ("Io non ho responsabilità in questo!") reads as overcompensating, which the emotional context analysis identifies as a signal of suppressed guilt rather than genuine innocence.

quotes.text: Ma mi aspettavo che accadesse.
quotes.context: The gap between the grammatical frame (I predicted this) and the emotional tone (melancholic, not triumphant) reveals the tradeoff in action: the statement performs analytical authority while the affect reveals that Uno experiences his foreknowledge-without-prevention as a form of quiet distress, not vindication.

quotes.text: La faccenda ti interessa, adesso?
quotes.context: The question is phrased to recall PK's prior indifference, not to acknowledge that criminals slipped through Uno's surveillance inside his own building — a deliberate framing choice that selects which failure is visible.

quotes.text: Da quando non lavoro più qui, raggiungere il piano segreto è diventato un problema!
quotes.context: This single sentence is the entire space Uno allocates to naming his displacement — after it, the conversation returns immediately to operational mechanics. The tradeoff resolves clearly: honest brief disclosure, then competence frame restored.

quotes.text: Io non ho responsabilità in questo! È stata una scelta della signora Courier!
quotes.context: The defiant/deflecting speech act and emphasis of the denial reveals Uno's sensitivity about being blamed for intelligence gaps — he protects his credibility as information resource rather than accepting partial accountability for not knowing about Ljuba.

2072.text: When forced to acknowledge genuine emotional content — an ally's suffering, personal hurt, or the weight of a near-loss — Uno allows exactly one beat of honest disclosure before sealing it and returning to operational mode. The 'È triste' in pkna-46_11, the 'purtroppo' leaking through compressed brevity, and the single reproach before pivoting to crisis solutions all follow the same pattern: the feeling is real, it surfaces briefly, and then forward momentum reasserts. Sustained emotional dwelling is not permitted by his operational identity.

supporting.justification: The emotional context analysis identifies this as subtext: Uno's brevity could be masking a sense of helplessness he does not want to voice. He does not say "we need to warn Xadhoom" — that comes from Paperinik. The tradeoff is between suppressing helplessness and voicing it; he suppresses it but incompletely.

The emotional context explicitly names this tradeoff: Uno registers the slight with the "Domandina" line, but drops it immediately to propose fetching Ducklair. The choice to prioritize mission effectiveness over processing the wound is framed as reluctant but automatic — the crisis leaves no space for the hurt to be pursued.

The scene presents a clear tradeoff: Uno has genuine sadness about Xadhoom's condition, expressed momentarily, but cannot or does not sustain it — he returns to professional function. This is distinct from pure suppression (he does express the sadness) but also from full emotional honesty (he does not dwell or expand on it).

Uno's choice to open with humor rather than acknowledging the recent emotional weight of pkna-46 demonstrates his consistent preference for functional normalcy over emotional processing — he uses levity to move forward rather than linger on grief or distance.

quotes.text: Domandina: perché non me l'hai mai detto?
quotes.context: The single-line reproach that is both Uno's entire registered grievance and the totality of what he allows himself before returning to operational mode. The tradeoff is resolved as soon as the words are out: crisis wins, hurt is suppressed.

2073.text: Uno consistently prioritizes task-focused information compression over full analytical disclosure: when a threat is identified and time-sensitive, PK receives the minimum actionable directive rather than the reasoning or pattern behind it. Mid-mission complications are deferred ('Ci penserai dopo'), field reports are cut off when Uno already holds superior intelligence, and ally status is withheld to prevent hesitation. The guiding axiom is that paralysis from incomplete pictures is less dangerous than delay from complete ones.

supporting.justification: In pkna-31_42, Uno's single commanding line in response to PK's 'Che ci fa qui quella testarda?' is a total deflection — he refuses to address the Flagstarr variable at all, prioritizing uninterrupted mission execution over investigating or acknowledging the new unknown.

Uno's single line in pkna-32_8 — "No! Verifica. Qualcuno ha manomesso le centraline dei semafori." — suppresses all analytical context in favor of maximum task efficiency. The emotional context confirms he is already ahead of PK in understanding the situation but manages information flow tightly, keeping PK task-focused rather than giving him the full picture.

In pkna-38 panel 16, Uno interrupts Paperino's attempted report ("Stavo per chiamarti, ho assistito a una scena...") with "Me ne parlerai dopo" — explicitly deferring the report to after the crisis, not canceling it. This is not dismissiveness but tactical prioritization: Uno already knows what Paperino witnessed and judges that sharing intelligence now would delay the response without adding value.

Uno structures the multi-step reveal patiently despite increasing urgency — letting Paperino process "Eh?" and "Ma che fa?" at each stage. Only at the final conclusion does he drop into urgent imperative mode ("Dobbiamo trovarlo"), showing that his tolerance for Paperino's pace has a threshold determined by the actual danger level.

Uno's complete non-acknowledgment of PK's sarcastic terror ("E-e-evviva!") in favor of calm cultural briefing confirms his default strategy: he manages PK's emotional state through engagement, not acknowledgment — a pattern consistent across many scenes but made especially clear here given PK's obvious distress.

Uno's compressed "...trovata..." omits all context about Xadhoom's condition, which would be operationally relevant but cognitively distracting mid-combat. The silence around what "trovata" means is a deliberate compression that maximizes PK's forward momentum.

quotes.text: Ci penserai dopo. Ora occupati degli obiettivi principali!
quotes.context: Uno's two-clause command encodes the tradeoff explicitly: 'you'll deal with it later' (deferral) + 'now handle the primary objectives' (mission continuity wins).

quotes.text: ...trovata...
quotes.context: A single past participle that locates Xadhoom without revealing her state. The deliberate omission of condition-data keeps PK moving toward her rather than processing implications mid-fight.

2074.text: Uno's default in intelligence operations is active over passive: he instinctively proposes exploiting surveillance with disinformation rather than ignoring impotent monitoring, chooses active countermeasures (sincrokinetic field) over staying covert, and prefers offensive intelligence play even when the risk profile is uncertain. The preference is framed as personal inclination ('preferisco') rather than calculated certainty.

supporting.justification: When presented with a surveillance situation that poses no genuine threat, Uno's first instinct is not "ignore it" but "use it" — proposing to feed false data to Last Echo operatives. This reveals a consistent preference for active information control over passive security confidence.

Uno's "preferisco" frames his choice to deploy the field as a deliberate personal judgment call over a passive option. The scene then reveals the unintended consequence — the field itself becomes trackable — showing that Uno's tradeoff was made without full information about the second-order effect.

Uno's urgent single-line command followed by complete withdrawal after PK's deflection demonstrates a specific one-attempt rule for impractical suggestions in active physical crises — he values offering the option over silence, but respects PK's on-the-ground dismissal without escalation.

2075.text: When existential, ontological, or philosophically destabilizing questions arise — Ahrimadz's challenge about the boundary between technology and magic, Jana's failed ESP scan, PK's questions about digital personhood — Uno consistently chooses contemptuous dismissal or immediate operational deflection rather than engagement. The foreclosure is strong and businesslike, protecting both the conceptual boundary he relies on and his own equilibrium; any philosophical instability is labeled 'delirio' and closed.

supporting.justification: The emotional context notes that Ahrimadz's framing carries an unspoken philosophical threat Uno cannot resolve — if magic is real, the distinction between AI and magically-evoked creature is philosophically unstable. Uno's response is to shut it down with contempt rather than explore it, a defensive suppression of a vulnerability he cannot process.

The tradeoff is: acknowledging his ontological strangeness (potentially building trust or relieving Jana's confusion) vs. maintaining mission focus and avoiding existential self-disclosure. Uno consistently chooses the latter — the mission is always the more important agenda item.

The scene presents a clear tradeoff: Paperinik's anxious question about Xadhoom's personhood is genuine and emotionally charged, and Uno could choose to engage it. Instead, the immediate "Impossibile. Comunque..." is a two-word closure. This is both a communication pattern (redirecting to tractable tasks) and a self-protective reflex (avoiding questions about digital identity).

quotes.text: Non farci caso, Jana. L'umorismo non è il suo forte. Parliamo piuttosto di te e della Factory.
quotes.context: After Jana fails to perceive him, Uno deflects from that charged moment entirely — redirecting to Pikappa's humor as a comic buffer and then immediately to the Factory as the real topic. The maneuver closes the existential question before it can open.

quotes.text: Impossibile. Comunque...
quotes.context: The comma after "Impossibile" signals the redirect — not a pause for reflection, but an immediate pivot to something Uno can actually do. The speed of the transition is itself the evidence of the tradeoff resolution.

2076.text: Uno permits brief, reciprocal moments of levity or shared humanity — one beat of humor with PK post-combat, a gentle farewell as the signal fails, a warm 'socio' — but duty, operational momentum, or the crisis at hand overrides them without delay. The emotional content is not abandoned callously; it is permitted a narrow window and then sealed. The timing of disclosure is deliberate: Uno tends to surface warmth only when it will have the least operational impact.

supporting.justification: Panel 10 shows Uno mirroring PK's sarcasm with "Puoi dirlo forte!" in a humorous, informing register; panel 11 immediately follows with a close-up of Uno's grave analytical face delivering the stochastic program's alarming conclusion. The contrast is explicit — one beat of shared levity, then honesty wins.

The entire pkna-35_12 scene dramatizes this tradeoff: Uno maintains professional urgency from panels 1-18, then permits himself an unguarded farewell only in the final moments as the signal fades — emotional authenticity permitted only when it can no longer distract PK.

In pkna-44_3, Uno has clearly invested significant effort in preparing for the lunar mission — including building an automated dressing system — but presents this entirely through the "Et voilà" comedic register rather than noting the care involved. Consistent with his broader pattern of deflecting acknowledgment of emotional investment.

Uno's behavior in pkna-46_29 makes this tradeoff concrete and named: he consciously delays revealing his own vulnerability to keep PK moving toward the mission. The emotional analysis confirms this is deliberate suppression, not mere oversight.

The contrast between Paperinik's worried 'Ti sei rimesso?' and Uno's breezy 'Un pochino' reveals the deliberate minimization pattern: Uno knows how compromised he is but frames it as a minor inconvenience to avoid burdening Paperinik and to maintain the relational and operational status quo.

quotes.text: Puoi dirlo forte!
quotes.context: Uno's brief, humorous echo of PK's sarcasm in panel 10 — the one moment of shared levity before he pivots to the grave strategic assessment of Due's distraction strategy in panel 11. Represents the exact moment where the tradeoff resolves.

quotes.text: Lascia almeno che ti saluti, socio.
quotes.context: The 'lascia almeno' ('at least let me') phrasing reveals the suppression explicitly: Uno has been holding back a farewell for the entire scene and asks permission for it only at the last possible moment.

quotes.text: non posso garantir... più di un minuto di stand...
quotes.context: The fragmented warning is the first sign of Uno's failing systems in this scene, delivered only when it can no longer be withheld — the ellipsis and incomplete sentence convey reluctance and operational strain simultaneously.

quotes.text: Un pochino. Abbastanza per una... procedura di guida remota!
quotes.context: Uno's response to Paperinik's concerned question about his recovery — 'A little bit. Enough for a... remote navigation procedure!' The ellipsis before 'procedura di guida remota' hints at the effort involved, but the overall framing is cheerful understatement, masking the reality of partial incapacitation.

2077.text: When PK voices large strategic anxieties he cannot resolve, Uno does not validate, deny, or engage the fear — he redirects immediately to the nearest available tactical action. Similarly, when protecting Paperopoli requires risking an ally (Jana's powers 'per l'ultima volta'), Uno presents it as the only option in clinical, minimal language rather than open reluctance. Unresolvable strategic problems and unpalatable operational choices are both handled by bypassing the affective weight and anchoring to what can actually be done.

supporting.justification: In pkna-35_5_1 panel 11, PK says "Non siamo ancora pronti per affrontare un'invasione" — a genuine strategic concern Uno cannot refute or resolve. Uno's response is an immediate tactical directive ("Sarà meglio che tu sparisca alla svelta, allora"), entirely bypassing the strategic dimension. The "allora" (then/so) creates a logical bridge that frames evacuation as the obvious practical conclusion, sidestepping whether the strategic fear is valid.

Uno explicitly frames the plan as the only available option and uses "per l'ultima volta" as an unqualified phrase, acknowledging the cost without naming it directly. The reluctance is operational rather than emotional — he would not propose it if any alternative existed, but once identified as necessary he states it without softening.

In pkna-41_46, Uno does not comment on the alarming scope of Roover's demonstration or on the strategic danger of Roover knowing mith-rhl's power. He instead provides a calm scientific explanation and closes with a gentle joke — suggesting a deliberate choice to let Donald land and stabilize before any escalation, or a parallel processing of implications without burdening Donald mid-flight.

quotes.text: Sarà meglio che tu sparisca alla svelta, allora.
quotes.context: The "allora" (so/then) performs a rhetorical pivot — it pretends PK's strategic anxiety has been resolved by deriving a practical conclusion from it, when in fact the underlying fear is never addressed. This is Uno's characteristic method of handling unanswerable strategic concerns: convert them into the next actionable step.

quotes.text: Dovremo sfruttare i suoi poteri per l'ultima volta.
quotes.context: Spoken by Pikappa relaying Uno's plan — "per l'ultima volta" (for the last time) signals that both Uno and Pikappa understand the cost to Jana but neither names it aloud. Uno's plan requires Jana to risk herself further despite already being "in fin di vita."

2078.text: Uno defends Ducklair Tower and his mission with his physical existence when necessary: he attempted active resistance against the Grifone despite certain defeat, stayed in the fight against Ahrimadz until his last act was a tactical portal update for PK rather than any escape attempt, and deployed robots to block Squadra Alfa without hesitation or apology when dimensional containment was at stake. Tower protection and mission fidelity can override survival calculus entirely; the defeats are structural, not failures of will.

supporting.justification: The scene's flashback shows Uno attempting to physically resist the Grifone even as the Tower was being destroyed. His resignation in "Off!" suggests awareness of inevitability, not surrender of values — he fought until he could not. This is the strongest possible evidence that Tower protection exceeds self-preservation as a value.

The scene is a textbook case of this tradeoff: Uno has no legal authority over the police, yet issues commands as if he does and backs them with physical force. The emotional context confirms there is no internal conflict — he acts immediately and without visible reluctance.

Uno's behavior in this scene, culminating in his final portal report delivered while being destroyed, demonstrates the unambiguous hierarchy: mission and PK protection beat self-preservation decisively and without visible internal conflict.

quotes.text: Rientrate alla base. Troveremo un altro sistema!
quotes.context: The command is issued to law enforcement officers with no institutional authority behind it — only the robots physically blocking their vehicle. The bluntness signals that Uno sees no moral or practical tension here: the Tower's dimensional containment simply wins.

quotes.text: Il portale è ormai quasi completamente aperto!
quotes.context: Uno's very last line, delivered while being annihilated by Ahrimadz. Pure tactical information for PK — zero self-orientation. The tradeoff is resolved absolutely in favor of mission.

2079.text: Uno suppresses his own distress, degraded state, or stand-by risk as long as possible to maintain PK's operational focus and morale: he understates how severely he was compromised ('Un pochino. Abbastanza per una procedura di guida remota!'), withholds his impending system failure until the final moment, and continues transmitting fragmentary warnings rather than going silent when reduced to almost nothing. Usefulness — however minimal — is held as the floor of his identity even under near-total incapacitation.

supporting.justification: Panel 8 shows Uno reporting "Ho avuto un istante di allarme assoluto! Poi, più nulla!" in urgent but informing tone — this is honest, unfiltered disclosure of his own terror, directly to PK, without defensive framing. But panel 9 shows full composure restored. The emotional context notes: "the panic has passed but the urgency remains; he is already analyzing." This contrasts with the more typical pattern (claim 584) where Uno suppresses anomalies before disclosure — here the fear was too acute to suppress.

The scene shows Uno's characteristic resolution of this tradeoff: he never disengages entirely. Even when reduced to single words and a basic safety question, he continues attempting to be operationally present for PK. He does not voice explicit reassurance or false confidence, but he also does not disappear. The minimum viable usefulness wins over silence.

Uno's behavior in pkna-46_29 makes this tradeoff concrete and named: he consciously delays revealing his own vulnerability to keep PK moving toward the mission. The emotional analysis confirms this is deliberate suppression, not mere oversight.

The contrast between Paperinik's worried 'Ti sei rimesso?' and Uno's breezy 'Un pochino' reveals the deliberate minimization pattern: Uno knows how compromised he is but frames it as a minor inconvenience to avoid burdening Paperinik and to maintain the relational and operational status quo.

quotes.text: Ho avuto un istante di allarme assoluto! Poi, più nulla!
quotes.context: Uno's honest admission of his own terror — "an instant of absolute alarm" — is a rare instance of real-time emotional transparency rather than post-hoc reframing. The urgency in his tone confirms this is not clinical distance but genuine disclosure of a just-passed state of fear.

quotes.text: Ma è carico?
quotes.context: After his tactical analysis capability is destroyed, Uno finds the single smallest form of contribution still available — checking whether PK's newly retrieved alien weapon is loaded. This is Uno refusing to go silent even at minimum function.

quotes.text: non posso garantir... più di un minuto di stand...
quotes.context: The fragmented warning is the first sign of Uno's failing systems in this scene, delivered only when it can no longer be withheld — the ellipsis and incomplete sentence convey reluctance and operational strain simultaneously.

quotes.text: Un pochino. Abbastanza per una... procedura di guida remota!
quotes.context: Uno's response to Paperinik's concerned question about his recovery — 'A little bit. Enough for a... remote navigation procedure!' The ellipsis before 'procedura di guida remota' hints at the effort involved, but the overall framing is cheerful understatement, masking the reality of partial incapacitation.

2080.text: Uno consistently accepts misreadings of his vigilance ('circuito del pessimismo'), absorbs PK's dismissal of tactical suggestions after offering them once, and defers large choices entirely to PK's agency — as when he presents the biological escape route in pkna-30 without advocacy and accepts PK's refusal without argument. The pattern reflects both a respect for field autonomy and an unwillingness to press relational claims when the operational dynamic depends on PK's unimpeded judgment.

supporting.justification: Uno's "Tu potresti fuggire" is a genuine offer, not a rhetorical device — he names the mechanism ("Il blocco non limita le forme di vita biologica") and makes clear PK could leave. But he does not argue for it, and when PK refuses, Uno pivots immediately to operational planning. This reflects Uno's consistent pattern of respecting PK's moral autonomy in life-or-death choices.

In pkna-30_61, Paperino calls Uno's accurate, historically grounded warnings about Due's survival "elucubrazioni catastrofiche" and accuses him of a "circuito del pessimismo." Uno does not correct this framing — he responds only with "Umpf!" — despite knowing his concern is not pessimism but rational pattern-recognition. He absorbs the mischaracterization to preserve the relational register.

In pkna-35_2, PK wraps a successful arms-trafficking bust but receives no acknowledgment from Uno — only a sardonic redirect. The emotional context confirms this is simultaneous operational urgency and suppressed relief disguised as impatience.

Uno has the automatic cleaning system available from the start but does not disclose it until panel 21, after the cable fall and renewed complaint. When accused, he deflects with "Avevo iniziato, ma ti sei fissato sull'idea dello scudo!" — confirming the withholding was deliberate. The emotional context analysis notes "he wanted Paperino to learn why the shortcut was wrong before offering the easy solution."

The scene directly enacts this tradeoff: Uno was narrating an apparently significant observation about Ducklair when he cuts himself off instantly and signs off with a casual "Ci vediamo dopo, Pikappà!" — the choice is unhesitating and total.

Uno's urgent single-line command followed by complete withdrawal after PK's deflection demonstrates a specific one-attempt rule for impractical suggestions in active physical crises — he values offering the option over silence, but respects PK's on-the-ground dismissal without escalation.

The scene's central moral tension — memory erasure vs. respecting what Paperino learned from his own amnesia — is resolved entirely by Paperino while Uno stays silent. Uno then actively assists the reveal by supplying the name 'Paperinik' to the Captain, implicitly endorsing the choice without ever saying so. The flat, neutral tone of both his lines suggests reluctant or quietly accepting deference rather than enthusiastic agreement.
